docs.title: Extension guide: what you have to write Java for (How-to)
docs.text:
For mod developers who want to give data-driven new capabilities. Readers need a working path first (see intro.md) and a basic grasp of the JSON format (see schema.md). This page covers only the extension points that have to land in Java, and every section is organized as "goal → code → why": adding a top-level type, an embedded type, registering a factory, extending property parsing, wiring into diagnostics, adding a reload content type, and how to write tests. Boundaries: for per-class and per-method signatures see api-registration.md / api-extension.md / api-diagnostics.md / api-reload.md; for content organization expressible in pure JSON (groups, blocks, items, index writing, the property cheat sheet) see guide-content.md; for field-level JSON rules and D1–D6 see schema.md. This page repeats neither the signature tables nor the JSON field rules.

Version baseline: Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.203 / mojmap + Parchment 2024.11.17 / Java 21. Line numbers in the text correspond to the file contents in the current working tree (the uncommitted data-driven reimplementation), baseline commit ec864a1; signatures follow api-registration.md / api-extension.md / api-diagnostics.md / api-reload.md.

docs.title: 0. Decide first: does this need Java?
docs.text:
Data-driven has two extension surfaces: JSON content, and capabilities JSON cannot recognize. Only the latter needs Java. Match your case in the table below:

flowchart TD
    A["What do you want to add?"] -->|"A different block/item/entity under an existing top-level type"| B["Register a factory<br/>FactoryRegistry"]
    A -->|"A new key for properties / item_properties"| C["Register a property compiler<br/>JsonPropertyParser / JsonItemParser"]
    A -->|"A brand-new top-level field in a content file"| D["Add a TypeHandler<br/>TypeHandlerRegistry"]
    A -->|"One more content type at reload time"| E["Implement and register a ReloadHandler"]
    A -->|"None of the above, you just want to write more blocks"| F["No Java needed<br/>see guide-content.md"]
Your goal Extension point Does the result need to go into a Minecraft registry Where in this page "type": "my_door" produces a block FactoryRegistry.register Yes §3 "type": "my_material" produces an item FactoryRegistry.registerItem Yes §3 "type": "my_be" attaches a block entity FactoryRegistry.registerBlockEntity Yes §3 A custom non-MC-registry object (effect, definition, ...) FactoryRegistry.registerGeneric + a custom TypeHandler No §1, §3 mymod:my_key appears in properties JsonPropertyParser.registerCompiler — §4 "my_things": [...] appears at the top level of a content file Implement and register a TypeHandler Depends on the definition §1 A block embeds "my_attach": {...} Embedded TypeHandler — §2 One more "xxx": [...] file is read after reload Implement and register a ReloadHandler — §6 Expose an extension's failures to ops/tests Diagnostics / JsonTreeBuilder.addLoadingError — §5

The factory classes used as examples, DataDrivenTestFactories and FanDataDrivenFactories, both live in their modules' contentTesting source set. Such content loads as a mod at test runtime but does not go into the published jar; a real mod puts its factories in its own src/main/java. See §8.

docs.title: 1.1 Goal
docs.text: Let a new top-level field appear in a content file, for example "my_definitions": [ {...}, {...} ], interpreted by your Java code. The system dispatches arrays to the matching TypeHandler by top-level field name: in the registration phase this happens in JsonTreeBuilder.dispatchContent, which walks TypeHandlerRegistry.all() (JsonTreeBuilder.java:492-513), and the field name is getTypeName().

docs.title: 1.2 Pick a shape first
docs.text:
Two shapes; decide which one you are taking:

  • It produces a Reg (goes into an MC registry): extend RegTypeHandler<T> (handler/RegTypeHandler.java:15). It bakes in the template "split the id → look up the factory → attach namespace/group/creative tab → store into the context" (RegTypeHandler.apply:63-112), so you implement only two abstract methods. blocks / items are written this way.
  • It produces no Reg (a pure data definition, or an object obtained through FactoryRegistry.registerGeneric): implement TypeHandler<T> directly (TypeHandler.java:8) and handle things yourself in apply. TestGenericFactory in the tests takes this route (TestGenericFactory.java:51-73).

docs.title: 1.3 Skeleton (Reg-shaped, lifted from the RegTypeHandler template)
docs.text:
The class below compiles as-is (EffectDef is only a placeholder definition). It is shaped after BlockTypeHandler (handler/BlockTypeHandler.java:16-64), with just the factory lookup step swapped for a Generic factory. To save space, code blocks from here on omit imports, and every symbol involved is given a source:

package com.example.mymod.data;

import com.google.gson.JsonObject;
import lib.kasuga.registration.Reg;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.handler.RegTypeHandler;
import lib.kasuga.registration.factory.FactoryRegistry;

public final class EffectTypeHandler extends RegTypeHandler<EffectTypeHandler.EffectDef> {

    /** The product of parse: an immutable definition object. Fields come from JSON, no side effects. */
    public record EffectDef(String id, String type, JsonObject params) {}

    @Override
    public String getTypeName() { return "effects"; }   // the top-level field name this handler claims

    @Override
    public int getPhase() { return PHASE_CONTENT; }     // see 1.5

    @Override
    public EffectDef parse(JsonObject json) {
        return new EffectDef(
                json.get("id").getAsString(),
                json.get("type").getAsString(),
                json.has("params") ? json.getAsJsonObject("params") : null);
    }

    @Override
    protected String resolveRawId(EffectDef definition) { return definition.id(); }

    /** Diagnostics show the JSON `type` value (such as my_effect), not the top-level field name effects. */
    @Override
    protected String resolveType(EffectDef definition) { return definition.type(); }

    @Override
    protected Reg<?, ?> createRegistration(EffectDef definition, String path) {
        FactoryRegistry.GenericFactory factory = FactoryRegistry.getGeneric(definition.type());
        if (factory == null) return null;    // returning null means "no factory"; the framework warns and skips (see §3.4)
        return factory.create(path, definition.params());
    }
}

path has already been stripped out of the id by the template and carries no namespace (RegTypeHandler.resolvePath:43-46); do not prepend a namespace again in the factory.

The pure-data shape can be shorter. It stores the definition in the BuildContext metadata slot for other handlers to look up (BuildContext.putMeta:22):

public final class MyDefinitionHandler implements TypeHandler<MyDefinition> {

    @Override public String getTypeName() { return "my_definitions"; }
    @Override public int getPhase() { return PHASE_GROUPS; }   // referenced by other content, so apply it first

    @Override public MyDefinition parse(JsonObject json) {
        return new MyDefinition(json.get("id").getAsString());
    }

    @Override public void apply(MyDefinition definition, BuildContext context) {
        context.putMeta(getTypeName(), definition.id(), definition);
    }

    /** Only a non-null result takes part in duplicate-id deduplication; the default null opts out. */
    @Override public String resolveIdentity(String modId, MyDefinition definition) {
        return definition.id();
    }
}

docs.title: 1.4 How parse and apply divide the work
docs.text:
• parse(JsonObject) takes one JSON object from the array and returns your definition object. It should be a pure function: no registration, no mutation of global state, no dependence on call order.
  • apply(T, BuildContext) is what performs registration. It is batched by getPhase() and called after every file has been parsed (JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod:61).

Splitting it this way has two concrete reasons:

  1. Duplicate ids are decided before apply. All entries are parsed first, resolveDuplicates uses resolveIdentity to find duplicates, and only the winner enters apply (JsonTreeBuilder:119, 652). The losing entries have also been parsed. So if parse has side effects, the losing entries take effect with their side effects.
  2. The same data may be referenced by several files/manifests; parse is the collection stage, apply the execution stage. Separating them lets deduplication and diagnostics happen inside one "side-effect-free window".

docs.title: 1.5 Choosing a phase
docs.text:
apply does not follow file order; it is batched in ascending getPhase() order (JsonTreeBuilder:119-121). The three constants are defined in TypeHandler.java:11-17:

Constant Value Use Reference implementation PHASE_GROUPS 0 Objects created first and referenced later RegistryGroupHandler (getPhase:23) PHASE_CONTENT 1 Regular content (blocks, items) BlockTypeHandler (:22) / ItemTypeHandler (:19) PHASE_EMBEDDED 2 Embedded types attached to a parent object BlockEntityTypeHandler (:24)

Almost every new type uses PHASE_CONTENT. If it gets looked up by id from later content, the way a group does, use PHASE_GROUPS; if it has to land after a parent object, the way a block entity does, use PHASE_EMBEDDED, together with §2.

Within the same phase the order is registration order (a stable Comparator sort); across phases the value order always holds. So do not guess "who comes first" from file order — guarantee it through getPhase or through lookups in BuildContext.

docs.title: 1.6 Registering the handler
docs.text:
TypeHandlerRegistry is a global static table, written with register and indexed by getTypeName() (TypeHandlerRegistry.java:11-17). The four built-in handlers are lazily registered once by JsonTreeBuilder.ensureHandlersRegistered() (JsonTreeBuilder:49-56); your handler must register itself, and it has to do so before the index is read:

@Context                                        // Micronaut eagerly initializes this
public class MyModDataDriven {

    @PostConstruct
    public void init() {
        TypeHandlerRegistry.register(new EffectTypeHandler());
    }
}

The @Context + @PostConstruct timing is safe: the JsonTreeIntegration that reads the index calls buildForMod only during startup dispatch, through a lazy RegisterContextRegistry callback, which is later than the construction of every @Context bean (see FanDataDrivenFactories.java:39-43 for a note on the same timing). If you register too late, the framework finds no handler for the field and reports that field as an "unknown top-level field" (JsonTreeBuilder:475-490).

docs.title: 1.7 The matching JSON and index
docs.text:
The field name is getTypeName(), the value must be an array, and each element must be an object (JsonTreeBuilder:500-506 enforces both):

{
  "effects": [
    { "id": "mymod:burn", "type": "my_effect", "params": { "duration": 600 } }
  ]
}

For this content file to be read, an index manifest has to list it. The manifest has only two array fields, on_register and on_reload; the old sources field is retired, and writing it is recorded as a loading error since it counts as an unknown field (schema.md §1.3). Registration-phase content goes under on_register:

{ "on_register": [ "mymod_content/effects.json" ] }

For manifest and content-file paths, syntax, and the D1–D6 rules see schema.md §1 and §2; for how to organize several content files see guide-content.md. The manifest location is fixed at data/<mod_id>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/ (JsonTreeBuilder.indexDirectorySegments:745-747).

docs.title: 1.8 Deduplication identity (optional)
docs.text:
resolveIdentity(modId, definition) (TypeHandler.java:64) returns a string meaning "the identity of this definition within the same type field". Two definitions with equal identities count as duplicates, and the later write wins (last-wins). The default returns null, meaning this type never takes part in deduplication.

  • When you extend RegTypeHandler this is already implemented: EffectiveId normalizes the id into its actual namespace so that "foo" and "minecraft:foo" correctly collide (RegTypeHandler:58-60).
  • When you implement TypeHandler directly, override it yourself. If your definition has no registration id (a pure effect list, say), just keep the default null; do not invent a fake id.
  • An exception thrown while resolving the identity degrades to "no identity": the entry is not deduplicated, and loading does not crash (JsonTreeBuilder.identityOf:691).

docs.title: 1.9 Why it is designed this way
docs.text: The reason for the three phases is plain: one content file can declare both groups and blocks, and a block has to attach to a group that already exists; applying in file order would fail when the block is written first. The phase encodes "who must precede whom" as a declaration instead of leaving it to the author's file ordering. Splitting parse and apply lets deduplication and diagnostics finish before registration, so a duplicate id never actually reaches the registry (the DuplicateIdResolver class comment explains why the registrar layer cannot be the backstop).

docs.title: 2. Embedded types: types that hang off a parent entry
2.1 Goal
docs.text: Some content hangs off a parent object instead of standing as its own entry, for example block_entity written inside a block (the block_entity.type in modelling contentTesting's fsm_blocks.json). Such a type takes no top-level field and can only be pulled out of the parent object.

docs.title: 2.2 How the three methods work together
docs.text:
Override getParentTypeName, getEmbeddedKeyName, and extractEmbedded (TypeHandler.java:38-50). The implementation below is taken from BlockEntityTypeHandler (handler/BlockEntityTypeHandler.java:27-53), with block_entity swapped for the key you want to use:

public final class AttachmentTypeHandler implements TypeHandler<AttachmentTypeHandler.AttachmentDef> {

    public record AttachmentDef(String type, String parentBlockId) {}

    @Override public String getTypeName() { return "attachments"; }  // for the registry index only
    @Override public int getPhase() { return PHASE_EMBEDDED; }       // apply after the parent object
    @Override public String getParentTypeName() { return "blocks"; } // lives inside blocks entries
    @Override public String getEmbeddedKeyName() { return "attachment"; } // the key name inside the parent entry

    @Override
    public List<JsonObject> extractEmbedded(JsonObject blockJson) {
        if (!blockJson.has("attachment")) return null;      // no embedded data
        JsonObject attachment = blockJson.getAsJsonObject("attachment").deepCopy();
        attachment.addProperty("_parent_block", blockJson.get("id").getAsString());
        return List.of(attachment);
    }

    @Override
    public AttachmentDef parse(JsonObject json) {
        return new AttachmentDef(
                json.get("type").getAsString(),
                json.get("_parent_block").getAsString());
    }

    @Override
    public void apply(AttachmentDef definition, BuildContext baseContext) {
        RegBuildContext context = (RegBuildContext) baseContext;
        Reg<?, Block> blockReg = context.getBlockReg(definition.parentBlockId());
        if (blockReg == null) return;                        // parent block does not exist; skip (a warn is optional)
        // ... build your embedded object from blockReg and attach it
    }
}

The contracts of the three methods:

  • A non-null getParentTypeName() declares "I am an embedded type", and its value is the parent type's getTypeName().
  • getEmbeddedKeyName() is used for diagnostics only. When an author writes an embedded type as a top-level field by mistake, the error message names "should be written in the <this key> of a <parent type> entry" (JsonTreeBuilder.dispatchContent:475-490). Without the override you lose that hint (it returns null).
  • extractEmbedded(JsonObject parentJson) receives one parent entry and returns a list of embedded objects (null for zero). _parent_block is not a field name the framework enforces; it is the convention this repository's BlockEntityTypeHandler uses. You can define your own, as long as your parse recognizes the key.

docs.title: 2.3 Differences from top-level types
docs.text:
• An embedded type takes no part in top-level field dispatch. dispatchContent filters the embedded handlers out first (JsonTreeBuilder:461-467) and checks root.has(getTypeName()) only for top-level handlers (:500-506); embedded data is extracted separately inside the parent loop (:528-535).
  • Consequently an embedded type's getTypeName() is not a legal top-level field. Writing "block_entities": [...] at the top level goes down the unknown-field path, reports an error, and hints at the correct key name.

docs.title: 2.4 Why a stray top-level write does not abort the whole file
docs.text:
An unknown top-level field records one diagnostic and processing continues with the other fields (the loop in JsonTreeBuilder:475-490 does not throw), and the file's legal fields parse as usual. This is deliberate "partial apply" semantics: one misplaced embedded type should not take the same file's healthy blocks/items down with it. The test JsonTreeBuilderEmbeddedTypeDispatchTest.topLevelEmbeddedTypeIsReportedAndTheRestOfTheFileStillDispatches (:46-67) pins down both "one error is reported" and "the sibling fields still dispatch".

A parent type can currently carry only one embedded child type: TypeHandlerRegistry.findByParent scans linearly and returns the first match (TypeHandlerRegistry.java:23-30).

docs.title: 3.1 Goal and choosing a table
docs.text:
type is the seam between JSON and Java. One factory builds one kind of object. FactoryRegistry provides four independent tables, each with its own register*/get*/contains* (modules/core/.../factory/FactoryRegistry.java):

Your JSON Registration method Factory signature Consumer type in blocks register(type, BlockFactory) (:44) create(String id, @Nullable JsonObject params) (:18-20) BlockTypeHandler.createRegistration:60-64 type in items registerItem(type, ItemFactory) (:58) create(String id, @Nullable JsonObject params) (:23-25) ItemTypeHandler.createRegistration:56-60 block_entity.type registerBlockEntity(type, BlockEntityFactory) (:74) create(String id, Supplier<Block[]> validBlocks, @Nullable JsonObject params) (:28-30) BlockEntityTypeHandler.apply:92 A custom top-level type registerGeneric(type, GenericFactory) (:93) create(String id, JsonObject params) (:33-35) your custom handler

A Generic factory's params carries no @Nullable annotation, so the implementation either accepts null or does its own null check.

docs.title: 3.2 Bean wiring: @Context + @PostConstruct
docs.text:
Factories have to be registered before the index is read, so they go in a @Context bean's @PostConstruct. The code below is taken from FanDataDrivenFactories (modules/modelling/src/contentTesting/java/test/kasuga/modelling/FanDataDrivenFactories.java:45-115) and DataDrivenTestFactories (modules/data-driven/src/contentTesting/java/test/kasuga/data_driven/DataDrivenTestFactories.java:21-55):

@Context
public class MyModFactories {

    @PostConstruct
    public void init() {
        // block factory: id holds the path only; the handler has already stripped the namespace
        FactoryRegistry.register("my_door", (id, params) -> blockWithItem(id, MyDoorBlock::new));

        // the same factory reads params to make variants
        FactoryRegistry.register("my_window", (id, params) -> {
            int height = params != null && params.has("height")
                    ? params.get("height").getAsInt() : 1;
            return blockWithItem(id, () -> new MyWindowBlock(height));
        });

        // item factory
        FactoryRegistry.registerItem("my_material", (id, params) -> ItemReg.of(id, Item::new));

        // block entity factory: validBlocks is a lazy Supplier; store it, do not call get() now
        FactoryRegistry.registerBlockEntity("my_be", MyModFactories::createBeReg);
    }

    @SuppressWarnings("unchecked")
    private static <T extends Block> Reg<?, Block> blockWithItem(
            String id, Function<BlockBehaviour.Properties, T> blockSupplier) {
        return (Reg<?, Block>) (Reg<?, ?>) BlockReg.of(id, blockSupplier).withDefaultBlockItem(id);
    }

    private static Reg<?, ?> createBeReg(String id, Supplier<Block[]> validBlocks, JsonObject params) {
        BlockEntityReg<MyBlockEntity> reg = new BlockEntityReg<>(id,
                r -> (pos, state) -> new MyBlockEntity(r.getEntry(), pos, state));
        reg.withProperty(Collection.class,
                col -> { col.addAll(Arrays.asList(validBlocks.get())); return col; });
        return reg;
    }
}

Symbol sources: for the use of BlockReg.of(...).withDefaultBlockItem(id) see DataDrivenTestFactories.java:27 and FanDataDrivenFactories.java:92 (withDefaultBlockItem is defined in BlockReg.java:108); ItemReg.of is in ItemReg.java:79; new BlockEntityReg<>(id, supplier) in BlockEntityReg.java:59; Reg.withProperty(Class, Function) in Reg.java:97.

docs.title: 3.3 The params contract
docs.text:
params is the raw JSON object of the definition's params field, it may be null, and its meaning is defined entirely by the factory. The built-in fsm_be reads state_machine / model / model_name from params and degrades an absent value to a warn rather than an exception (FsmBlockEntityFactories.java:63-76). A custom factory should do the same: warn on a missing parameter and let the object exist in a degraded shape instead of failing the whole entry.

BlockEntityFactory.validBlocks is a Supplier<Block[]> evaluated lazily; the factory should store it in a supplier rather than calling get() at create time (api-extension.md §10).

docs.title: 3.4 When a factory is missing: warn and skip, not an error
docs.text:
If JSON's type has no matching factory, RegTypeHandler.createRegistration returns null by convention and the template immediately logs a WARN and returns (RegTypeHandler.apply:70-74):

Reg<?, ?> reg = createRegistration(definition, path);
if (reg == null) {
    LOGGER.warn("No factory for type '{}' (id '{}')", resolveType(definition), rawId);
    return;
}

This WARN goes into the log only, not into the diagnostics bucket (api-diagnostics.md §12 lists it in the "log only" column). The reason is that "the factory may not be registered yet" is a common state during development, and treating it as a loading error would make the bucket too noisy. The cost is that a missing factory means the block/item is silently skipped, and at runtime you see only one WARN. When you are chasing "my block does not show up", look at this log line first.

An embedded block entity has a further precondition: when the parent block is missing or the BE type is unknown, BlockEntityTypeHandler.apply:75-86 also warns and skips.

docs.title: 3.5 Why it is designed this way
docs.text: Factories are separate from handlers because the same type (say my_door) is decided jointly by "who creates it" and "which registry it goes into", while different mods may reuse the same set of handlers. Factories register into a global static table backed by a ConcurrentHashMap (FactoryRegistry.java:37-40), and registering the same type twice overwrites silently (FactoryRegistryTest.registerDuplicateOverwrites). That also means type names are globally shared; a mod prefix is worth adding to lower the odds of a collision.

docs.title: 4.1 Goal
docs.text: Let custom keys appear in properties (blocks/groups) or item_properties (items/blocks/groups). This layer only changes "how a key is compiled into a mutation function for Properties"; it touches no other field of the content file.

docs.title: 4.2 Block properties: JsonPropertyParser.registerCompiler
docs.text:
JsonPropertyParser is a singleton (INSTANCE:23 or getInstance():217). Two ways to register:

// Option 1: exact key match (recommended)
JsonPropertyParser.getInstance().registerCompiler("mymod:hardness_per_axis", (key, value) -> {
    float hardness = value.getAsFloat();
    return props -> { props.strength(hardness); return props; };
});

// Option 2: custom matching logic
JsonPropertyParser.getInstance().registerCompiler(new PropertyCompiler(
        (key, value) -> key.startsWith("mymod:"),          // BiPredicate: is this key mine to handle?
        (key, value) -> props -> { props.strength(1.0F); return props; } // compile into a mutation function
));

For signatures see JsonPropertyParser.registerCompiler:197/201; for the PropertyCompiler constructor see compiler/PropertyCompiler.java:16. Both append to the end of the compiler list (addCompiler:187-190).

Matching rule: valid(key, value) is tried one by one in list order, and the first hit wins (parseBlockProperty:44-49). Built-in keys come first (buildCompilers:148-174), so a custom compiler cannot override a built-in key — registering "strength" has no effect, for instance, because the built-in strength is hit first. Use a prefixed key name instead; built-in entries cannot be pulled out, because removeCompiler needs a PropertyCompiler instance and the built-in instances are not exposed (see §10).

When no compiler matches, Unknown block property: <key> is logged as a WARN and the key is ignored (:50-52); a value that fails to parse logs a WARN and returns null (:54-57). Neither goes into the diagnostics bucket.

docs.title: 4.3 Item properties: JsonItemParser.registerParser
docs.text:
JsonItemParser is likewise a singleton (INSTANCE:15), and keys are matched verbatim (Map<String, ItemPropertyParser>, registerParser:67):

JsonItemParser.INSTANCE.registerParser("mymod:durability_bonus", (key, value) -> {
    int bonus = value.getAsInt();
    return props -> { props.durability(bonus); return props; };
});

ItemPropertyParser is the functional interface parse(String, JsonElement) → Function<Item.Properties, Item.Properties> (JsonItemParser.java:71-74). Two things to note: keys are case-sensitive (unlike block properties, whose keys pass through RLCompiler and get lowercased, RLCompiler.java:17-23); tab is a reserved key that the parser stage skips outright (JsonItemParser.parseItemProperty:52), since the handler layer translates it into a creative tab binding — your parser never sees it.

docs.title: 4.4 Lifecycle
docs.text:
Both parsers are process-level singletons, and a custom compiler persists once registered: it is not cleared across mods or across /reload (clearCompilers is protected, JsonPropertyParser.java:205). So:

  • Use keys that carry your mod namespace (mymod:xxx) to lower the chance of colliding with other mods. When you use registerCompiler(String, ...) for a block property, the key is parsed as a ResourceLocation, and a bare key lands under the minecraft: namespace.
  • Register at the same time as factories: @Context + @PostConstruct, earlier than content parsing.

docs.title: 4.5 Why it is designed this way
docs.text: Once a property is compiled into a Function<Properties, Properties>, the Reg property chain stacks them parents-first and children-last (Reg.applyProperties, Reg.java:103-110), so the block level applies last and therefore wins. This "chain of overrides, whole-key replacement" lets a group supply a default and a block level override it without any field-merging logic (detail in api-extension.md §11.3).

docs.title: 5.1 Two dimensions, and what each one covers
docs.text:
Diagnostics (diagnostics/Diagnostics.java) is the single facade, and error addresses come in two dimensions that never mix:

Dimension Write Read Who uses it By mod id report(String modId, Throwable) (:64) errors(modId) (:73) the whole registration domain By domain + source key report(Domain, String key, Throwable) (:96) errors(Domain, key) (:107) the reload domain uses Domain.RELOAD_DATA (key = namespace); the assets / config domains are still reserved

report(modId, ...) delegates verbatim to JsonTreeBuilder.addLoadingError(modId, error) (JsonTreeBuilder:844), and errors(modId) on the read side delegates to getLoadingErrors(modId) (:806). So the existing contract "assert getLoadingErrors(modId) is empty" is unaffected by the facade (DiagnosticsTest.modDimensionIsTheExistingBucket).

docs.title: 5.2 Which channel a handler error should take
docs.text:
When you extend a handler, the three failure channels have different consequences:

Where you throw Handler Consequence Throw inside apply (and you do not catch it yourself) JsonTreeBuilder.applyUnchecked:712 ERROR log + recorded into that mod's bucket; the remaining entries proceed Throw inside parse JsonTreeBuilder element-level tolerance in the registration phase one bucket entry entry <i> in '<key>' failed to parse: <msg>; entry skipped; only that element is lost, sibling entries in the same file proceed as usual Do not throw, just LOGGER.warn you log only, no trace in the bucket

The convention that follows: be tolerant in parse (supply defaults for missing fields, do not throw), because the parse stage has no context and its diagnostics come out less complete than apply's. When you really do want to drop an entry, throwing from parse and throwing from apply now both affect only that entry, with the framework keeping accounts and continuing with the entries after it; a throw from apply carries the type name, mod id, and original cause in its diagnostic, which is more informative and generally the better choice. The test JsonTreeBuilderLoadingErrorTest.failingHandlerApplyIsRecordedInTheBucket (:168-181) pins down that a throw from apply records the type name, mod id, and original cause into the bucket.

When you need a soft hint that does not go into the bucket (a missing factory, a missing optional parameter, ...), just log a WARN as in RegTypeHandler.apply:70-74; §3.4 has explained that this is a deliberate degradation.

If you really want a non-fatal record in the bucket, call Diagnostics.report(context.getModId(), new IllegalStateException("...")) directly: apply receives the BuildContext, whose getModId() is available (BuildContext.java:17). Note that parse cannot get the modId or the context, so a soft diagnostic from the parse stage can only be added during apply. §10 lists this as a design shortcoming.

docs.title: 5.3 An easy trap: RegTypeHandler swallows exceptions internally
docs.text: If a custom handler extends RegTypeHandler, the template method apply comes with its own try/catch that logs a WARN and returns after catching (RegTypeHandler.apply:107-111). This means an exception you throw in createRegistration or configureTypeSpecific never reaches applyUnchecked, and therefore never reaches the bucket. If you want the failure recorded in the diagnostics bucket, either implement TypeHandler directly (letting the exception escape apply), or call Diagnostics.report explicitly at a layer that catch does not cover.

docs.title: 5.4 The reload domain uses the domain dimension (Domain.RELOAD_DATA)
docs.text:
Errors on the reload side are reported through ReloadOrchestrator.reportError (:566-573) and each handler's reportError / reportWarning (for example FsmReloadHandler.java:118-130); both call Diagnostics.report(Domain.RELOAD_DATA, namespace, ...), where namespace is the namespace the failing file sits in. In other words reload errors land in the domain / source-key dimension (Domain.RELOAD_DATA, key = namespace), separate from the registration phase's mod dimension. The two dimensions are told apart by different labels in /kasuga_data errors output (mod dimension [<mod>] <error>, reload dimension [RELOAD_DATA[<namespace>]] <error>); the reload dimension is cleared at the start of every cycle (Diagnostics.clear(Domain.RELOAD_DATA) in runCycle, :208), so consecutive /reloads do not accumulate.

All four constants of Diagnostics.Domain and the errorsBySource table are in place, and the reload domain already writes RELOAD_DATA (Diagnostics.java:40-49, 55). A new extension picks its dimension by attribution: attribute to a mod with report(modId, ...); a failure that "belongs to a source rather than a mod" uses report(Domain, key, ...). The assets / config domains are still reserved.

docs.title: 5.5 The read side
docs.text:
• In game: /kasuga_data errors [mod]. With no argument it prints one summary line per non-empty bucket (Diagnostics.summarize():143); with a mod id it lists that mod's failures entry by entry across both dimensions (the mod dimension and the RELOAD_DATA[<namespace>] source dimension). The command tree is defined in DataDiagnosticsCommands.kasugaDataCommand:45 and registered in onRegisterCommands:57; permission level 2 is required.
  • In tests: assert JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors(modId) is empty, or use Diagnostics.errors(modId) (equivalent).
  • Summary line format (summarize): mod buckets print <mod>: N error(s), source buckets print <DOMAIN>[<key>]: N error(s), in a deterministic order that makes assertions easy (DiagnosticsTest.summarizePrintsOneLinePerNonEmptyBucketDeterministically).

docs.title: 6.1 Goal and prerequisites
docs.text:
Reload-phase content (read from the pack stack on /reload, overridable by data packs) is orchestrated by ReloadOrchestrator (ReloadOrchestrator.java:121). The orchestrator itself knows no type name: it walks ReloadHandlerRegistry and treats every registered ReloadHandler's typeName() as a legal top-level key, routing, deduplicating, and registering file by file. So to add a reload content type you implement and register one ReloadHandler and change no framework class.

The interface mirrors the registration phase's TypeHandler: one TypeHandler handles the parse/apply of one registration type, one ReloadHandler handles the decode/register of one reload type. Their separate registries (TypeHandlerRegistry / ReloadHandlerRegistry) are both owned by data-driven, so data-driven still does not depend on modelling (see §8 item 1).

Prerequisite: the handler implementation has to live in a module that can import data-driven. ReloadHandler / ReloadHandlerRegistry / Decoded / Reloaded all sit in data-driven's lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.reload package; this repository's two FSM handlers live in modelling (the consuming module), and the dependency direction is still modelling → data-driven. The data-driven side offers only reusable pure functions (JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest / resolveIndexManifests / validateSourcePath, DuplicateIdResolver).

docs.title: 6.2 Implementing and registering a ReloadHandler
docs.text:
The shortest example is FsmClipsReloadHandler (index-only, no cross-type validation). Write yours to its shape: typeName() claims the top-level key, decode decodes purely, register writes into its own bucket. The class below demonstrates every callback of the interface (MyThing / MyThingCodec / MyBucket are the author's own placeholder types, not framework API; bucket.clearResource() / registerResource(...) is the bucket this handler owns, modeled on FsmAnimationClips' clearResource / registerResource):

package com.example.mymod.reload;

import com.google.gson.JsonObject;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.reload.Decoded;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.reload.ReloadHandler;

public final class MyThingsReloadHandler implements ReloadHandler<MyThing> {

    private final MyBucket bucket;

    public MyThingsReloadHandler(MyBucket bucket) { this.bucket = bucket; }

    @Override
    public String typeName() { return "my_things"; }        // the top-level key claimed, also the dedup collision space

    @Override
    public String describeFile() { return "my thing file"; } // the noun used in decode diagnostics (default "reload-domain file")

    @Override
    public void clearBucket() {
        bucket.clearResource();   // drops reload-sourced entries only; script/code registrations survive reload
    }

    @Override
    public Decoded<MyThing> decode(JsonObject root) {
        // Pure decode: reads no file (the orchestrator owns I/O); malformed content comes back as errors, not an exception.
        // Delegate to your own pure decoder, wrapping each entry as Decoded.Entry(id, payload).
        return MyThingCodec.decode(root);
    }

    @Override
    public void register(MyThing payload) {
        bucket.registerResource(payload.id(), payload);  // the last-wins winner lands here
    }
}

A @Context bean registers it in @PostConstruct, at the same time as factories/handlers (before any reload):

@Context
public class MyModReloadHandlers {

    @PostConstruct
    public void init() {
        ReloadHandlerRegistry.register(new MyThingsReloadHandler(MyBucket.GLOBAL));
    }
}

ReloadHandlerRegistry.register indexes by typeName() and keeps order with a LinkedHashMap: registering the same name twice replaces in place and keeps the position, so re-running the bean in tests is idempotent. Registration order matters — the orchestrator decides dispatch/register order by registration order, which also decides cross-type last-wins and which handler's afterReload can see entries another handler has already landed. For this reason the FSM side uses a separate bean FsmReloadHandlerRegistrar (:22-31) to register FsmReloadHandler → FsmClipsReloadHandler in that order.

docs.title: 6.3 Lifecycle: when the four callbacks run
docs.text:
Within one reload cycle the orchestrator calls, for every handler in turn:

  1. clearBucket() — once per cycle, before discovery. The implementation must drop only the reload source ("script wins"), so it delegates to the bucket's clearResource() rather than clearing everything. A thrown exception is isolated in place by the orchestrator (runClear, :250-261) and recorded under Domain.RELOAD_DATA, while the other handlers proceed as usual.
  2. decode(JsonObject) — called for every file whose top-level key hits typeName(). It does not read files (the orchestrator does the I/O) and does not throw on malformed content (shape violations come back as Decoded.errors(), and the orchestrator pairs them with a log line + a diagnostics bucket entry). A Decoded.Entry(id, payload) binds the payload to its identity for deduplication — the handler picks the identity (both existing types use their own id).
  3. register(payload) — called only for the last-wins winner, and only after the whole discovery round has finished. A registration failure should throw; the orchestrator isolates it and attributes it to the namespace the entry sits in.
  4. afterReload(List<Reloaded<T>>) — after every handler's register stage has run, called only for the entries actually registered this round. Cross-type validation belongs here: FsmReloadHandler's dangling clip check has to wait until the clip handler's bucket has landed. Reloaded carries a modId, letting the handler attribute a diagnostic to the namespace that produced the entry.

docs.title: 6.4 Directory glob (optional)
docs.text: The directories returned by globDirectories() have their *.json pulled into discovery by the orchestrator (the default is the empty set = index only: a file no manifest lists is never read). FsmReloadHandler returns Set.of("state_machines"), so state_machines/ has a glob; FsmClipsReloadHandler keeps the default, so animation_clips/ has no glob. When you declare several directories, use an ordered set to preserve discovery order. If a file is hit by both a glob and an index, the orchestrator skips the glob copy and reads it once through the index — the handler does not have to deduplicate the two entry points itself.

docs.title: 6.5 Hard rules on file shape
docs.text: The two existing decoders no longer require a file to have exactly one top-level key: an extra key does not reject the whole file. A decoder validates only the shape of its own key (the body is an object, the key exists, the value is an array, the elements are objects), and the remaining top-level keys go to the orchestrator for judgment and routing (shape rules are centralized in the shared ContentStructure). So a file can declare state_machines alone, or declare state_machines and animation_clips together, with each handler contributing its own entries. ReloadOrchestrator.dispatch records an ERROR for a genuinely unknown top-level key (one no handler claims) and gives the reverse D9 hint pointing out "if this is registration content, list it under on_register instead" (:439-446); that error does not block the contributions of the known keys.

docs.title: 6.6 Differences from extending a registration-phase type
docs.text: Dimension Registration phase (§1) Reload phase (this section) Extension mechanism register with TypeHandlerRegistry.register, no framework class changes register with ReloadHandlerRegistry.register, no framework class changes Read source the mod jar (IModFile.findResource) the pack stack (ResourceManager) When it takes effect once, during mod construction on every /reload Data pack override No Yes Discovery all through on_register the on_reload index, or a directory glob declared by the handler through globDirectories() Where entries live BuildContext (one buildForMod) the bucket (process-level, survives reloads, split into RESOURCE/SCRIPT halves)

docs.title: 6.7 Why it is designed this way
docs.text: The reload and registration domains share a contract (manifest syntax, identity and conflict semantics, error outlets, failure isolation) but not an implementation (SDD §3.2–3.3): the registration domain reads the jar, once during mod construction; the reload domain reads the pack stack, at /reload time, which is why data packs can override it and hot reload works. Both domains now follow the same "registry + handler" shape, with the registry provided by data-driven and the handler registered by the consumer, which makes them symmetric without creating a cycle.

docs.title: 7.1 Pure JVM: use parseContentBody
docs.text:
JsonTreeBuilder.parseContentBody(modId, contentLabel, JsonObject) (:557-571) is the in-memory half of the content pipeline: it runs the full dispatch, extraction, and parse, returns the results grouped by type name, and records diagnostics into that mod's bucket — with no mod jar and no NeoForge runtime needed. Use it to test top-level field dispatch, unknown-field diagnostics, and embedded extraction. Examples: JsonTreeBuilderEmbeddedTypeDispatchTest (:46) and JsonTreeBuilderReloadHintTest (:40):

JsonTreeBuilder.clearLoadingErrors(MOD);
Map<String, List<Object>> collected = JsonTreeBuilder.parseContentBody(
        MOD, "test:my.json", JsonParser.parseString(CONTENT).getAsJsonObject());

assertEquals(1, collected.getOrDefault("effects", List.of()).size());
assertEquals(List.of(), JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors(MOD));   // clean load

Note: parseContentBody only parses, it does not apply. So it verifies "claiming the field, parsing, diagnostics" and not the registration side effects.

docs.title: 7.2 Recording fake factories: test the whole parse → apply chain
docs.text:
To verify that your handler passes factory parameters through verbatim from extraction, use a "recording fake factory": register a factory that captures its parameters and returns a minimal Reg, then build a RegBuildContext by hand to drive extractEmbedded → parse → apply. The example is FactoryParamsForwardingTest (now in modelling's test source set: modules/modelling/src/test/java/lib/kasuga/test/registration/data_driven/FactoryParamsForwardingTest.java; registerRecordingFactory:47-56, shippedBlockForwardsStateMachineAndModelIntoFactoryParams:66-103, buildContext:124-129):

private static JsonObject capturedParams;

@BeforeAll
static void registerRecordingFactory() {
    FactoryRegistry.registerBlockEntity("my_be", (id, validBlocks, params) -> {
        capturedParams = params;
        return new FakeBlockEntityReg();     // a minimal Reg whose getEntry returns itself
    });
}

RegBuildContext context = new RegBuildContext("mymod", new JsonRegistryGroup("mymod:json_root"));
context.putReg("blocks", parentBlockId, new FakeBlockReg());
handler.apply(def, context);
assertSame(expectedParams, capturedParams);   // the object apply passes to the factory is not rebuilt

This makes the "factory parameter contract" assertable in a pure JVM, with no real modelling factory on the classpath.

docs.title: 7.3 Registration assertions under the FML gate
docs.text:
Real registration (into BuiltInRegistries) can only be verified in a runtime that has a mod list. Guard it with Assumptions.assumeTrue: a pure JVM skips it, and the FML test runtime really runs it. Example FanDataDrivenRegistrationTest (:45-73):

@Test
void dataDrivenIndexLoadsWithoutErrors() {
    Assumptions.assumeTrue(neoForgeRuntimeLoaded(), "NeoForge runtime / mod list not available");

    JsonTreeBuilder.clearLoadingErrors(MOD_ID);
    JsonRegistryGroup root = JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod(MOD_ID);

    assertNotNull(root);
    assertEquals(List.of(), JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors(MOD_ID));
}

private static boolean neoForgeRuntimeLoaded() {
    try {
        ModList modList = ModList.get();
        return modList != null && !modList.getModFiles().isEmpty();
    } catch (Throwable t) {
        return false;
    }
}

The division of labor between the two gates: modelling's modelUnitTest task filters junit-fml-* off the classpath (modules/modelling/build.gradle:49-56), runs in a pure JVM with no ModList, and skips via assumeTrue; data-driven's test task, through neoForge.unitTest.enable() (modules/data-driven/build.gradle:99-102), runs under the FML wrapper (build.gradle:21-29 notes that this is not a separate unitTest Gradle task), where the assertions really take effect.

docs.title: 7.4 Unit-testing the factory itself
docs.text: FactoryRegistryTest demonstrates three kinds of assertion: contains/get agree after registration (registerAndGet:12-18), an unregistered type returns null (unknownTypeReturnsNull:26-28), and a duplicate registration overwrites (registerDuplicateOverwrites:31-37). factoryCreatesRegInstance:39-46 and factoryWithParams:48-67 assert that a real factory can be fetched and reads params — the latter depends on simple_block / params_block registered in contentTesting.

docs.title: 8. Pitfall checklist
docs.text:
1. data-driven must not depend on modelling. The dependency direction is modelling → data-driven (modules/modelling/build.gradle:330 comments "one-way edge and creates no cycle"). So both registries belong to data-driven (TypeHandlerRegistry and ReloadHandlerRegistry), and handlers are registered from the modelling side. The registration-phase D9 hint's mention of reload key names is also no longer a literal hard-coded string — it enumerates from ReloadHandlerRegistry at runtime (JsonTreeBuilder.java:559-570), so data-driven avoids importing modelling while the hint still updates automatically as reload types are added. If your new type's definition class belongs to modelling, then it can only live in modelling; putting it in data-driven would create a cycle.
  2. contentTesting is "a mod but not published". DataDrivenTestFactories / FanDataDrivenFactories load as a mod at test runtime through @Context, but jar/shadowJar take only sourceSets.main.output, so they never enter the published jar. A real mod has to put its factories and handlers in src/main/java, or downstream gets "missing factory, silently skipped".
  3. Registration must happen before the index is read. Both factories and handlers register early through a @Context bean's @PostConstruct. Late registration shows up as a missing-factory WARN, or a top-level field judged an "unknown field".
  4. parse has no side effects, and losing entries call it too. Duplicate ids are decided before apply, and the losing entries were parsed as well (JsonTreeBuilder:119). Registering an object inside parse makes an eliminated duplicate id really take effect.
  5. TypeHandlerRegistry is a global static table with no namespace isolation and silent overwrite on a name clash (TypeHandlerRegistry.register:11-13); FactoryRegistry is the same (a duplicate type overwrites). A mod prefix on type names and top-level field names is worth adding.
  6. A parent type can currently have only one embedded child type (findByParent returns the first match, TypeHandlerRegistry.java:23-30).
  7. getRegistryGroup / getBlockReg sit on RegBuildContext, not on BuildContext. The apply parameter type is BuildContext, while the registration path actually passes a RegBuildContext (JsonTreeBuilder:82), so a cast is needed; if a test passes a bare BuildContext, the cast fails.
  8. RegTypeHandler swallows exceptions internally (§5.3), so failures do not reach the bucket. For bucket visibility, implement TypeHandler directly or call Diagnostics.report explicitly.
  9. The domain dimension of Diagnostics is already written by the reload domain (Domain.RELOAD_DATA, §5.4). An extension's failures pick their dimension by attribution: the mod dimension for the registration phase, the domain dimension for failures that "belong to a source rather than a mod".
  10. A property compiler cannot override a built-in key (§4.2); use a new key name.
  11. The handler implementation for a reload type has to live in modelling or further downstream (a module that can import data-driven). data-driven itself cannot depend on modelling in reverse, while ReloadHandlerRegistry is a registration point usable from either side (§6.1, §10).

docs.title: 9. Wrap-up checklist
docs.text:
Check these off one by one once the extension is done:

  • The handler's getTypeName() matches the top-level field in the content file, and the value is an array.
  • parse has no side effects; registration happens in apply.
  • The getPhase() choice matches the dependency relations (referenced → smaller phase).
  • Both handler and factory are registered in a @Context bean's @PostConstruct.
  • The content file is listed by the index manifest under on_register (registration phase) or on_reload (reload phase).
  • A pure-JVM test runs parseContentBody; registration side effects have an assertion under the FML gate.
  • getLoadingErrors(modId) is empty (a clean load).
  • If downstream is to use it, the factory/handler is in src/main/java rather than contentTesting.

docs.title: 10. Known shortcomings of the current extension points (observations)
docs.text:
The gaps below were found while reading the code. They are recorded only; this page offers no fixes:

  1. ~~There is no extension registry on the reload side.~~ Resolved. The reload side is now symmetric with the registration phase: there is a ReloadHandlerRegistry to hook into, and extending means implementing a ReloadHandler + calling register in a @Context bean's @PostConstruct, with no framework class changed (see §6). The two FSM types are the two handlers of this registry (FsmReloadHandler / FsmClipsReloadHandler, registered by FsmReloadHandlerRegistrar).
  2. The cost remains: wiring it up means writing a @Context bean that calls register (there is no SPI auto-scan), and the handler implementation has to live in a module that can import data-driven. So it is "no framework class changed", not "zero code for a third-party mod".
  3. TypeHandlerRegistry is a global static table with no namespace isolation, silent overwrite on a same-name put (TypeHandlerRegistry.register:11-13), and no unregister entry point. A custom handler registered in a test stays alive in the same JVM until the process ends (the TestEffect registered by TestGenericFactory, for example).
  4. parse cannot get the BuildContext or the modId, so it cannot record a non-fatal diagnostic during parsing; a soft error from the parse stage can only be added during apply (§5.2).
  5. RegTypeHandler swallows exceptions internally (apply:107-111), so a handler extending it does not get its failures into the diagnostics bucket (§5.3).
  6. RegTypeHandler.resolveItemProperties is declared but has no call site (RegTypeHandler.java:34; api-extension.md §8.4 mentions it too). An implementation resolves properties in its own configureTypeSpecific instead.
  7. A parent type can carry at most one embedded child type: TypeHandlerRegistry.findByParent returns the first match (TypeHandlerRegistry.java:23-30).
  8. A property compiler can only be appended, never override a built-in key: matching is "first hit wins" with the built-ins first (§4.2); removeCompiler needs the exact instance, and the built-in instances are not exposed.
  9. The two kinds of property parser disagree on key semantics: JsonPropertyParser normalizes keys into a ResourceLocation (lowercase, namespace optional), while JsonItemParser matches verbatim and case-sensitively (§4.2, §4.3).
  10. The domain dimension of Diagnostics already has a writer: reload errors land under Domain.RELOAD_DATA with key = namespace (§5.4). An extension's failures pick their dimension by attribution.
  11. The built-in item property parsers cover only a few keys: JsonItemParser builds in stacks_to / rarity / fire_resistant / durability / no_repair (tab is consumed separately by the loader); food properties, item components, and the like are not built in, and an unknown key is only warned about and ignored (JsonItemParser:63). Extend with registerParser when needed (§4.3).
  12. An embedded BE's data_type (the DataFixer type) cannot be configured from JSON: BlockEntityReg has a DataType modifier (RegFacade.transformObject("DataType", …), passed to BlockEntityType.Builder.build(dataType)), but block_entity on the JSON side has only type / params (schema.md §2.5), with no channel for it.

docs.title: Data-driven getting started: from an empty directory to a moving block
docs.text: Type: Tutorial (learning-oriented, follow along once). Applies to: Minecraft 1.21.1 · NeoForge 21.1.203 · Parchment 2024.11.17 · Java 21. The paths and behavior on this page hold only within this set of versions. Code baseline: KasugaLibNext branch model-loader (2026-10-04, baseline commit ec864a1). Line numbers in this page refer to the current working tree (the uncommitted data-driven reimplementation). This page only gets you started. For the complete list of fields see schema.md; for Java class and method signatures see the data-driven API reference; for specific tasks (adding a block, wiring a creative tab, inheritance) see guide-content.md; for writing a custom TypeHandler see guide-extension.md.

docs.title: 1. What data-driven solves
docs.text:
Data-driven lets you declare in JSON which blocks, items, and groups to register, and the framework reads them into Minecraft's registries at startup, instead of you calling register() one by one in Java.

It does not do the Java half for you. JSON says "register a block with id mymod:panel of type simple_block", and simple_block must first be registered in Java as a factory; how the factory builds that block is still decided by code.

The division of labor therefore works out like this: someone with a Java background builds a factory once and registers a creative tab once; after that, team members who do not write Java add content with JSON only.

The scope of this round has to be drawn clearly first: data pack authors have no use for this registration pipeline. The registration phase reads files from the mod jar only, and data packs cannot reach it (the reason is in the next section).

docs.title: 2. Remember one thing first: the two phases
docs.text:
This is the most important concept on the page, and almost every rule that follows is derived from it.

registration phase (registration) reload phase (reload) When it runs during mod startup and construction, once when you run /reload or reload resources Where objects go MC registries (such as BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK) the reload bucket (not into MC registries) Where it reads from the mod jar the pack stack Can it hot reload No; restart the game after a change Yes; /reload takes effect Can a data pack override it No Yes What the content looks like registry_groups / blocks / items (embedded block_entity) state_machines / animation_clips Code entry point JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod ReloadOrchestrator.reload

A one-line mnemonic: anything that goes into an MC registry belongs to the registration phase, and anything that does not belongs to the reload phase.

Which phase a piece of content belongs to is decided by whether the index file lists it under on_register or on_reload, and has nothing to do with which directory it sits in.

docs.title: 3. The three kinds of files
docs.text:
All the input data-driven takes is three kinds of files.

The index file is the only entry point, and it answers only "which files to read"; it contains no objects of its own. Its location is fixed: data/<namespace>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/<name>.json.

Content files hold object definitions. Paths are relative to data/<namespace>/, and the top-level field name (blocks, registry_groups, ...) decides which handler receives them.

Reload-phase state machine and animation clip files are content files too, only listed under on_reload.

How a file is discovered differs between the two reload content types, and this is where you are most likely to get tripped up. The state_machines/ directory has a glob, so files in data/<namespace>/state_machines/*.json are read even when no index lists them; the animation_clips/ directory has no glob, so a clip file that no on_reload lists is never read.

There can be more than one index. Every .json under the same mod's data_driven/ directory counts as an index, read in ascending filename order.

docs.title: 4.1 Prerequisite: type needs a factory first
docs.text:
type in JSON is a factory registration key. Before copying the example below, confirm this key exists in your environment:

  • The only block factory built into the library itself is fsm_block (modelling module);
  • Keys such as simple_block and simple_item used in the examples here are registered by this repository's contentTesting source set, and are test fixtures that are not published with the library.

When type finds no factory, the entry gets a WARN and is skipped (it does not go into the error bucket). For how to write a factory for your own mod see guide-extension.md.

docs.title: 4.2 Place three files
docs.text:
Assume your namespace is mymod:

src/main/resources/data/mymod/kasuga_lib/data_driven/content.json   ← index
src/main/resources/data/mymod/kasuga_lib_content/groups.json        ← content: groups
src/main/resources/data/mymod/kasuga_lib_content/blocks.json        ← content: blocks

kasuga_lib_content/ is only a conventional directory name inside the library and is not mandatory; content files at any relative path under data/mymod/ are legal.

docs.title: 4.3 Write the index
docs.text:
data/mymod/kasuga_lib/data_driven/content.json:

{
  "on_register": [
    "kasuga_lib_content/groups.json",
    "kasuga_lib_content/blocks.json"
  ]
}

Only on_register, because both files below are consumed in the registration phase. Entry paths are relative to data/mymod/ and must include .json (write kasuga_lib_content/blocks.json, not data/mymod/..., and not blocks).

docs.title: 4.4 Write the group
docs.text:
data/mymod/kasuga_lib_content/groups.json:

{
  "registry_groups": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:panels",
      "item_properties": {
        "tab": "mymod:main"
      }
    }
  ]
}

A group is a container for properties shared by a set of blocks. Which creative tab a block item goes into is attached here as well, through item_properties.tab; tab must be a creative tab id you have already registered. For the full table of registry_groups fields see section 2.2 registry_groups entries in schema.md.

docs.title: 4.5 Write the block
docs.text:
data/mymod/kasuga_lib_content/blocks.json:

{
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:panel",
      "type": "simple_block",
      "registry_group": "mymod:panels",
      "properties": {
        "destroy_time": 2.0
      }
    }
  ]
}

registry_group points at the group from 4.4. Without it the block is still registered, it just does not inherit the group's properties and the item does not go into a creative tab. For the full table of blocks fields see section 2.3 blocks entries in schema.md.

The field names and shapes in the examples are copied from this repository's fixture contentTesting/resources/data/kasuga_lib/kasuga_lib_content/, with only the namespace changed; such shapes parse and load without errors, which JsonTreeBuilderIndexPathTest.contentTestingIndexLoadsWithoutErrors covers.

docs.title: 4.6 Path rules
docs.text:
Three rules. Violating any one produces one error and skips that entry (the remaining entries continue):

  1. The index directory must be exactly data/<namespace>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/, four segments. kasuga_lib is a fixed spelling and data_driven uses an underscore; writing kasuga-lib, or dropping the kasuga_lib level, results in silently loading 0 entries. Source: JsonTreeBuilder.indexDirectorySegments, locked down by the test JsonTreeBuilderIndexPathTest.indexDirectorySegmentsMatchCanonicalLayout.
  2. Index entries are resolved relative to data/<namespace>/, must end with .json, must not start with /, and must not contain an empty segment or a ./.. segment. Source: JsonTreeBuilder.validateSourcePath, test JsonTreeBuilderSourcePathTest.
  3. An entry cannot cross namespaces. The implementation guarantees this: at load time the path is always joined under data/<modId>/ (JsonTreeBuilder.parseSource).

docs.title: 5. Hands on (2): make the block move
docs.text:
The registration phase only makes the block exist. Making it move, that is wiring a state machine and an animation clip to it, means entering the reload phase. This section walks through the real fixture in this repository's modelling module, the only end-to-end working example in this document that also has test coverage.

The fixture is at modules/modelling/src/contentTesting/resources/data/kasuga_lib/, with namespace kasuga_lib.

docs.title: 5.1 Index (declaring both domains at once)
docs.text:
data/kasuga_lib/kasuga_lib/data_driven/modelling.json:

{
  "on_register": [
    "kasuga_lib_content/fan_formula_data_driven.json",
    "kasuga_lib_content/fsm_blocks.json"
  ],
  "on_reload": [
    "animation_clips/fan_fsm_data_driven.json"
  ]
}

Note the state machine file is not here; it is discovered through the directory glob from 5.3. This is exactly an instance of the glob difference in section 3. fsm_blocks.json originally belonged to data-driven's contentTesting, and moved to the modelling side because the fsm_block / fsm_be factories live in modelling only.

docs.title: 5.2 Registration phase: a block plus an embedded block entity
docs.text:
kasuga_lib_content/fan_formula_data_driven.json:

{
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "kasuga_lib:test_fan_formula_data_driven",
      "type": "fan_block",
      "block_entity": {
        "type": "fan_be",
        "params": {
          "model": "kasuga_lib:models/be/test_fan_be.bbmodel",
          "state_machine": "kasuga_lib:fan_machine_data_driven"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

The block binds a block entity through the embedded block_entity, and params hands the model path and the state machine id to the BE factory. fan_block / fan_be are factories registered by FanDataDrivenFactories on the Java side. An embedded type can only be written as a key of the parent object; written as a top-level field it produces an error with a hint.

This block has no registry_group, so the item does not automatically go into a creative tab; you can obtain it with /give kasuga_lib:test_fan_formula_data_driven.

docs.title: 5.3 Reload phase: the state machine (discovered by directory glob)
docs.text:
state_machines/fan_machine_data_driven.json:

{
  "state_machines": [
    {
      "id": "kasuga_lib:fan_machine_data_driven",
      "state_vars": [
        { "name": "cycle", "type": "bool", "default": false, "ephemeral": true, "reference": "kasuga_lib:fan/cycle" },
        { "name": "kasuga_lib:fan/current_speed", "reference": "kasuga_lib:fan/current_speed" },
        { "name": "kasuga_lib:fan/angle", "reference": "kasuga_lib:fan/angle" }
      ],
      "layers": [
        {
          "id": "gear",
          "mode": "base",
          "initial_state": "off",
          "states": [
            { "id": "off", "clip": { "id": "kasuga_lib:fan_fsm_data_driven", "loop": true } },
            { "id": "g1", "clip": { "id": "kasuga_lib:fan_fsm_data_driven", "loop": true } },
            { "id": "g2", "clip": { "id": "kasuga_lib:fan_fsm_data_driven", "loop": true } },
            { "id": "g3", "clip": { "id": "kasuga_lib:fan_fsm_data_driven", "loop": true } }
          ],
          "transitions": [
            { "id": "off_to_g1", "from": "off", "to": "g1", "trigger_on": "cycle", "cross_fade_seconds": 0.25 },
            { "id": "g1_to_g2", "from": "g1", "to": "g2", "trigger_on": "cycle", "cross_fade_seconds": 0.25 },
            { "id": "g2_to_g3", "from": "g2", "to": "g3", "trigger_on": "cycle", "cross_fade_seconds": 0.25 },
            { "id": "g3_to_off", "from": "g3", "to": "off", "trigger_on": "cycle", "cross_fade_seconds": 0.25 }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

The top level is the state_machines key, and its value is an array of definitions (extra top-level keys no longer cause the file to be rejected, see fsm.md section 2.4). What goes inside a definition (state_vars, layers, ...) belongs to the state machine specification, see fsm.md and section 4.2 state_machines wrapper in schema.md.

docs.title: 5.4 Reload phase: the animation clip (index only)
docs.text:
animation_clips/fan_fsm_data_driven.json:

{
  "animation_clips": [
    {
      "id": "kasuga_lib:fan_fsm_data_driven",
      "duration_seconds": 12.0,
      "functions": [
        { "bone": "group", "channel": "rotate", "y": "query.angle" },
        { "bone": "fan", "channel": "rotate", "y": "11 * query.angle" },
        { "bone": "cover", "channel": "rotate", "z": "sin(rad(2 * query.angle)) * 30" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

This file must appear in on_reload (5.1 already lists it), because animation_clips/ has no glob. The kasuga_lib:fan_fsm_data_driven referenced by states[].clip in the state machine is the id from here. For the element format see section 4.3 animation_clips wrapper in schema.md.

docs.title: 5.5 Hot reload
docs.text: Change a file from 5.3 or 5.4, run /reload, and the new content takes effect immediately. Changing the block from 5.2 (registration phase) instead requires restarting the game. That is what the table in section 2 looks like in practice.

docs.title: 6.1 Read the log
docs.text:
A successful registration phase prints one INFO line (once per mod), in this format:

Loaded N JSON entries across M types for mod '<mod id>'

The real output of this repository's contentTesting fixture (source: the system-out of modules/data-driven/build/test-results/test/TEST-lib.kasuga.test.registration.data_driven.JsonTreeBuilderIndexPathTest.xml):

Loaded 23 JSON entries across 4 types for mod 'kasuga_lib'

Each top-level type that gets applied has one additional DEBUG-level Applying ... line. A real instance from the downstream KuaYue runtime:

Loaded 174 JSON entries across 2 types for mod 'kuayue'
Applying 8 entries for type 'registry_groups'
Applying 166 entries for type 'blocks'

If N is 0, or the line is missing entirely, the index was not found or it declared no entries.

The reload phase prints one INFO per entry on every /reload. Real output (source: the system-out of modules/modelling/build/test-results/test/TEST-lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.dynamic.fsm.FanDataDrivenReloadTest.xml):

Loaded state machine definition 'kasuga_lib:fan_machine_data_driven' from 'data/kasuga_lib/state_machines/fan_machine_data_driven.json' (reload domain, mod 'kasuga_lib')
Loaded animation clip 'kasuga_lib:fan_fsm_data_driven' from 'data/kasuga_lib/animation_clips/fan_fsm_data_driven.json' (reload domain, mod 'kasuga_lib')

docs.title: 6.2 Query with a command
docs.text:
In game (permission level 2 required):

  • /kasuga_data errors: one line per bucket that has errors. The mod dimension looks like <mod>: N error(s), the reload dimension looks like RELOAD_DATA[<namespace>]: N error(s); when everything is clean the output is Kasuga data: no loading errors recorded.
  • /kasuga_data errors <mod>: the errors for that mod, entry by entry, in both dimensions. The registration phase looks like [<mod>] <error>, the reload phase looks like [RELOAD_DATA[<namespace>]] <error>.

This is faster than reading logs, and it covers the buckets on both the registration and reload sides. Source: DataDiagnosticsCommands, test DataDiagnosticsCommandsTest.

docs.title: 7. The three mistakes beginners make most often
7.1 You wrote sources
docs.text:
sources is the old field, and it is now an illegal field. Writing:

{ "sources": ["kasuga_lib_content/blocks.json"] }

produces two errors at once: contains unsupported field 'sources', plus declares neither 'on_register' nor 'on_reload', so nothing gets loaded at all. The fix is to replace sources with on_register (or with on_reload for reload-domain content).

docs.title: 7.2 The index lists it, but the content file path is wrong
docs.text: Entries are relative to data/<namespace>/, not to the index directory and not to the resource root. Two common mistakes: adding a data/mymod/ prefix, or omitting the .json suffix. The first reports Source file not found for mod '<mod>': data/<mod>/<path>; the second reports an illegal path. Both skip only that entry, and the remaining entries proceed as usual.

docs.title: 7.3 You listed reload-domain content under on_register
docs.text: Listing a state machine file (with state_machines at the top level) under on_register: the registration phase does not recognize this top-level field, reports unsupported top-level field 'state_machines', and appends list this file under 'on_reload' instead to the end of the message. Other registration fields in the same file are still processed normally. The opposite direction (listing blocks under on_reload) has a symmetric hint pointing back to on_register.

docs.title: 8. What to read next
docs.text:
• schema.md: the complete specification of JSON fields, types, requiredness, defaults, and rule sources. Use it as a dictionary while writing content.
  • the data-driven API reference: signatures and behavior contracts for JsonTreeBuilder, Diagnostics, ReloadOrchestrator, ReloadHandler, and similar classes.
  • guide-content.md: step-by-step procedures for specific tasks (adding a block, wiring a creative tab, property inheritance, ...).
  • guide-extension.md: extensions on the Java side. Register your own factories and TypeHandlers to bring a team's private content into data-driven.
  • fsm.md: the format of state machine definitions and animation clip elements.

docs.title: Chinese-English Glossary
docs.text:
The site's documentation, source code and issues use one set of terms in both languages. When you write docs or issues, or read the other language's pages, take your wording from this page.

Identifiers (class names, JSON keys, commands, module names, paths, version strings) keep their original form in both languages, and this page gives no translations for them.

docs.title: Core terminology
docs.text: Grouped by subsystem. The left column is the term used in the English pages, the right column is the Chinese wording that appears in the Chinese pages. Everyday prose outside these tables follows ordinary technical English.

docs.title: Model and animation
docs.text: English 中文 Notes pose Pose / 姿态 The code type name is Pose; not posture or stance static pose 静态姿态 A constantly sampled clip; channel ownership and reset rules are the same as for any other clip pose blending 姿态混合 Layers compose in a fixed order: the base layer sets the reference, additive layers accumulate local motion, override layers replace the masked bone range pose provider 姿态供应器 Where Supplier<WorldCameraView> appears it is a Java interface; models and the camera only follow it clock 时钟 An independent player owns its clock: game ticks advance time, and render frames only sample by partial tick keyframe 关键帧 component track 分量轨道 Each track drives one component of x / y / z / yaw / pitch / roll / zoom easing 缓动 Reuses the model's Easing and applies to the next segment after a keyframe morph morph Not translated; not deformation or blend shape material frame 材质帧 bone mask 骨骼掩码 Affects only the listed bone groups layer 层 / 状态层 Multiple layers run in parallel and their poses are composed into the model each tick layered state machine 分层状态机 The FSM is a Mecanim-style layered state machine transition 转移 guard 守卫 All guards must be true for the transition to be allowed trigger 触发器 Points at a boolean variable name or id; docs.title: Skeleton, physics and ragdoll
docs.text: English 中文 Notes skeleton 骨架 / Skeleton Structures always take skeleton; not framework bone 骨骼 / Bone bind pose 绑定姿态 Code field bindPoseFollowers skinning 蒙皮 Same form for noun and gerund; not skin, since Skin / SkinInstance are the format's skin data in glTF/PMX skin weight 蒙皮权重 rigid body 刚体 GenericRigidBody is the default for non-PMX content joint 关节 constraint 约束 limit 限位 Only limit / limits, never limiter or position limit reverse mapping 反向映射 ikChainsByBone() gives the mapping from a driver bone to every chain that controls it inverse kinematics (IK) 逆向运动学 / IK The abbreviation IK is not translated diamond closure 菱形闭环 Two bases share a pivot at the bind position and two tips stand for the same closure point. Not diamond constraint or diamond loop closure residual 闭环残差 Counts both the tip separation and the base separation; stopping the iteration does not mean convergence, so diagnostics keep residual and satisfied driver bone 驱动骨 effector bone 末端骨 / effector The field name effector stays; use endpoint only when describing the closure point chain / IK chain 链 / IK 链 From base to tip; the last link points at the effector writeback 写回 Not feedback or write into fixed step 固定步长 KinematicDriver.beginStep(world) runs before every fixed step physics writeback 物理写回 Only the hierarchy is rebuilt afterwards; IK cannot be solved again ragdoll 布娃娃 active ragdoll 主动布娃娃 The same frame's animation/IK targets become bounded PD spring forces and torques; Box3D still handles contacts and joints secondary motion 次级运动 Not secondary physics; keys such as include_secondary_bodies are copied verbatim body profile 主体 profile profile stays as is; the profile generates capsules, semantic mass and joints from the actual bone segments floating origin 浮动原点 The model root's world translation is moved out of the float bone matrices and kept as a separate double worldOrigin large coordinates 大坐标 world anchor 世界锚点 The double world anchor is kept apart from the local float physics coordinates; environment collision, rays and drag are converted into one simulation frame first solver 求解器 CalikoIkSolver offers solve() and results() sleeping 休眠 Sleeps a whole group of rigid bodies; turn it off when debugging contacts or continuous airborne simulation impulse 冲量 Changes velocity immediately; not momentum; code entry point applyImpulse force / torque 力 / 力矩 Integrated by the next native Box3D step; not strength drag 拖拽 Creates a kinematic anchor and a spherical joint in native Box3D instead of teleporting the body environment mesh 环境网格 StaticEnvironmentMesh incrementally syncs MC terrain through putCell / removeCell; Java never solves collisions contact 接触 A negative separation means penetration take over 接管 IK takes over the authored local pose of the chain bones; with physics enabled, physics takes over pose evaluation crosshair picking 准星拾取 The mouse button (0 is the left button) and the maximum picking distance base body 素体 The undressed base humanoid model; not bare model

docs.text: English 中文 Notes pipeline 管线 Not conduit or duct model pipeline 模型管线 ModelPipeLine scheduling 调度 ModelRenderScheduler keeps one policy per mounted instance, ALWAYS by default visibility 可见性 Continuous drawing, explicit host control and the vanilla renderer mark are the three policies culling 剔除 Not cropping or clipping frustum 视锥 Always view frustum render distance 视距 setMaxRenderDistance(instance, blocks) culls by squared camera distance; 0 means unlimited frame mark 帧标记 The host renderer calls markRenderedThisFrame within its visible frame; the first model pass calls flipFrame once gate (verb: gating) 门控 / 闸门 Two Chinese wordings for one concept, both gate; distance and frustum are extra gates on top of the mode mount 挂载 The registry matches mounts by the caller's key; not installation attachment 装备挂接 McModelHandle.attachToAnchor / detachFromAnchor camera view 机位 One rendering unit inside the same client process; consumers may not resize or delete textures read-only borrow 只读借用 compositing 合成 effect 效果 Effects of the same kind share renderers and pipeline state post-processing 后处理 scope 作用域 A registrar for dynamic content that closes the resources it owns; parent scopes own child scopes descriptor 描述 An immutable value that defines a piece of resource configuration generation 分代 Shader handles stay stable across resource reloads while the internal compiled instances are replaced per generation upload 上传 A GPU upload receives a complete snapshot; the dirty range describes the changed elements in-flight read 在途读取 Storage cannot be overwritten while the GPU is still reading it upload ring 上传环 UploadRing handles slot rotation, dirty-element merging, version tracking and resource lifetime atlas 图集 Base color, normal and specular are packed into three matching atlases material variant 材质变体 Same source texture with different parameters produces an independent variant and independent normal/specular sprites straight alpha 直通 alpha translucent replay 半透明回放 Every draw and every translucent replay records consumption; a completion marker must not be missed even when this frame's data did not change ray marching 光线步进 The cloud field is drawn with one sky-covering ray march plus one composite pass, never one full-screen pass per cloud self-shadowing 自遮光 The cloud field samples nearby density along the sun direction to approximate its own shadowing batching 合批 Static block geometry suits section mesh batching host 宿主 The host owns the frame and view entry points; the source is the pack stack, so data packs can override it the two phases 两个时机 registration phase and reload phase; not "two timings" domain 域 The two arrays of an index manifest: on_register (registration domain) and on_reload (reload domain);
