docs.title: MC final frame offscreen output
docs.text:
Interface, configuration, and call reference. For the principles see frame-output.md.

MinecraftFrameOutputs routes the frame at the final RenderTarget.blitToScreen(width, height) call in Minecraft.runTick. The world, post-processing, HUD, GUI, loading screen, and FPS debug overlay have already been drawn; the output reuses the shader and scaling of that same native final blit. It does not replace getMainRenderTarget() and does not modify the camera or intercept other internal FBOs during the world pass. This is the WYSIWYG output entry point for the final frame.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Register on the render thread, keep the returned registration, and close it when the output is no longer needed:

import lib.kasuga.rendering.output.FrameOutputMode;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.output.mc.MinecraftFrameOutputs;

// Shown in both the MC window and the output FBO.
var capture = MinecraftFrameOutputs.open(FrameOutputMode.MIRROR, frame -> {
    var texture = frame.resource();
    // texture.textureId(): the complete final frame, usable by materials, compositors, and encoders.
    // texture.framebufferId(): the color attachment can be read in the current GL context.
    // frame.width()/height(): the window's actual framebuffer pixel size.
    // frame.viewId()/frameNumber(): the output view and the delivery sequence number of that view.
    consumeTexture(texture);
});

// No longer shown in the MC window; delivered to the output FBO only.
var exclusive = MinecraftFrameOutputs.open(FrameOutputMode.OFFSCREEN_ONLY, frame -> {
    consumeTexture(frame.resource());
});

// Unsubscribe on the render thread. The view's FBO and color texture are released only after the last subscription closes.
capture.close();
exclusive.close();

The consumeTexture in the code is the caller's consumer. The output provides a color texture in this process and the current GL context; transferring it to another process, machine, or video file is up to the consumer (readback, encoding, or sharing). There is no need to render the world a second time just for the output.

With no registration, the native screen blit runs directly, no FBO is allocated, and no GL state is queried. The same view is captured only once per frame; multiple registrations share the same read-only OutputFrame and FBO/color texture handle, and capture does not repeat as subscriptions grow. Any OFFSCREEN_ONLY registration that delivered normally and is still valid cancels the screen blit for that frame. Window events, the game loop, and the display swap keep running. After all exclusive outputs are closed, normal display resumes automatically.

docs.title: Lifecycle and errors
docs.text:
• All registration, delivery, and closing operations are held by the render thread; the MC entry point and registration modification operations check the thread. Callbacks also run synchronously on the render thread; do not block inside them waiting on encoding/network.
  • OutputFrame and FrameTexture are shared read-only borrows; they must not be written, resized, or deleted. A texture ID is a GPU handle, not a CPU pointer; the immutability of the Java record cannot stop a caller from wrongly calling GL write operations. The next frame may overwrite the texture, and a resize or the closing of the last subscription deletes the old GL objects. Keeping the frame outside the callback requires copying it into your own storage; do not hand a bare texture ID to an async thread with no GL context.
  • The FBO resizes automatically to the final window framebuffer size; the output color is RGBA8 with no depth. The native screen blit writes RGB only, and the output is initialized to opaque alpha. On a size change the new FBO is validated first, then the old FBO is retired, without changing MC's render size, GUI scale, or projection.
  • Textures follow the OpenGL bottom-left origin. When writing top-left images such as PNG, flip Y as the consumer requires.
  • Output targets restore their own independent read/draw framebuffer bindings and viewport; texture bindings, clear color, color mask, and scissor modified temporarily during allocation are restored before the final blit. Consumers should restore any other GPU state they modify and follow MC's state caching API.
  • A consumer exception closes only that registration; other consumers keep borrowing the same completed frame. If target creation or drawing fails, all subscriptions of that view are closed and the capture error is reported once; other views are unaffected. If no valid exclusive output succeeds, the native screen blit still runs for that frame, so a single export failure does not permanently swallow the screen. A registration's isClosed() reveals outputs that were removed automatically; latest() can be borrowed only while the registration is valid.
  • Closing your own/another registration or the whole router inside a callback defers the actual resource release until the current publication ends; borrowed resources do not become invalid mid-callback.
  • On Minecraft shutdown, the Mixin releases all outputs before the window and render resources are destroyed.

docs.title: Multi-camera
docs.text:
The default view is minecraft:main. FrameOutputRouter<T>, FrameOutputTarget<T>, and FrameBlitter do not depend on Minecraft. A view ID identifies a view that has already finished rendering and can be used for multiple cameras, different output windows, or encoding channels. The actual camera producer is now provided by MinecraftWorldViews; for usage and supported scope see the multi-camera and offscreen output document.

var cameraOutput = MinecraftFrameOutputs.open("camera:rear", FrameOutputMode.MIRROR,
        frame -> consumeTexture(frame.resource()));

// A custom producer can also deliver directly once its own final frame is complete:
var delivery = MinecraftFrameOutputs.publish("camera:rear", width, height,
        (w, h) -> rearCameraFinalTarget.blitToScreen(w, h));

Registering only an output consumer does not create a camera; you also need to register a MinecraftWorldViews producer with the same view ID. The camera owns the world rendering color/depth targets, and the output router owns the shared color target of the completed frame per view; closing a consumer only unsubscribes, and the color target is released only when the last subscription closes. Closing the camera producer and unsubscribing remain different operations.

A non-MC host can use new FrameOutputRouter<>(checkThread, targetFactory) and then call register(viewId, mode, consumer). The factory is called lazily once per view. The retained four-argument register overload lets the first registration of that view choose the factory; later registrations share the existing target and the factory passed in is not executed until the last subscription closes.

docs.title: Verification entry
docs.text:
./gradlew :modules:modelling:test :modules:modelling:renderGlTest
./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClient \
  -PkasugaTestFrameOutput=true \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=/absolute/path/to/isolated-client-directory

The unit tests cover shared frame identity, single capture, release on the last subscription, replacement inside a callback, view isolation, failure fallback, and deferred release. The standalone GL regression adds three consumers sharing one FBO/one final blit, consumer exception isolation, and release on the last subscription, while using Minecraft's final blit fragment shader to check RGB/orientation, opaque alpha, resize, read/draw/viewport restoration on exception, and release on close.

The optional client test runs on the menu screen, compares the native complete GUI colors with the output FBO pixel by pixel, toggles MIRROR/OFFSCREEN_ONLY, resizes the window and deliberately fails one consumer, then restores normal frames and exits. Results and PNGs are written to debug/frame-output/ in the isolated directory.

docs.title: State Machine and Animation Clip JSON Reference
docs.text: Type: Reference (information-oriented, for lookup). Applies to: Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.203, Parchment 2024.11.17, Java 21. The fields on this page only hold within this version range. Line numbers are locator hints only and may drift as the source changes; treat class names, method names, and test names as authoritative. Authoritative sources: element fields come from the codecs (StateMachineDefinition.CODEC, AnimationClip.CODEC, and their sub-codecs); wrappers and discovery rules come from StateMachineDefinitionLoader / AnimationClipLoader / ReloadOrchestrator / FsmReloadHandler / FsmClipsReloadHandler. Every rule cites its source; this page does not carry over the old conclusions from before the rewrite. Boundary: this page covers only the element format, the file wrapper, and the reload orchestration of state machine definitions and animation clips. For index files and registration-phase content files see data-driven/schema.md; for Java API signatures see data-driven/README.md; for content-organization practice see data-driven/guide-content.md.

docs.title: 0. Two Files, Three Kinds of Readers
docs.text:
The animation state machine (FSM, finite state machine) is a Mecanim-style layered state machine: multiple layers (state layers) run in parallel, and every tick composites the pose of each layer into the model. Both the FSM and the animation clips it plays (an animation clip is a segment of bone / morph / material-frame tracks sampled along a timeline) are defined in JSON.

The reload phase (the resource re-read triggered by /reload) has exactly one orchestrator: ReloadOrchestrator (data-driven module, package lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.reload). It reads the pack stack (not the jar), so data packs can override these files. Types are not hard-coded into it: the typeName() of each registered ReloadHandler is a valid top-level key; the modelling side registers two handlers, corresponding to two top-level keys:

Top-level key handler (modelling) Decoder it delegates to Content state_machines FsmReloadHandler StateMachineDefinitionLoader.decodeFile State machine definitions animation_clips FsmClipsReloadHandler AnimationClipLoader.decodeFile Animation clip elements

Both decoders (StateMachineDefinitionLoader / AnimationClipLoader) are pure file-layer components and stay in modelling; neither of them holds a reload listener or bucket-clearing logic of its own anymore. The two ReloadHandlers are one layer wrapped around them: they claim the top-level keys, declare the glob directories, write to buckets, and run the wrap-up validation, and FsmReloadHandlerRegistrar registers them into ReloadHandlerRegistry at context startup in fsm → clips order. The whole reload cycle (clear buckets / discover / register / re-check) is owned by ReloadOrchestrator; the orchestrator itself does not know either name, state_machines or animation_clips.

docs.title: 1. File Locations and Discovery
docs.text:
Content Location Discovery State machine data/<namespace>/state_machines/<path>.json, or any path listed by on_reload Directory glob + index, two entry points Animation clip Any path listed by on_reload (by convention placed under animation_clips/) Index only
  • state_machines/ has a directory glob: FsmReloadHandler.globDirectories() declares StateMachineDefinitionLoader.PATH = "state_machines" (FsmReloadHandler.java:69-71), and ReloadOrchestrator.collectGlob (:348-367) uses ResourceManager.listResources to list that namespace's .json files in resource-location order. A file is read even if no index lists it.
  • animation_clips/ has no directory glob (AnimationClipLoader.java:29; FsmClipsReloadHandler keeps globDirectories() at its default empty set). A clip file that no index lists is never read. Test: AnimationClipReloadTest.animationClipsDirectoryIsNotGlobDiscovered.
  • A state_machines/ file that the index lists is skipped by the glob entry point so it is read only once (collectGlob, ReloadOrchestrator.java:348-367; test ReloadOrchestratorTest.globAndIndexListingTheSameFileReadItOnce).

A file path and a definition id need not match: the id is decided by the element's own id field (see §5.1, §6.1). A bare path (no colon) is given the default namespace minecraft by Id.parse (Id.java:49-71).

docs.title: 2.1 The Top-Level Key state_machines
docs.text:
Every state_machines file is a JSON object in which the value of the state_machines key must be an array:

{ "state_machines": [ <definition>, ... ] }

Rules (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.decodeFile, :67-100):

  • the body must be a JSON object;
  • it must have the top-level key state_machines (constant FIELD_STATE_MACHINES = "state_machines", :42);
  • the value of that key must be an array.

Multiple top-level keys are legal: a file may carry other top-level keys as well (such as animation_clips); this decoder reads only its own key and ignores the rest, and no longer rejects the file for that reason. Among them, keys claimed by no reload type (genuinely unknown keys) get one unsupported top-level field report from the orchestrator, but this does not affect the contribution of state_machines (see §2.4).

The three violations (non-object body, missing key, non-array value) reject the whole file, return one error, and register no definitions. The per-case wording is in decodeFile (:67-100); the missing-key diagnostic quotes the expected shape {"state_machines": [ <definition>, ... ]} verbatim (EXPECTED_SHAPE, :45).

docs.title: 2.2 A Legal Example
docs.text:
Below is a complete file the current loader can parse (id = example:lamp, two states, one trigger transition + one guard transition):

{
  "state_machines": [
    {
      "id": "example:lamp",
      "state_vars": [
        { "name": "lit", "type": "bool", "default": false, "ephemeral": true }
      ],
      "layers": [
        {
          "id": "main",
          "mode": "base",
          "initial_state": "off",
          "states": [
            { "id": "off" },
            { "id": "on", "pose": { "morphs": { "glow": 1.0 } } }
          ],
          "transitions": [
            { "id": "off_to_on", "from": "off", "to": "on", "trigger_on": "lit", "cross_fade_seconds": 0.2 },
            { "id": "on_to_off", "from": "on", "to": "off", "when": ["example:not_lit"], "cross_fade_seconds": 0.2 }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}

trigger_on: "lit" points to a boolean variable name declared in this machine's state_vars; when: ["example:not_lit"] points to a guard function registered on the code side. If either is not registered it only warns when the machine is built and does not affect file decoding (see §5.7).

docs.title: 2.3 The Old Wrapper-Less Shape Is Rejected (Breaking Change)
docs.text:
The old format put the definition directly at the top level (with no state_machines wrapper). This is the legacy shape for the current implementation, and the whole file is rejected:

{
  "id": "example:lamp",
  "state_vars": [ { "name": "lit", "type": "bool" } ],
  "layers": [ { "id": "main", "initial_state": "off" } ]
}

Writing it this way yields missing top-level key 'state_machines' and 0 registrations. The pre-rewrite fsm.md gave exactly this format; the two are directly opposite.

Executable evidence:

  • StateMachineDefinitionLoaderTest.legacyShapeIsRejectedAndReportsExpectedShape (:77-83): asserts that the decode result is an empty definition list and that the error text contains state_machines;
  • ReloadOrchestratorTest.legacyShapeRegistersNothing (:244-247): after a full reload cycle the id is null.

docs.title: 2.4 Extra Top-Level Keys No Longer Reject the File
docs.text:
{
  "state_machines": [
    { "id": "example:lamp", "layers": [ { "id": "main", "initial_state": "off" } ] }
  ],
  "extra": 1
}

extra is claimed by no reload type, so the orchestrator reports one unsupported top-level field 'extra' for it (with a reverse D9 hint attached); but state_machines is still decoded and still registered as usual. The decision no longer depends on "how many top-level keys there are" but checks each unknown key one by one (ReloadOrchestrator.dispatch; ContentStructure.unknownKeys). Tests StateMachineDefinitionLoaderTest.extraTopLevelKeyDoesNotAffectThisType (:96-102), ReloadOrchestratorTest.extraTopLevelKeyIsReportedButDoesNotRejectTheFile (:265-275).

Earlier versions checked root.size() != 1 inside decodeFile and rejected the whole file for one extra key; that check has been removed.

docs.title: 3. The animation_clips File Wrapper
docs.text:
The shape is symmetric, and the claimed top-level key is animation_clips (constant AnimationClipLoader.FIELD_ANIMATION_CLIPS = "animation_clips", :45):

{ "animation_clips": [ <clip>, ... ] }

The exact same three file-level violations, with the same whole-file-rejection semantics (AnimationClipLoader.decodeFile, :69-102). Tests in AnimationClipLoaderTest: rejectsANonObjectBody / rejectsAMissingTopLevelKey / ignoresAnExtraTopLevelKey / rejectsANonArrayValue.

Multiple top-level keys are legal: one file may declare both state_machines and animation_clips, and each of the two handlers claims its own key and contributes its own entries, with no effect on the other (ReloadOrchestrator.dispatch, :429-470; test AnimationClipReloadTest.mixedTopLevelKeysAreConsumedByBothHandlers). Only a genuinely unknown key (claimed by no handler) reports unsupported top-level field, and it does not block the known keys.

docs.title: 4. File-Level Strictness vs Element-Level Tolerance
docs.text:
Both decoders share the same failure isolation, whose boundary is file and element:

Level Violation Consequence File level Non-object body / missing top-level key / non-array value The whole file is rejected, one error, 0 registrations File level A genuinely unknown top-level key (claimed by no handler) One unsupported top-level field report; known keys still contribute as usual (partial-apply) Element level An array element is not an object Only that element is skipped, reporting key[i] must be an object ...; element skipped Element level The element is an object but codec decoding fails (missing required field / wrong type / unknown enum token) Only that element is skipped, reporting key[i] failed to decode ...; element skipped; siblings carry on as usual Element level The element object has a key the codec does not name No error; ignored
  • The dividing line is implemented by two sections of logic in decodeFile: the shape check runs first and returns for the whole file; only after it passes are elements decoded one by one through CODEC.parse(...).resultOrPartial(...) (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.java:88-98; AnimationClipLoader.java:90-100).
  • Tests for element-level tolerance: StateMachineDefinitionLoaderTest.badElementIsSkippedWhileSiblingsDecode (:85-94, an array with a number and an object missing layers sandwiched in it, where both good elements still decode), AnimationClipLoaderTest.skipsAMalformedElementAndKeepsItsSiblings (:104-114) and skipsAnElementWithoutAnId (:117-126).
  • Unknown keys inside an element are ignored: AnimationClipLoaderTest.ignoresKeysTheClipRecordDoesNotName (:132-144). This is the biggest difference between the element level and the file level: a genuinely unknown key at the file's top level does get reported (though the file's known keys still take effect as usual), whereas one extra key inside an element object is silently ignored with no output at all. State machine elements are the same (StateMachineDefinition.CODEC is also a RecordCodecBuilder), but so far only the clip side has a dedicated test for this.
  • An empty array is legal: {"animation_clips": []} passes cleanly (AnimationClipLoaderTest.emptyClipArrayIsValid, :53-59).

docs.title: 5. state_machines Element Fields
docs.text: The element schema is decided by StateMachineDefinition.CODEC (StateMachineDefinition.java:21-25) and is independent of the wrapper: the wrapper exists only at the file layer, so inline / script registration, content hashing, and programmatic registration are all unaffected (StateMachineDefinitionLoader class Javadoc :14-33).

docs.title: 5.1 Definition Top Level
docs.text:
Field Type Required Default Meaning id string (namespace:path) Yes — Machine identifier; blocks / BEs use it to bind; parsed by Id.CODEC (Id.java:112) state_vars array No [] Typed variable declarations layers array Yes — Parallel state layers

Source: StateMachineDefinition.CODEC (StateMachineDefinition.java:21-25). A missing or illegal id → that element fails to decode and is skipped.

docs.title: 5.2 state_vars[]
docs.text:
Field Type Required Default Meaning name string Yes — Reference name within this machine; trigger_on resolves by it (this machine's declarations are checked first, then the registry) type string No "float" Built-in type token, see below default any JSON No That type's zero value Default value matching the codec of type reference string No — namespace:path, referencing an already-registered variable; once given, type / default are ignored ephemeral bool No false true = cleared automatically at the end of the tick, used as a trigger external_writable bool No true false = a derived parameter, writable only inside the machine sync bool No false true = goes through the FSM sync channel (server-authoritative)

Source: StateVarDefinition.CODEC (StateVarDefinition.java:51-59); for field semantics see that class's Javadoc (:12-27).

The built-in type token catalog (StateVarType, StateVarType.java:24-28): bool / int / float / string / vec3. Three things to note:

  • type and default are resolved only at build time: StateVarDefinition.CODEC stores them as a string / raw JSON, and an unknown type or a mis-decoded default does not reject the file. Resolution happens in DefinitionStateMachineFactory.resolveInline (:124-138): an unknown type makes StateVarType.byToken throw; a failed default decode only WARNs and falls back to that type's zero value (decodeOrDefault, :140-146).
  • For reference-mode resolution see resolveReference (:112-121): a referenced id that does not exist → WARN, and that variable does not take effect.
  • The pre-rewrite documentation also listed resource as a built-in type. The current StateVarType catalog has no resource, and no StateVarType.register(...) call can be found anywhere in the repository; today resource is called built-in only in scripting's Javadoc (AnimatorBuilderApi.java:192). See Appendix B, "To Be Confirmed".

docs.title: 5.3 layers[]
docs.text:
Field Type Required Default Meaning id string Yes — Layer identifier mode string No "base" base (bottom layer) / additive (accumulate) / override (overwrite) weight float No 1.0 Weight of this layer bone_mask string No all Bone mask (affects only the specified bone group); resolution in LayerDefinition.resolvedMask states array No [] State nodes transitions array No [] Transition edges initial_state string Yes — Initial state id

Source: LayerDefinition.CODEC (LayerDefinition.java:24-32). mode is parsed by BlendMode.CODEC (BlendMode.java:18-23), and an unknown value reports a decode error outright, causing the whole definition element to be skipped.

Layer compositing semantics (BlendMode Javadoc, BlendMode.java:10-17): base is the bottom layer and its pose is the baseline; additive accumulates on top of the baseline; override overwrites the channels selected by the mask.

The BlendMode here (layer compositing: base / additive / override) and MorphInstance.BlendMode (color multiply-add for a single morph) are two different axes (BlendMode.java:6-9).

docs.title: 5.4 states[]
docs.text:
Field Type Required Default Meaning id string Yes — State identifier duration_ticks int No none Number of ticks the state lasts; with a when_complete transition it ends automatically pose object No empty pose The static pose this state applies to the model (see §5.6) on_enter / on_exit / on_update id[] No [] Action function ids (see §5.7) clip string or object No none Animation clip reference (see §5.8)

Source: StateDefinition.CODEC (StateDefinition.java:25-33).

docs.title: 5.5 transitions[]
docs.text:
Field Type Required Default Meaning id string Yes — Transition identifier from / to string Yes — From / to state ids trigger_on string No none Trigger: points to a boolean variable name / id, fires when it is set when_complete bool No false Fires when the from state reaches duration_ticks cross_fade_seconds float No 0 Cross-fade seconds; 0 = switch immediately when id[] No [] Guard function ids; the transition is allowed only if all of them are true on_fire id[] No [] Action function ids executed when the transition fires

Source: TransitionDefinition.CODEC (TransitionDefinition.java:25-34). trigger_on requires the variable to be of boolean type; a non-ephemeral variable only WARNs and is handled with tick semantics (DefinitionStateMachineFactory.resolveTrigger, :231-248). When from / to point to a state that does not exist, that transition is skipped at build time (buildLayer, :175-180).

docs.title: 5.6 pose
docs.text:
pose is the generic static pose a state applies to the model: morph weights, bone transforms, material frames, and IK switches. The same Pose is also usable through ModelPosing, and the shared runtime does not require the target model to come from any particular file format.

Field Type Required Default Meaning morphs object (string→float) No {} morph name → weight bones array No [] List of bone transforms frames array No [] List of material frames ik_enabled object (string→bool) No {} Generic IK chain name to enabled state, see Pose IK channel

Source: PoseDefinition.CODEC. The IK channel follows the same pose blending and write-ownership rules; after driving stops, or after switching to a pose that lacks that channel, the default enabled state is restored.

bones[] (PoseDefinition.BoneDefinition.CODEC, :31-35):

Field Type Required Default name string Yes — transform object Yes — mode string No "replace" (replace / add / multiply; an unknown value falls back to replace, ApplyMode.byName, ApplyMode.java:28-38)

transform (TransformDefinition.CODEC, TransformDefinition.java:26-30): translate / rotate / scale are all arrays of exactly 3 floats (VEC3F_CODEC, :19-22), defaulting to [0,0,0] / [0,0,0] / [1,1,1] respectively; rotate is in degrees.

frames[] (PoseDefinition.FrameDefinition.CODEC, :42-45): material (string, required), frame (int, required).

docs.title: 5.7 Behavior Function References
docs.text:
The ids in when / on_enter / on_exit / on_update / on_fire are registered by the code side (Java or script) through FsmFunctionLibrary: guards with registerCondition, actions with registerAction (FsmFunctionLibrary.java:19-25). JSON stores only the ids.

Unregistered functions do not affect file decoding: they are aggregated into a single WARN when the machine is built, a missing condition degrades to false, and a missing action is a no-op (DefinitionStateMachineFactory.validateDefinition Javadoc, :321-326).

docs.title: 5.8 clip
docs.text:
states[].clip references an already-registered animation clip, written in two ways (StateDefinition.ClipDefinition.CODEC, StateDefinition.java:47-50):

  • Object: { "id": "ns:clip", "loop": true }, where loop defaults to false (:40-45);
  • String shorthand: "ns:clip", equivalent to loop: false.

Reference resolution and dangling handling are in §9. All four states of the real fixture fan_machine_data_driven.json use the object form to reference the same clip and set loop: true.

docs.title: 6. animation_clips Element Fields
docs.text: The element schema is decided by AnimationClip.CODEC (AnimationClip.java:47-54). An element carries its own id (the very id states[].clip references); the loader does not extract an id separately (AnimationClipLoader class Javadoc :20-26).

docs.title: 6.1 Clip Top Level
docs.text: Field Type Required Default Meaning id string (namespace:path) Yes — Clip identifier duration_seconds float No 1.0 Clip duration (seconds) bones array No [] Bone keyframe tracks morphs array No [] morph value tracks frames array No [] Material frame tracks functions array No [] Formula tracks (evaluated every frame)

docs.title: 6.2 bones[]
docs.text:
Field Type Required Default bone string Yes — keyframes array Yes —

keyframes[] (Keyframe.CODEC, AnimationClip.java:71-75): time (float, required), transform (TransformDefinition, required, fields as in §5.6), easing (string, optional, default "linear").

docs.title: 6.3 morphs[]
docs.text: morph (string, required) + keyframes (required); a keyframe is { "time": float, "value": float, "easing": string? } (MorphKeyframe.CODEC, :93-97).

docs.title: 6.4 frames[]
docs.text: material (string, required) + keyframes (required); a keyframe is { "time": float, "frame": int } (FrameKeyframe.CODEC, :111-114). Material frame tracks round to the nearest keyframe and do not interpolate (FrameTrack Javadoc, :100).

docs.title: 6.5 functions[]
6.6 easing Names
docs.text:
easing maps a string to a built-in easing (EASING_CODEC, AnimationClip.java:39-45). An unknown name does not error; it falls back to linear. The available names are Easing.NAMED (Easing.java:232-246):

linear, ease_in_quad, ease_out_quad, ease_in_out_quad, ease_in_cubic, ease_out_cubic, ease_in_out_cubic, ease_in_sine, ease_out_sine, ease_in_out_sine, back, elastic, bounce.

docs.title: 6.7 Unknown Keys Inside an Element Are Ignored
docs.text: Keys the AnimationClip record does not name are ignored by the codec, so an author can add comment-like fields without breaking loading (AnimationClipLoader class Javadoc :24-26; test AnimationClipLoaderTest.ignoresKeysTheClipRecordDoesNotName, :132-144).

docs.title: 7. Differences Between the Two Discovery Paths
docs.text:
state_machines animation_clips Directory glob Yes (data/<ns>/state_machines/*.json) No Listed by the index on_reload Supported The only entry point When not listed in the index Still picked up by the glob Never read Both entry points listing the same file The glob entry skips it; read once Not applicable

Source: FsmReloadHandler.globDirectories() (FsmReloadHandler.java:69-71) declares StateMachineDefinitionLoader.PATH (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.java:39); the glob listing is in ReloadOrchestrator.collectGlob (:348-367); AnimationClipLoader class Javadoc (:29); ReloadOrchestrator class Javadoc (:77-91). Tests AnimationClipReloadTest.animationClipsDirectoryIsNotGlobDiscovered, ReloadOrchestratorTest.globAndIndexListingTheSameFileReadItOnce.

The glob only handles discovery; routing always follows the file's top-level key. A file that lands in the state_machines/ directory but writes animation_clips at the top is still handled by the clip handler (ReloadOrchestrator.collectGlob Javadoc, :340-347).

docs.title: 8. The Orchestrator ReloadOrchestrator and the Two Handlers
8.1 The Stage Order of reload()
docs.text:
reload(ResourceManager) (:186-193) wraps the private runCycle (:198-248); the order within one cycle is fixed and type-agnostic (it walks the registry rather than hard-coding the two types):

  1. Build the cycle: create one HandlerCycle per handler in ReloadHandlerRegistry.all() (:199-201).
  2. Clear the buckets: call runClear(entry) → clearBucket() for each handler, exactly once per cycle (runClear, :250-261; call sites :213-215). An exception thrown by clearBucket() is caught in place by runClear and recorded as a Domain.RELOAD_DATA diagnostic, while the other handlers clear their buckets as usual (a per-handler guard, the same kind as in the wrap-up stage). FsmReloadHandler clears only the RESOURCE half of FsmDefinitions, and FsmClipsReloadHandler clears only the RESOURCE half of FsmAnimationClips (script wins, see §10).
  3. Aggregate the glob directories: collect each handler's globDirectories() (:222-225); state_machines contributes state_machines/, clips contributes nothing.
  4. List the namespaces and sort them, with dual-path discovery per namespace (collectNamespace, :266-288): first readReloadPaths (:307) reads the index manifest's on_reload, then collectGlob (:348-367) scans the aggregated glob directories (skipping paths already listed), and finally collectIndex (:369) reads the files that on_reload points to.
  5. Register: call register(entry) for each handler (:507-526); glob candidates come first and index candidates after (HandlerCycle.candidates(), :595-599) → deduplicate and write to the bucket.
  6. Wrap-up re-check: call runAfterReload(entry) for each handler (:530-538), only for entries registered this cycle, and after all the registers. FsmReloadHandler.afterReload runs the dangling clip check here.

The index side reuses the registration domain's JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest / resolveIndexManifests, so D6's "the same path listed in both → neither domain consumes it" also holds on the reload side (readReloadPaths, :307).

docs.title: 8.2 Types Are Registry-Driven, Not Hard-Coded
docs.text:
The orchestrator does not know any reload type name: the set of top-level keys is derived from ReloadHandlerRegistry.all() by knownTypeNames() (:473-486), and dispatch (dispatch, :429-470) routes by each handler's typeName(). Adding one reload type = implementing one ReloadHandler and calling ReloadHandlerRegistry.register in a @Context bean, without touching the orchestrator. This is what §4.6 means by "the reload side is symmetric with the registration phase"; the two FSM types are registered by FsmReloadHandlerRegistrar (:23-31) in fsm → clips order, and that order decides the dispatch/registration order and in turn the cross-type last-wins.

To understand how one handler's responsibilities are split, see §8.5.

docs.title: 8.3 last-wins and "No Side Effects for the Loser"
docs.text: Across the two entry points, the last same-id candidate in the load sequence wins (glob first, index second; within a file, the array's writing order). The decision uses the shared DuplicateIdResolver, and the loser never enters the handler's register at all, so no override notification is triggered; each conflict logs a WARN plus one bucket entry (resolveAndReport, :545-556). Tests: ReloadOrchestratorTest.indexEntryWinsOverTheGlobEntryAndTheLoserIsNotRegistered, duplicateIdWithinFileLastWins; on the clip side AnimationClipReloadTest.laterClipFileWinsForTheSameId.

docs.title: 8.4 Four Layers of Exception Guards + a Fallback
docs.text:
reload() sits on the reload listener path; a thrown exception would abort the whole pack reload with the buckets half-cleared, so every failure must be turned in place into a "log + bucket" diagnostic:

Layer Location Attribution target Per handler (bucket clearing) runClear :250-261 The library mod (KasugaLib.MODID) Per file (read / decode) readAndDispatch :405-415 The namespace the file lives in Per namespace (discovery mechanism) collectNamespace :266-288 That namespace Per entry (registration) register :507-526 The namespace the entry lives in Per handler (wrap-up re-check) runAfterReload :530-538 The library mod (when no finer attribution exists) Fallback (no attribution available) reload() :186-193 The library mod (KasugaLib.MODID)

Tests ReloadOrchestratorExceptionBoundaryTest: uppercaseIndexPathIsRejectedAndTheCycleContinues, throwingFileIsIsolatedAndTheNextFileStillLoads, wholeCycleFailureIsCaughtAndRecordedAgainstTheLibraryMod. When the whole cycle fails, the buckets stay empty: the empty state is the truthful outcome and the errors stay in the bucket (class Javadoc :106-114).

docs.title: 8.5 How the Two Handlers Split Responsibilities
docs.text: FsmReloadHandler FsmClipsReloadHandler typeName() state_machines animation_clips globDirectories() {state_machines} default empty = index-only describeFile() "state machine file" "animation clip file" clearBucket() definitions.clearResource() clips.clearResource() decode() delegates to StateMachineDefinitionLoader.decodeFile delegates to AnimationClipLoader.decodeFile register() definitions.registerResource(id, def) AnimationClipLoader.register(clips, clip) afterReload() runs the dangling clip check (see §9) not overridden (default empty)

docs.title: 8.6 Diagnostics Go Through the Domain/Source-Key Dimension (Domain.RELOAD_DATA)
docs.text:
ReloadOrchestrator.reportError (:566-573) and both handlers' reportError / reportWarning all call Diagnostics.report(Diagnostics.Domain.RELOAD_DATA, namespace, ...), where namespace is the namespace of the file that failed. Reload-phase diagnostics go through the domain/source-key dimension (Domain.RELOAD_DATA, key = namespace), separate from the registration-phase mod dimension; runCycle clears that dimension at the start of each cycle and does not accumulate (Diagnostics.clear(Domain.RELOAD_DATA), :208). Read them with /kasuga_data errors [mod] (which lists both dimensions); details in sections 6 and 13 of data-driven/README.md.

The reload phase also gives a reverse hint for an unknown top-level key: if those fields are in fact registration content (such as blocks / items / registry_groups), list the file under on_register instead (dispatch, :439-446). The registration-type examples in the hint are derived at runtime from TypeHandlerRegistry.

docs.title: 9. clip References and Dangling References
docs.text:
• Build time: states[].clip is resolved by id in FsmAnimationClips; if it does not exist → WARN, and the state degrades to a static pose (configureState, :184).
  • Reload wrap-up: FsmReloadHandler.afterReload (:95-116) runs DefinitionStateMachineFactory.unknownClipReferences (:303-323) over each definition that did land this cycle, aggregating the dangling references (layer id + state id + missing clip id) into one WARN + bucket entry.
  • A dangling reference is only recorded; it does not block registration, nor does it change the build-time degradation behavior (ReloadOrchestrator class Javadoc :100-104; FsmReloadHandler.afterReload).
  • A candidate already shadowed by a script definition with the same id skips the re-check; it is no longer a live entry in the bucket (FsmReloadHandler.java:99-104).
  • Tests: AnimationClipReloadTest.missingClipFileIsReportedAfterTheLoad, wrongClipIdInTheClipFileIsReported; the same rule also feeds the build-time aggregate warning (unknownClipReferences Javadoc :289-302).

docs.title: 10. script-wins (Bucketing)
docs.text:
Both buckets split their entries in half by source:

Bucket SCRIPT entry RESOURCE entry Bucket clearing FsmAnimationClips register (FsmAnimationClips.java:53-59) registerResource (:66-74) clearResource (:100-102) drops RESOURCE only; clear() = clearResource (:117-119); clearAll (:108-110) clears everything FsmDefinitions register (FsmDefinitions.java:59-67) registerResource (:71-81) clearResource (:84-92) drops RESOURCE only
  • Write-side invariant: register (SCRIPT) overrides RESOURCE (with a WARN, "script wins"); registerResource (file) does not override SCRIPT entries.
  • So AnimationClipLoader.register always goes through registerResource (:113-121): a file clip can never shadow a same-id clip registered by a script / content test / game test.
  • Each reload cycle's clips.clearResource() drops only file-origin entries, so script-registered clips survive across reloads.
  • Tests: AnimationClipReloadTest.scriptClipWinsOverTheFileVersion, secondCycleReplaysClipFilesWithoutLeftovers; bucket unit tests in FsmAnimationClipsTest.

docs.title: 11. Counterexample Roundup
docs.text:
These snippets are listed so a reader can recognize "a shape copied from the old documentation" at a glance; two of them are no longer illegal under the new contract:

  1. A top-level definition without a wrapper (§2.3) → missing top-level key 'state_machines', whole file rejected.
  2. A genuinely unknown top-level key (§2.4) → one unsupported top-level field '...' report plus a reverse D9 hint, but known keys still contribute as usual (no longer a whole-file rejection).
  3. The top-level key's value written as an object (such as {"state_machines": {}}) → must be an array, whole file rejected (StateMachineDefinitionLoaderTest.nonArrayValueRejectsWholeFile; ReloadOrchestratorTest.NON_ARRAY_JSON).
  4. One file writing both kinds of content (§3) → now legal: each of the two handlers claims its own key and contributes its own entries, 0 diagnostics.
  5. An element missing layers (§4) → only that element is skipped; siblings carry on as usual.

docs.title: 12. Binding to Blocks
docs.text:
A data-driven registered block binds a machine id through the fsm_block / fsm_be factories: fsm_block creates the block (with a default block item), and fsm_be creates an AnimationBlockEntity, reading state_machine / model from params (FsmBlockEntityFactories.java:27-30,48-74). The state_machine string at the top level of the block entry is forwarded into the embedded BE's params.state_machine (BlockEntityTypeHandler.extractEmbedded, see schema.md §2.5).

This part belongs to registration-phase content files; for the format see the blocks and embedded block_entity chapters of data-driven/schema.md; for a working end-to-end example see data-driven/guide-content.md.

docs.title: Minecraft outfit resources and instance switching API
docs.text: For generic geometry/skeleton assembly see Model Assembly. This page only describes Minecraft's resource lookup, publication and handle integration; Model and its generic subsystems have no model format allowlist.

docs.title: Resource pack definitions
docs.text:
Files live in assets/<namespace>/model_assemblies/<path>.json, and the definition ID is <namespace>:<path>. For example assets/example/model_assemblies/winter.json corresponds to example:winter. Source models still have to be preloaded through the existing model_proxy configuration, see model loading.

{
  "body": {
    "id": "body",
    "model": "example:models/character.bbmodel",
    "regions": { "torso": [0, 1, 2] },
    "hide_regions": ["torso"]
  },
  "parts": [
    {
      "id": "shirt",
      "model": "example:models/shirt.glb",
      "bone_mappings": { "shirt_root": "root" }
    },
    {
      "id": "coat",
      "model": "example:models/coat.mmd.zip",
      "model_name": "coat",
      "include_dynamics": true
    }
  ],
  "bind_tolerance": 0.0001
}
Field Default/Requirement body Required part object; id defaults to body parts Optional part array, order preserved; each item's id is required and must not repeat model Required resource location per part; routing reuses the registered model pipeline model_name Optional internal model name, for Readers that need an internal entry lookup bone_mappings Object from source bone name to output bone name, default {}; the body cannot have aliases regions Object from region name to source face index array, default {} hide_regions Array of hidden region names, default []; an unknown name is an error hide_meshes Array of additional hidden face indices, default []; indices must be integers match_body_bones boolean, default true include_dynamics boolean, default true bind_tolerance Finite positive number, default 1e-4

Definitions are read during the resource preparation phase; after textures are ready they are published on the game thread. Invalid JSON makes that preparation fail, and a partial outfit definition is not published. When sources are missing the definition can still be registered, but mount returns false and it retries on the next tick. Validations that depend on the actual model, such as bind matrices and hidden face ranges, run after the full sources are ready. The body and the clothing must already be in the same bind space; this is not an automatic body-fitting interface.

docs.title: McModelHandle
docs.text:
Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.api.

McModelHandle handle = McModelHandle.ofAssembly(
        ResourceLocation.parse("example:winter"), instanceId, entity.position());
if (handle.mount()) {
    handle.scheduleVanillaRenderer();
    handle.markRenderedThisFrame();
}

boolean switched = handle.switchAssembly(ResourceLocation.parse("example:summer"));
Method Behavior static McModelHandle ofAssembly(ResourceLocation id, ResourceLocation instanceId, @Nullable Vec3 pos) Uses the global assembly service; may be created before the resource is published boolean switchAssembly(ResourceLocation id) Swaps using the global service; returns false when the service or the source is not ready boolean switchAssembly(McModelAssemblies service, ResourceLocation id) Explicit service, suited to custom pipelines McModelHandle onInstanceChanged(BiConsumer<ModelInstance, ModelInstance> callback) Called after the new instance has finished restoring its basic state; can install custom drivers/physics; null clears the callback

A swap first resolves the full sources, gets the cached model and mounts the new instance, then releases the handle's old instance. When a source is not ready, the current outfit is left unchanged; a bind/callback exception cleans up the new instance and is thrown to the caller, keeping the old instance. The callback runs before the generic driver migration, and a new driver set there takes precedence; external side effects of the callback itself are the caller's responsibility.

Position, rotation, scale and the double floating origin, the visibility mode, the distance limit and the ambient multiplier are preserved. Bone local inputs under compatible names, morph activation values, IK switches and persistent targets are copied to the new instance. Temporary per-frame IK targets, physics simulation results, custom tick-loop modules and anchor callbacks are not copied; reconfigure them in the callback. Manual material frames that need per-part remapping are handled in the callback as well.

The generic ModelPosing, AnimationPlayer and FsmPoseDriver implement RebindablePoseDriver. A named ModelPosing refreshes its data from the new Model's clip library and keeps the original timeline, playback time, speed and paused state; a missing clip restores an empty pose. An external shared clock is not restarted, and other targets following that player's own clock keep the same clock. The rebind of a plain AnimationPlayer/FSM migrates into the target; when its external clip data needs updating, hook that in the callback. A custom driver implements the same interface or is created in the callback.

Replacing or removing a source model, or reloading outfit resources, takes down the instances that borrowed the old resources. The handle keeps the basic state, and a later mount() re-resolves and mounts automatically; outfit definitions in the registry are kept while a source is temporarily missing. destroy() reclaims the current instance and its publication subscriptions, and releases the pending restoration state held by the handle. The instanceId of a global Actor should be managed uniquely by the host; the same service should not let two handles manage the same outfit/instanceId at the same time.

docs.title: Programmatic registration and custom services
docs.text:
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.loaders.assembly.ModelAssemblyDefinition;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.api.McModelAssemblies;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.registry.PipelineRegistry;

var definition = ModelAssemblyDefinition.builder("body",
        new McModelAssemblies.Reference(bodyLocation))
        .part("shirt", new McModelAssemblies.Reference(shirtLocation),
                part -> part.mapBone("shirt_root", "root"))
        .build();
var service = PipelineRegistry.assemblies(); // null before the client's built-in pipeline is initialized
if (service != null) service.register(outfitId, definition);

PipelineRegistry.ASSEMBLY has the value assembly; its pipeline has no format Reader and accepts derived generic Models. A plain of(modelLoc, ...) still routes by file extension; outfit definitions use ofAssembly and do not need a faked file extension.

The complete McModelAssemblies interface:

new McModelAssemblies(
    ModelPipeLine<?, ?, ResourceLocation, ResourceLocation, ?> output,
    Function<McModelAssemblies.Reference, McModelAssemblies.PublishedSource> sources,
    ModelAssemblyCache cache);

new McModelAssemblies.Reference(ResourceLocation model);
new McModelAssemblies.Reference(ResourceLocation model, @Nullable String modelName);
new McModelAssemblies.PublishedSource(
    ModelPipeLine<?, ?, ResourceLocation, ResourceLocation, ?> pipeline, ResourceLocation key);

void register(ResourceLocation id, ModelAssemblyDefinition<McModelAssemblies.Reference> definition);
boolean unregister(ResourceLocation id);
void replaceResourceDefinitions(Map<ResourceLocation, ModelAssemblyDefinition<McModelAssemblies.Reference>> next);
Map<ResourceLocation, ModelAssemblyDefinition<McModelAssemblies.Reference>> definitions();
@Nullable ModelAssembly resolve(ResourceLocation id);
@Nullable ModelInstance createAndBind(ResourceLocation id, ResourceLocation instanceId, @Nullable Transform root);
McModelHandle handle(ResourceLocation id, ResourceLocation instanceId);
ModelPipeLine<?, ?, ResourceLocation, ResourceLocation, ?> pipeline();
ModelAssemblyCache.Stats cacheStats();
void close();

A programmatic definition takes precedence over a resource-pack definition of the same name and is kept across resource reloads. unregister removes the programmatic override and reclaims that definition's instances; if a resource-pack definition exists it is restored, and the return value says whether a programmatic definition was removed. replaceResourceDefinitions applies a fully resolved resource snapshot and cleans up derived models and the assembly cache. close is idempotent and reclaims derived instances, cache references and source publication subscriptions; after closing, calling the resolve/register interfaces is an error. Service operations and model publication/render mounting must run serially on the game thread; the independent synchronization semantics of the base cache are still as described in the generic API.

The default source adapter reuses KasugaModelPipelines.publishedSource(Reference); while a resource reload is in progress it does not resolve resources of the old publication generation. A custom source function can integrate any published Model pipeline, without restricting its format.

docs.title: Generic resource definitions and publication lifecycle
docs.text:
The following interfaces are in render-core and do not depend on Minecraft:

static <K> ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> ModelAssemblyDefinition.builder(String bodyId, K source);
static <K> ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> ModelAssemblyDefinition.builder(
        String bodyId, K source, Consumer<ModelAssemblyDefinition.PartBuilder> configure);
ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> part(String id, K source);
ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> part(String id, K source, Consumer<ModelAssemblyDefinition.PartBuilder> configure);
ModelAssemblyDefinition.Builder<K> bindTolerance(float tolerance);
ModelAssemblyDefinition<K> build();
@Nullable ModelAssembly.Request ModelAssemblyDefinition.resolve(Function<? super K, ModelAssembly.Source> sources);

PartBuilder provides mapBone(String,String), matchBodyBones(boolean), includeDynamics(boolean), hideMeshes(int...), region(String,int...) and hideRegions(String...). This resource definition's hideRegions is resolved at call time, so define a region before hiding it. A definition can be constructed directly as ModelAssemblyDefinition(List<Part<K>>, float); the parameters of a nested Part<K> are, in order, id, source, Map<String,String> boneMappings, Set<Integer> hiddenMeshes, matchBodyBones, includeDynamics. Any K can be supplied by the host; resolving with a missing source returns null and produces no partial geometry.

new ModelAssemblyRegistry<K, I>(Function<? super K, ModelAssembly.Source> sources, ModelAssemblyCache cache);
void register(I id, ModelAssemblyDefinition<K> definition);
ModelAssemblyDefinition<K> definition(I id);
Map<I, ModelAssemblyDefinition<K>> definitions();
boolean remove(I id);
@Nullable ModelAssembly resolve(I id);
Set<I> invalidate(Model source);
void clearResolved();
ModelAssemblyCache.Stats cacheStats();

The registry keeps resource definitions and the latest complete results, and returned collection views are read-only; call invalidate when a source is updated, and it returns the definition IDs that depend on that old Model, which the host should use to take down the derived instances. A temporarily missing source produces no partial result.

ModelPipeLine adds:

Method Behavior Model getModel(StorageIdentifierType key) null when not published long modelRevision(StorageIdentifierType key) Current published version; 0 when absent StorageIdentifierType modelKeyOf(ModelInstance instance) Looks up the registered key, null when unregistered; the key is kept after binding for constant-time checks AutoCloseable onModelChanged(Consumer<ModelChange<StorageIdentifierType>> listener) game thread notification, running before the old instance is closed; closing the subscription unregisters void publishModels(Map<StorageIdentifierType,Model>) Merged publication; identical objects are skipped; replacing reclaims that key's instances void replaceModels(Map<StorageIdentifierType,Model>) Full replacement, deleting models missing from the snapshot boolean removeModel(StorageIdentifierType key) Removes that key and its instances; returns false when absent Builder.buildForPublishedModels() A derived pipeline without a SourceManager/Loader; still needs a bridge and backend

ModelChange<K> is key, previous, current, revision, and current is null on deletion. A listener exception does not skip other listeners or the old-instance reclamation; the errors are aggregated and thrown after cleanup completes. Instances are registered by resource key, and different keys sharing the same Model do not reclaim each other; createInstance with the same key/instanceId is idempotent. Calling prepare/load on a publication-only pipeline is an error; the old build methods of SourceManager/Loader pipelines still require a Reader.

ModelPublicationBatch<K>.publish(prepared) publishes one complete generation of a resource manager: the keys of prepared are ModelPipeLine<?,?,K,?,?>, and the values are Map<K,Model>. Old managed keys missing from the next generation are deleted, and other publishers' keys are kept. Every managed pipeline gets a chance to clean up, even if an earlier pipeline's cleanup fails.

docs.title: Driver and input migration
docs.text:
interface RebindablePoseDriver extends PoseDriver { void rebind(ModelInstance fresh); }
void ModelPosing.rebind(ModelInstance fresh);
ModelInstance ModelPosing.model();
void AnimationPlayer<T>.rebind(ModelInstance fresh, AnimationSampler<T> sampler, T data);
void AnimationPlayback<T,R>.retarget(AnimationSource<T,R> source, T data);
void SkeletonInstance.copyPoseInputsTo(SkeletonInstance target);
void MorphInstance<Id>.copyInputsTo(MorphInstance<Id> target);

Skeleton migration copies only named local transforms, IK switches and persistent targets; the root transform and floating origin are migrated separately by the host. Morph migration copies the activation value/factor corresponding to the identity, and does not copy result caches or source structure objects. Names that do not exist on the target are ignored. AnimationPlayback.retarget keeps the clock object/ownership; an own clock is updated to the new clip's duration, and an external clock is not modified. These control operations must run serially with tick, and the render sample consumes the existing snapshot mechanism.

docs.title: PMX and glTF Ragdoll Configuration
docs.text:
Interface, configuration, and call reference. For the concepts see mmd-ragdoll.md.

Physics definitions, IK, and diamond closure now all hang under Skeleton.getDynamics(). For extending the Reader/Builder and for the Caliko integration see skeleton-dynamics.md. SkeletonRagdoll keeps its historical API name; at runtime it only reads the generic skeleton definitions.

SkeletonRagdoll has two construction paths:

  • enablePhysics() uses every rigid body in the PMX file, so it also includes secondary-motion rigid bodies such as skirts and hair.
  • enablePhysics(profile) works for PMX or glTF and uses the profile's bodies to generate stable humanoid capsules and semantic masses; a PMX profile can keep unregistered author-made rigid body chains such as skirts, hair, and accessories through include_secondary_bodies as well. Inertia is generated by Box3D from the shape and the mass. glTF is not allowed to guess a human structure automatically without a profile.

Physics solving is done by the vendored Box3D C17 engine. RigidBodyWorld, SimBody, GenericRigidBody, and BallJoint in uml/dynamic/physics/core only handle Java object mapping, fixed steps, lifecycle, and state synchronization; SkeletonRagdoll is the PMX/skeleton adapter. Any code can create a world directly:

docs.title: Large-coordinate precision
docs.text:
When SkeletonRagdoll is enabled, the model root's world translation is moved out of the float bone matrices and stored as a separate double worldOrigin. Bone evaluation, Box3D rigid bodies, joints, and the cached block collisions all use local coordinates near that origin; at render time worldOrigin - cameraPosition is computed in double first, and only then written into the float pose matrix.

Body.position() and RayHit.point() are simulation-local coordinates; use ragdoll.worldPosition(body) when you need a world position. Double world coordinates such as a camera's or an entity's should enter the physics world through raycastWorld(...), beginDragWorld(...), updateDragTargetWorld(...), addStaticBoxColliderWorld(...), or worldToSimulation(...).

The MinecraftRagdollDeployments.Request constructor that takes a Vector3d worldOrigin preserves the fractional part of the deployment position; the old constructor is still compatible, but it can only inherit the float precision already present in the original Transform.

var crate = GenericRigidBody.box(new Vector3f(0.5f), 8f).at(2f, 5f, 1f);
var world = new RigidBodyWorld(List.of(crate), List.of(),
        RigidBodyWorld.DEFAULT_SUBSTEP_COUNT);
world.addGroundPlane(0f, 0.8f, 0f);
world.step(dt, RigidBodyWorld.KinematicDriver.none());

docs.title: Official implementation: physics blocks
docs.text:
The client-side service MinecraftBlockPhysics turns a Minecraft block's real VoxelShape into a compound Box3D rigid body (MinecraftBlockRigidBody): mass comes from block hardness and friction from slipperiness, it is drawn visually with the vanilla block renderer, terrain collision reuses the ragdoll's incremental block environment, and it interacts with the local player through a kinematic AABB proxy. For the full API and the client/server boundary see physics.md. Command entry points:

  • /kasuga_physics block [1-32]: spawns a physics block in front of the view.
  • /kasuga_physics status / clear: show or clear every physics block.

The cap is MAX_PROPS = 256; blocks that fall out of the bottom of the world are reclaimed automatically, and a dimension change clears everything.

docs.title: Debug commands
docs.text:
• /kasuga_ragdoll deploy: deploys a ragdoll with the built-in demo model on the ground in front of the player.
  • /kasuga_ragdoll deploy <model resource location>: reads the model manifest and deploys any published glTF that declares a ragdoll.
  • /kasuga_ragdoll list, remove all: list and undeploy deployments.

Lifecycle: a dimension change or leaving the world cleans up every deployment and releases mouse dragging; block-collision-environment invalidation notices are forwarded to nearby environments in real time by core's ClientBlockUpdateHooks (the ClientLevel#sendBlockUpdated mixin), and the periodic refresh is only a fallback.

docs.title: Native Box3D backend
docs.text:
• Box3D is pinned to the official main commit 30c67b5e6d0a3a66f0f506c69ce9e9e0587e3b7c, with the source in modules/modelling/src/main/native/box3d; for the license see modules/modelling/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.
  • CMake statically links Box3D into the kasuga_box3d JNI library; Gradle puts the current platform's artifacts in native/<os>-<arch>/, and the runtime extracts and loads them from the jar. CI builds and tests on Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, and macOS ARM64 separately, then merges them into the kasuga-modelling-universal universal jar.
  • Box3D owns integration, broad phase, narrow phase, contact, CCD, sleeping, and joint solving; Java contains no fallback solver.
  • PMX spheres, boxes, and capsules map directly to Box3D shapes. PMX six-axis joints map to spherical joints; the rotation range is approximated as cone/twist, and the three-axis translation range is currently tightened to a fixed anchor.
  • Minecraft block collision boxes map to Box3D static hulls created and destroyed incrementally. An infinite plane is approximated by a large static thin box placed along its normal.
  • Box3D has no fluid volume/buoyancy interface, so the old in-house fluid force model has been removed; a Minecraft fluid change still triggers a refresh of the adjacent collision cache, but applies no buoyancy or flow drag.

On the Minecraft side, MinecraftRagdollConfig.load(resourceManager, location) reads a configuration from the resource pack, after which you call config.attach(instance, levelSupplier). The built-in example is at assets/kasuga_lib/ragdolls/test_mmd.json, and a resource pack can override it or provide a new resource location. The built-in rendering demo now uses TDA Bunny Miku 2.0.pmx from test3.mmd.zip, whose body rigid body mapping is at assets/kasuga_lib/ragdolls/tda_bunny_miku.json. Rigid body indices are not reusable across different PMX files.

Model size is controlled by the .mmd.json next to the archive. For example test2.mmd.zip corresponds to test2.mmd.json:

{
  "encoding": "gbk",
  "model_scale": 0.1
}

model_scale can be a uniform scale number or [x, y, z]. When it is omitted, the legacy-compatible 1/12 is still used. The scale is applied uniformly to vertices, bones, rigid body shapes, and joint positions, so render and collision sizes stay consistent.

glTF uses the adjacent .gltf.json model manifest. For example character.glb corresponds to character.gltf.json:

{
  "model_scale": 1.3,
  "ragdoll": "example:ragdolls/character.json"
}

The manifest is the only automatic association entry point: the loader takes the model scale from it and the deployer takes the ragdoll profile from it; Java code never hardcodes selection logic on maribel, renko, or any bone name. A glTF without a ragdoll field still renders and plays animations normally, but a generic ragdoll deployment fails explicitly.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
• bodies: the body rigid body topology. In PMX, rigid_body and parent are PMX rigid body indices; in a glTF profile they are glTF node indices of the model that owns the manifest; the root node omits parent. The MMD adapter first walks the real bone tree to find the nearest registered physics ancestor; only when it finds no physics ancestor does it use parent to bridge separated PMX branches (for example the "upper body" and "lower body" branches that both sit under "waist").
  • include_secondary_bodies: PMX only, default false. When enabled, author-made rigid bodies and their joints that are not replaced by bodies and do not conflict with the main body bones enter the physics world as well, which suits the common bone-driven skirts and hair. It is not the same as PMX 2.1 per-vertex soft-body. Under a hybrid profile, secondary-motion bones keep the animated translation and write back only the physics rotation, so that hair strands and skirt bones are not stretched by the different reference frame of the main body capsules. An attachment point on the main body drives the secondary-motion chains one-way through a kinematic proxy that moves with the main body, using a separate 16-layer collision namespace, which stops a large number of secondary-motion rigid bodies from dragging the main body backward or bouncing off the generated capsules. The built-in TDA example uses 8 Box3D substeps; per-vertex soft-body currently only reads the format and is not yet connected to Box3D solving or vertex writeback.
  • role: pelvis, spine, chest, neck, head, shoulder, upper_arm, lower_arm, hand, upper_leg, lower_leg, foot, or toe.
  • Top-level limits: swing/twist limits can be declared per role instead of repeating them on every body; fields on the body itself take precedence.
  • The humanoid profile uses swing/twist limits by default: max_swing_degrees controls the cone swing, and min_twist_degrees / max_twist_degrees control the twist along the bone axis. limit_stiffness is a legacy profile compatibility field; Box3D manages the limit correction strength itself. The three angle fields must be provided together. When they are omitted, the humanoid defaults for the role apply.
  • rotation_min_degrees / rotation_max_degrees: the legacy three-axis Euler box limit compatibility path; they must appear together and cannot be mixed with the swing/twist fields.
  • simulation.hertz: the fixed world step frequency; a variable frame length is never used to solve directly.
  • simulation.update_mode: render_frame is advanced by an independent runtime and no longer depends on the model actually being drawn by the backend; manual is advanced by the caller through MinecraftRagdollRuntime.step(instance, dt) or instance.simulatePhysics(dt).
  • simulation.substeps: the number of solver substeps per fixed world step. For long multi-segment secondary-motion chains such as long hair and skirts, 8 is recommended; the built-in TDA configuration uses that value.
  • simulation.solver_iterations: legacy configuration compatibility field; Box3D does not expose this iteration count, so it is currently only validated and does not change the solve.
  • simulation.constraint_hertz / constraint_damping_ratio: joint constraint softening parameters.
  • simulation.max_linear_speed: mapped to the Box3D world maximum linear speed. max_angular_speed is a legacy configuration compatibility field; the current Box3D API has no corresponding world-level setting.
  • simulation.max_fixed_steps_per_update: the maximum number of catch-up fixed world steps in a single tick/frame update, default 12; backlog beyond the budget is dropped, which stops one stall from causing a sustained physics spiral.
  • sleeping.enabled: whether the whole group of rigid bodies sleeps. It is recommended to turn this off when debugging collisions or running sustained airborne simulation.
  • sleeping.linear_speed / angular_speed: scaled by each shape's size into a per-rigid-body farthest-point speed threshold for Box3D. delay_seconds is a legacy configuration compatibility field; the actual sleep delay is managed by Box3D itself.
  • collision.self_collision: whether the inside of one ragdoll collides with itself. false uses a Box3D negative group index; turning it off is recommended for a humanoid main body. When it is false, Box3D filters shape pairs inside the whole ragdoll, not just adjacent joints.
  • collision.continuous: whether to enable swept collision, to avoid penetration at high speed.
  • environment: the Minecraft block collision cache refresh frequency, boundary expansion, friction, and restitution.
  • initial_state: the optional overall initial offset and root rigid body velocity, mainly for demos or spawn effects.
  • dragging.enabled: register this instance for crosshair dragging.
  • dragging.mouse_button / max_distance: the mouse button (0 is the left button) and the maximum picking distance.
  • dragging.bias_rate: mapped to the spring hertz of the Box3D drag spherical joint. The remaining legacy drag tuning fields are still read for resource pack compatibility, but no extra Java stabilizer runs.

In game, aim the crosshair at the model's main body and hold the left button to drag it; after release the rigid bodies keep the velocity they had at the moment of release. Profile humanoid picking uses the capsules generated from the bones; the profile-less compatibility mode still uses PMX spheres, boxes, and capsules. What is grabbed is a local point on the hit surface; the whole skeleton is not teleported. The whole group of rigid bodies stays awake for as long as the mouse constraint exists, so gravity, joints, and collisions do not suddenly freeze mid-drag. Dragging applies a soft constraint only at the grab point of the hit rigid body and no longer applies extra linear or angular damping to the whole group. After the mouse is released, the rigid bodies only sleep normally once they touch the static environment and meet the low-speed threshold.

docs.title: Runtime deployment and removal
docs.text:
The client main thread can create instances dynamically through MinecraftRagdollDeployments. The model package must already have been scanned and published by models/model_proxy.json; while it is not yet published, deploy returns empty and you can retry after resource loading completes:

var request = new MinecraftRagdollDeployments.Request(
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("kasuga_lib", "models/pmx/test3.mmd.zip"),
        "TDA Bunny Miku 2.0.pmx",
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("example", "ragdoll/1"),
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("kasuga_lib", "ragdolls/tda_bunny_miku.json"),
        new Transform().translate(x, y, z),
        true
);
RagdollDeployment deployment = MinecraftRagdollDeployments.deploy(request).orElseThrow();

For glTF, prefer a manifest request rather than passing a hardcoded configuration path:

var request = new MinecraftRagdollDeployments.Request(
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("example", "models/character.glb"),
        ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("example", "ragdoll/1"),
        new Transform().translate(x, y, z),
        true
);
RagdollDeployment deployment = MinecraftRagdollDeployments.deploy(request).orElseThrow();

The handle exposes both instance() and ragdoll() for applying velocity or changing parameters at runtime. The two removal forms below are equivalent and can be called repeatedly:

deployment.remove();
MinecraftRagdollDeployments.remove(ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath("example", "ragdoll/1"));

ragdoll() exposes a stable runtime control interface: query rigid bodies with body(PMX rigid body index) and body(bone name), and call the impulse, force, torque, gravity scale, and drag APIs. lastFixedStepCount(), droppedSimulationTime(), selfContactCount(), staticContactBodyCount(), and sleepTime() are available for performance panels and collision/sleep diagnostics. The deployment handle also supports entity mounting: anchorTo(entity) hangs the nearest dynamic rigid body at the entity's eye position through a soft constraint, and detachAnchor() releases it; mouse dragging takes over the anchor automatically.

Removal takes the model out of the render backend and the pipeline instance table, unregisters mouse dragging, shuts down the block collision environment, and restores/releases the physics pose. removeAll() can be used for a level exit or for a caller that unloads everything at once.

Plain PMX and profile humanoids both use the four substeps Box3D recommends. The profile still handles bone capsules, semantic masses, physics bone writeback, and bind-pose follower tracking, but all physics constraints and the drag anchor are solved by Box3D.

docs.title: Model assembly and outfit cache API
docs.text:
Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.loaders.assembly. This interface accepts a generic Model from any source and composes geometry, materials, skeleton, morph, named animations and dynamics into a single Model. For the principles and ownership see model subsystems; for pose control see ModelPosing. For Minecraft's resource definitions, automatic invalidation and the instance swap entry point see outfit resources and switching.

Here a Mesh is a face definition. The assembly result is one Model and one Skeleton, handed to the existing backend to form geometry buffers; it does not pack the vertices of several faces into one Mesh, nor does it promise a single draw for different materials/passes.

docs.title: Minimal call
docs.text:
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.loaders.assembly.*;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.dynamic.ModelInstance;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.structure.material.MaterialSetInstance;

// The cache is owned by the clothing/model management service; do not create a new one every frame.
ModelAssemblyCache cache = new ModelAssemblyCache(32, 1_000_000);
ModelAssembly outfit = new ModelAssemblyBuilder("body", bodyModel, bodyRevision,
        body -> body.region("torso", 0, 1, 2).hideRegions("torso"))
        .part("shirt", shirtModel, shirtRevision)
        .part("coat", coatModel, coatRevision,
                coat -> coat.mapBone("coat_root", "root"))
        .assemble(cache);

var model = outfit.model();
ModelInstance instance = new ModelInstance(model, null, null, null,
        new MaterialSetInstance(model.getMaterialSet()), null);
instance.getPosing().play("walk", true);       // body clip names are kept
instance.getPosing().play("shirt/fit", false); // clothing clip names get a part prefix

Source models must already be fully loaded and use the same bind space/units. For shared bones, the difference between the source and target absolute bind matrices must not exceed bindTolerance; the default is 1e-4, compared per matrix component. Assembly does not automatically scale clothing, fit the body or retarget animations from a different skeleton. Shared bones use the body hierarchy; bones unique to the clothing keep their original absolute bind pose. All default mappings and geometry clones run on a cache miss; each frame only updates the pose of the merged instance.

docs.title: ModelAssemblyBuilder
docs.text:
new ModelAssemblyBuilder(String bodyId, Model body, long revision);
new ModelAssemblyBuilder(String bodyId, Model body, long revision,
                         Consumer<ModelAssemblyBuilder.PartBuilder> configure);

The first part is the body. revision is the resource version managed by the caller, and any long is allowed; after modifying a resource in place you must update the revision or call the cache invalidation interface. Source Models are distinguished by object identity; the format type is not read, and no content hash of the whole resource is computed.

Method Behavior ModelAssemblyBuilder part(String id, Model model, long revision) Appends a part in order; by default matches same-named body bones and keeps dynamics ModelAssemblyBuilder part(String id, Model model, long revision, Consumer<PartBuilder> configure) Appends after configuring mappings, hidden regions and dynamics integration ModelAssemblyBuilder bindTolerance(float tolerance) Finite positive number, default 1e-4 ModelAssembly.Request build() Copies and validates the request; creates no geometry or GPU resources ModelAssembly assemble() Assembles directly with the standard assembler, without the cache ModelAssembly assemble(ModelAssemblyCache cache) Builds the request and fetches the cache result

A part id must be non-empty, must not be all whitespace and must not repeat. The body cannot have bone aliases set. The configure callback runs synchronously; the request stores its result, not the callback. Part order affects material indices and render order, so it is part of the cache key.

docs.title: PartBuilder
docs.text:
Method Behavior PartBuilder mapBone(String source, String target) Source bone name to output bone name; the source bone is resolved immediately, the target is validated at assembly time PartBuilder mapBone(Bone source, String target) Uses a source Bone reference, which must belong to that source model PartBuilder matchBodyBones(boolean enabled) Default true; matches same-named body bones when there is no explicit mapping PartBuilder includeDynamics(boolean enabled) Default true; false excludes that part's inheritance, fixed axes, IK/closures and physics definitions PartBuilder hideMeshes(int... indices) Removes faces by index into the source Model's Mesh array PartBuilder region(String name, int... indices) Defines a named region inside this part; the same name replaces it PartBuilder hideRegions(String... names) Hides those regions; expanded into face indices when the Part is constructed

Explicit mappings take precedence over automatic same-name matching; a target may be a body bone or a bone already introduced by an earlier part, and may not reference a later part. Unmapped part bones are named partId/sourceName; bones without a name use bone_<source index>. New bones keep the source absolute bind matrix, and their local bind is recomputed relative to the already-mapped parent bone; an independent root is attached under the body root. Output bone name conflicts, invalid mappings, incompatible binds or a cycle in the source hierarchy throw IllegalArgumentException.

Hidden indices must be within the source Mesh array's range; an unknown region is an error. Only vertices used solely by hidden faces and their morphs are removed; shared vertices are kept; hiding geometry does not automatically remove bones or physics. Regions are supplied by the integrating party; occlusion is not guessed automatically. Pure triangles and quads can be combined into MIXED and handled by the existing backend; lines and surfaces must be assembled separately.

docs.title: ModelAssembly and reference remapping
docs.text:
Model ModelAssembly.model();
ModelAssembly.Request ModelAssembly.request();
Map<String, ModelAssembly.Remap> ModelAssembly.parts();
ModelAssembly.Remap ModelAssembly.part(String id);

new ModelAssembly.Source(Model model, long revision);
new ModelAssembly.Part(String id, ModelAssembly.Source source, Map<Bone, String> boneMappings,
                       Set<Integer> hiddenMeshes, boolean matchBodyBones, boolean includeDynamics);
new ModelAssembly.Request(List<ModelAssembly.Part> parts, float bindTolerance);
new ModelAssembly.PartMorphId(String part, Object original);

The result mappings and the request's collections are unmodifiable, and an unknown part id is an error. The body keeps its original morph/clip/anchor names; part morph identities are PartMorphId, avoiding identity collisions caused by string concatenation; clips and anchors use partId/name.

The complete set of Remap methods:

Method Return value/behavior String id(), Model source() Source part identity and the shared Model Bone bone(Bone source) Output bone reference; an unknown source is an error Vertex vertex(Vertex source), Mesh mesh(Mesh source) Output elements; null when hidden or unused Material material(Material source) Output material; an unknown source is an error Object morphId(Object source) Body original identity or the part's PartMorphId String boneName(String source) Output name of a source bone name; unknown names are kept String ikName(String source) Output chain name; the same shared chain may reuse the body name String animationName(String source), String anchorName(String source) Output names int rigidBodyIndex(int sourceIndex) Index from the source physics table to the output table; -1 when the part excludes dynamics Pose pose(Pose source) Converts bone name, morph, IK and material frame references <T> AnimationSampler<T> sampler(AnimationSampler<T> source) Wraps the sampler, preserving duration, original interpolation and formula Namespace MorphType<?, ?, ?> morph(MorphType<?, ?, ?> source) Copies a morph for the assembly extension; returns null for a hidden target 
Object fit = outfit.part("shirt").morphId("fit");
instance.getMorph().activateMorph(fit, 0.8f);
int clothBody = outfit.part("coat").rigidBodyIndex(2);

Vertex, UV, normal, Mesh, Bone, Material and Sprite/SpriteSet definitions are copied separately.
