docs.title: Skeleton Dynamics API Reference
docs.text: This page covers the generic skeleton dynamics interfaces in render-core. Data conversion happens at the model construction stage; at runtime, instances are controlled by IK chain name. Algorithms and ownership are documented in the concept document. The underlying world, forces, collision, active ragdoll, and Minecraft integration are covered in Physics API; format manifest/profile are covered in MMD/glTF configuration.

docs.title: Types and Packages
Lifecycle and Units
docs.text:
1. Load the Model; the configureSkeleton(Skeleton) hook of format metadata runs during Model construction.
  2. Create a dynamics Builder from the Skeleton, append or override definitions, then attach().
  3. Create a ModelInstance; set targets, tick loop modules, and physics.
  4. Evaluate through the instance's pose pipeline; on disposal, close the ModelInstance or detach physics.

Dynamics configuration should be completed before creating instances. The collections in shared definitions are immutable, and both vector constructor arguments and vector accessor results are copied, but Bone is a structural reference, and its definition transform cannot be modified as an instance pose. Multiple instances each keep their own targets and solver corrections.

Data Unit/coordinates RigidBody.position, Joint.position, shape sizes, and translation ranges definition coordinates; the physics adaptation multiplies by Physics.unitScale RigidBody.rotation, Joint.rotation, and rotation ranges XYZ Euler, radians IK angles, maxRotationStep, Rotor, Hinge radians IK tolerance distance units in the current evaluation space; import/root scaling affects the actual corresponding scale Targets of setIkTarget, setFrameIkTarget, IkTargetModule world coordinates, Vector3f; with floating origin enabled, the double world anchor is subtracted at evaluation time SkeletonRagdoll.Body.position() and ordinary physics queries simulation-local coordinates; use the worldPosition/*World interfaces to obtain or supply world coordinates

A float external target is already precision-limited by itself; floating origin does not restore world-coordinate fractions lost when the Vector3f was constructed.

docs.title: Skeleton and SkeletonDynamics
docs.text:
SkeletonDynamics Skeleton.getDynamics();
void Skeleton.setDynamics(SkeletonDynamics dynamics);

new SkeletonDynamics(Physics physics, List<IkChain> ikChains,
                     List<DiamondConstraint> diamonds);
new SkeletonDynamics(Physics physics, List<IkChain> ikChains,
                     List<DiamondConstraint> diamonds, List<BonePoseConstraint> poseConstraints);

Skeleton uses SkeletonDynamics.EMPTY by default. It is usually mounted through a Builder after validation; direct construction and the setter do not perform all bone ownership, chain hierarchy, joint reference, and closure validation.

Accessor Returns physics() the shared physics definition poseConstraints() unmodifiable map from target Bone to inheritance/fixed-axis constraints; empty by default with the three-argument constructor ikChains() IK chain list preserving definition order diamonds() diamond closure constraint list chainsByName() read-only Map<String, IkChain>; chain names must be unique ikChainsByBone() read-only Map<Bone, List<IkChain>>; reverse mapping from a driver bone to all chains that control it

docs.title: SkeletonDynamicsBuilder
docs.text:
new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(Skeleton skeleton);

Construction copies the definitions already mounted on the Skeleton into the Builder; it does not automatically clear the original rig.

Full method Behavior Skeleton skeleton() current target skeleton Bone bone(String name) resolves a structural reference by bone name; unknown names throw IllegalArgumentException <T> SkeletonDynamicsBuilder read(T source, SkeletonDynamicsReader<? super T> reader) runs the Reader synchronously, returns this Builder SkeletonDynamicsBuilder physics(Physics definition) replaces the whole physics definition, preserving IK/closure SkeletonDynamicsBuilder physics(List<RigidBody> bodies, List<Joint> joints) replaces bodies/joints; unit scaling, no required profile, affine writeback, radius scale 1, no bind-pose followers SkeletonDynamicsBuilder ik(IkChain chain) adds a chain; the same chain name replaces the existing chain SkeletonDynamicsBuilder diamond(DiamondConstraint diamond) adds a constraint; the same constraint name replaces the existing constraint SkeletonDynamicsBuilder pose(BonePoseConstraint constraint) adds a bone pose constraint; the same target Bone replaces the existing constraint SkeletonDynamics build() validates and returns the definition; does not mount, create a solver, or create a native world SkeletonDynamics attach() calls build() first, then writes into the Skeleton and returns the mounted definition

The structural validation performed by build()/attach() includes:

  • Non-null body bones, bind-pose followers, and IK controller/effector/link all belong to the target Skeleton.
  • A pose constraint's target and inheritance source both belong to this Skeleton; self-references and inheritance cycles are rejected.
  • A joint's two rigid body indices are valid and different; the indices refer to Physics.bodies(), not Bone.index.
  • The IK chain is non-empty, driver bones do not repeat, and each subsequent link/effector must be a descendant of the previous link; intermediate bones may be skipped.
  • A diamond closure references two existing POSITION chains; the same chain cannot belong to multiple closures.
  • Closure branches do not share driver bones, their endpoints differ, the bind positions of the branch bases are no farther apart than the closure tolerance, and one branch's driver bone cannot be an ancestor of the other base.

Illegal structures throw IllegalArgumentException. Null required arguments usually throw NullPointerException.

docs.title: Reader and Existing SkeletonBuilder
docs.text:
@FunctionalInterface
public interface SkeletonDynamicsReader<T> {
    void read(T source, SkeletonDynamicsBuilder builder);
}

The Reader only fills generic definitions into the Builder; it does not attach() by itself. External formats may use any source type:

Skeleton skeleton = model.getSkeleton();
SkeletonDynamicsReader<String> reader = (chainName, builder) -> builder.ik(
        new IkChain(chainName, builder.bone("hand-target"), builder.bone("hand"),
                List.of(new IkLink(builder.bone("upper-arm")),
                        new IkLink(builder.bone("forearm")))));

new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(skeleton).read("left-arm", reader).attach();

The existing SkeletonBuilder provides:

SkeletonBuilder dynamics(Consumer<SkeletonDynamicsBuilder> configure);

The callback runs after the skeleton's build(...) completes Bone/Anchor/Vertex binding, and automatically validates and mounts. Repeated calls to dynamics(...) replace the configuration callback; clear() removes it as well. A custom ModelData may override void configureSkeleton(Skeleton skeleton), hooking up a Reader during Model construction. The Model construction hook of format metadata runs after the SkeletonBuilder callback and may override the physics table or same-named chains; configuration that needs to override format defaults should go after Model loading and before ModelInstance creation.

docs.title: Generic Bone Pose Constraints
docs.text:
new TransformInheritance(Bone source, float weight, boolean translation, boolean rotation);
new BonePoseConstraint(Bone bone, TransformInheritance inheritance, Vector3f fixedAxis);

Both are public records under SkeletonDynamics; they do not require a BoneData type. The inheritance weight must be finite and may be negative; at least one of translation or rotation must be enabled. The inheritance source provides the currently evaluated local pose delta, translation is multiplied by weight, and rotation is slerped from the identity quaternion by weight; it does not inherit the source's bind pose or world position. The target bone's original local pose applies inheritance first, then extracts the twist along fixedAxis, and then applies IK and physics overrides. The fixed axis is in the target bone's local coordinates; the input vector is copied and normalized, and is rejected when its squared length is less than 1e-8. The physics override takes the final simulated pose as authoritative; this axis constraint does not replace physics joint limits.

inheritance or fixedAxis may be null, but not both. fixedAxis() returns a copy; hasFixedAxis() queries whether an axis is defined, and fixedAxis(Vector3f destination) copies into the caller's scratch when an axis is defined. The Builder validates skeleton ownership and inheritance cycles by bone reference. Instances are evaluated in dependency order; cross-branch inheritance does not depend on hierarchy traversal order, and the update range is widened to cover affected vertices.

PMX/PMD bone inheritance and fixed axes are converted in MmdSkeletonDynamicsReader.read; when reading a PMX bone table alone, you can also call MmdSkeletonDynamicsReader.readBoneConstraints(builder) and readIk(builder). Index references of format files exist only in the Reader layer; MC or external formats just fill these definitions through the same Builder.

docs.title: Physics
docs.text:
new Physics(List<RigidBody> bodies, List<Joint> joints, Vector3f unitScale,
            boolean profileRequired, boolean affineWriteback,
            float profileRadiusScale, Set<Bone> bindPoseFollowers);
Parameter Contract bodies, joints copied definition lists; profile/joints reference the list indices of bodies unitScale three finite positive components; used for rigid body position/size and joint translation profileRequired when true, this table cannot be enabled directly without a profile; used for candidate tables affineWriteback when true, computes the local physics transform inversely within the full affine parent hierarchy, preserving scale/shear profileRadiusScale finite positive number; radius scale of generated profile capsules bindPoseFollowers follower bones without a direct physics body; they can follow the bind-to-current affine delta of the nearest physics ancestor

Physics.EMPTY: empty tables, unitScale=(1,1,1), profileRequired=false, affineWriteback=true, profileRadiusScale=1, empty follower set.

docs.title: RigidBody
docs.text:
new RigidBody(String name, String alias, Bone bone, int collisionGroup,
              int nonCollisionMask, int shape, Vector3f size, Vector3f position,
              Vector3f rotation, float mass, float linearDamping,
              float angularDamping, float restitution, float friction, int mode);
Parameter Contract name, alias non-null display/auxiliary names; they are not required to be bone names; alias may be an empty string bone may be null, meaning a body not bound to a bone; when non-null it must belong to the Skeleton collisionGroup integer 0..63 nonCollisionMask integer filter mask; the physics adaptation preserves exclusion layer semantics shape SPHERE=0, BOX=1, CAPSULE=2 size finite non-negative vector; spheres use the x radius, boxes use xyz half-extents, capsules use x radius / full height of the y cylinder segment position, rotation body position in definition coordinates and XYZ Euler orientation; both finite mass finite non-negative mass; 0 produces no dynamic inverse mass linearDamping, angularDamping finite non-negative damping restitution, friction finite non-negative material parameters mode the motion/writeback mode in the table below Constant Value Runtime behavior KINEMATIC 0 rigid body driven by animation targets DYNAMIC 1 physics writes back the full pose DYNAMIC_ROTATION 2 dynamic body; writes back only the bone rotation, preserving animation translation

Definition construction allows non-negative sizes; when collision shapes are actually created, sphere/capsule radii and all three box half-extents must be positive. Creating physics bodies may therefore reject degenerate shapes further.

docs.title: Joint
docs.text:
new Joint(String name, String alias, int rigidBodyA, int rigidBodyB,
          Vector3f position, Vector3f rotation, Vector3f positionMin,
          Vector3f positionMax, Vector3f rotationMin, Vector3f rotationMax,
          Vector3f positionSpring, Vector3f rotationSpring);

name/alias are non-null, and all vectors are finite and copied. rigidBodyA/B must be valid and different during Builder validation. position/rotation is the shared joint frame, *Min/*Max are the author limits, and *Spring are the author spring parameters. The current model adapter maps this set of six-axis author parameters to a Box3D spherical cone/twist; translation is tightened to a fixed anchor. Other native joints are created through the Physics API and are not selected by this record's type field.

docs.title: Physics Example Without Format Metadata
docs.text:
var builder = new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(model.getSkeleton());
var body = new RigidBody("torso-body", "", builder.bone("torso"),
        0, 0, RigidBody.BOX, new Vector3f(0.2f, 0.3f, 0.1f),
        new Vector3f(0, 1, 0), new Vector3f(),
        2f, 0.05f, 0.1f, 0f, 0.6f, RigidBody.DYNAMIC);
builder.physics(List.of(body), List.of()).attach();

var instance = new ModelInstance(model, null, null, null, null, null);
var ragdoll = instance.enablePhysics();
if (ragdoll != null) {
    ragdoll.setGravity(new Vector3f(0, -9.80665f, 0));
    // Called once per frame by the host; instances already wired into the Minecraft runtime are advanced by that runtime.
    instance.evaluatePhysicsFrame(0f, 1f / 60f);
}
// On lifecycle end: instance.detachPhysics() or instance.close().

The high-level enablePhysics returns null when the native library is unavailable; it throws IllegalArgumentException when the library is available but bodies are empty, or when profileRequired=true and no profile is passed. Body.source() returns this generic RigidBody, and Joint.source() returns this generic Joint.

docs.title: IkLink, RotationLimit, and IkJoint
docs.text:
new IkLink(Bone bone);
new IkLink(Bone bone, RotationLimit limit);
new IkLink(Bone bone, RotationLimit limit, IkJoint joint);
new RotationLimit(Vector3f minimum, Vector3f maximum);
new Rotor(float angle);
new Hinge(Vector3f axis, Vector3f reference, float minimum, float maximum);
Type Parameters and behavior IkLink bone required; limit/joint may be null; the omitted fields of the two simplified constructors are null RotationLimit finite XYZ Euler lower/upper bounds, per-axis minimum ≤ maximum; applies to the IK local correction IkJoint sealed interface, permits Rotor and Hinge Rotor finite angle 0..π; the first segment revolves around the uncorrected pose direction, later segments are relative to the previous segment's direction Hinge axis/reference are in the driver's uncorrected local frame; non-zero, automatically normalized, orthogonality error ≤ 1e-4; angle in [-π,π] and minimum ≤ maximum

Rotor/Hinge constrain position solving in Caliko; RotationLimit projects onto the local correction. When both are given, both restrictions participate, but Euler box projection does not guarantee global convergence for complex constraints. Chains that have already reached the target do not choose another solution.

docs.title: IkChain
docs.text:
new IkChain(String name, Bone controller, Bone effector, List<IkLink> links);
new IkChain(String name, Bone controller, Bone effector, List<IkLink> links,
            int iterations, float tolerance, float maxRotationStep,
            boolean replaceAuthoredRotation, TargetMode targetMode);
Parameter Simplified-construct default Contract name required non-blank chain name; control and diagnostics address it by this name, and it is not required to equal the controller bone name controller required default target source bone effector required final effector bone links required non-empty, from base to tip; the final link points to the effector iterations 32 1..256; caps the adaptation iterations and the library's attempt count tolerance 1e-4f finite positive distance maxRotationStep π finite non-negative value, the maximum angle of each direction-alignment increment; 0 limits that increment to zero, and subsequent Euler projection can still adjust the correction replaceAuthoredRotation false true takes over the chain bones' authored local pose; the current implementation starts from the identity local transform and skips even authored translation/scale, while morph/grant/fixed-axis still participate afterwards targetMode POSITION non-null; modes below

POSITION uses the controller's current absolute position as the default target. DIRECTION determines orientation from the bind bone-segment direction and the controller's rotation difference when there is no external target, ignoring its pure translation. When a persistent or single-tick external target exists, it switches to position blending; this mode does not interpret the external Vector3f as a direction vector.

var builder = new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(model.getSkeleton());
var elbow = new Hinge(new Vector3f(0, 0, 1), new Vector3f(1, 0, 0),
        -(float) Math.PI / 2f, 0f);
builder.ik(new IkChain("left-arm", builder.bone("hand-target"), builder.bone("hand"),
        List.of(new IkLink(builder.bone("upper-arm")),
                new IkLink(builder.bone("forearm"), null, elbow)))).attach();

This hinge example assumes the forearm's bind direction is local +X and the bend axis is +Z; real assets need to fill in their own bone frame.

docs.title: Diamond Closure
docs.text:
new DiamondConstraint(String name, String firstChain, String secondChain);
new DiamondConstraint(String name, String firstChain, String secondChain,
                      int iterations, float tolerance);

The simplified constructor uses iterations=32 and tolerance=1e-4f. The name is non-blank, the two chain names are required and different, iterations is 1..256, and tolerance is a finite positive number. Branch requirements are validated by the Builder, see its structural validation list.

var builder = new SkeletonDynamicsBuilder(model.getSkeleton());
var left = new IkChain("left-linkage", builder.bone("closure-target"), builder.bone("left-tip"),
        List.of(new IkLink(builder.bone("left-base")), new IkLink(builder.bone("left-mid"))));
var right = new IkChain("right-linkage", builder.bone("closure-target"), builder.bone("right-tip"),
        List.of(new IkLink(builder.bone("right-base")), new IkLink(builder.bone("right-mid"))));
builder.ik(left).ik(right)
        .diamond(new DiamondConstraint("linkage", left.name(), right.name()))
        .attach();

The two bases should coincide at the bind pose position and drive separate hierarchies; the two endpoints represent the same closure point. The two controllers may be the same bone or have separate targets; solving starts from the midpoint of the two targets. Disabling either chain pauses the closure; when branches belong to a closure they are not first solved as independent chains. The constraint only guarantees position closure; it does not guarantee equal endpoint orientation, equal side lengths, or native mechanical feedback.

docs.title: SkeletonInstance Runtime Control
docs.text:
var skeleton = instance.getSkeletonInstance();

In the table below, name always denotes an IK chain name. The existing parameter names boneName/controllerBone are historical.

Method signature Returns/Behavior boolean setIkEnabled(String name, boolean enabled) returns false for an undefined chain; on success requires re-evaluation boolean isIkEnabled(String name) reads the toggle, default true; not an existence check, unknown chains also return true void resetIkEnabled() clears overrides, restoring the default true boolean clearIkEnabled(String name) clears an individual chain's explicit toggle; returns true when state was removed boolean setIkTarget(String name, Vector3f worldTarget, float weight) persistent target; false for an undefined chain; copies the target and requires an update boolean clearIkTarget(String name) clears the persistent target; returns false when there is no target void clearIkTargets() clears all persistent targets boolean setFrameIkTarget(String name, Vector3f worldTarget, float weight) transient target for the current pose pipeline cycle; false for an undefined chain void clearFrameIkTargets() clears transient targets; ModelTickLoop calls it automatically at the start of a cycle void updateTransform() evaluates hierarchy, IK, and final hierarchy; manual hosts call it according to their own evaluation order void updateTransformAfterPhysics() rebuilds the hierarchy after writeback, preserving solved IK corrections without solving IK again Map<String, CalikoIkSolver.SolveResult> ikSolveResults() read-only diagnostic view of the most recent IK solve

Targets must be non-null and finite, and weight must be finite and within [0,1]; otherwise the corresponding argument exception is thrown. Blending runs from the controller's current position to the external position; weight is not "the strength of enabling IK". Transient targets take precedence over persistent targets; unknown chains return false before the target value is validated. Setting a target only marks the input as changed; it does not solve immediately. Afterwards run the instance's normal evaluation entry point.

var skeleton = instance.getSkeletonInstance();
boolean accepted = skeleton.setIkTarget("left-arm", new Vector3f(1, 2, 0), 1f);
instance.updateImmediate();
var result = skeleton.ikSolveResults().get("left-arm");

The accessors of SolveResult(float residual, boolean satisfied) are residual() and satisfied(). For an ordinary chain, residual is the distance from the actual endpoint to this target; for a closure, it is the larger of the two endpoint distance and the two base distance. Closure branch results correspond to the most recent shared target and do not mean that the branch's original controller target was necessarily reached. satisfied only expresses that the corresponding position residual is within tolerance; it is not a complete angular/dynamics acceptance. Disabled or unrun chains have no result for that solve; the Map is a live read-only view that is cleared and updated on the next solve; copy it yourself if you need to keep a snapshot.

docs.title: Per-Tick Targets: IkTargetModule
docs.text:
new IkTargetModule(String name, Vector3f worldTarget);
new IkTargetModule(String name, Vector3f worldTarget, float weight);

The two-argument constructor uses weight 1 and initial enabled true. Accessors: controllerBone() (chain name), target() (copied vector), weight(), enabled(). Control methods: void setTarget(Vector3f), void setTarget(Vector3f,float), void setEnabled(boolean). Setting the target preserves the enabled state; the one-argument setter preserves the current weight.

var target = new lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.dynamic.tick_loop.handler.IkTargetModule(
        "left-arm", new Vector3f(1, 2, 0));
instance.getTickLoop().addPreIk("hand-target-input", target);
target.setTarget(new Vector3f(1.2f, 2, 0), 0.6f);
target.setEnabled(false);

The constructor only validates that the name is non-blank and the target values; it does not verify that the chain exists. Chain names are resolved only when the module is published to an instance at runtime. addPreIk places the module before IK and after the default apply; transient targets are consumed by both IK and physics within the same cycle. When you need to write pending transforms for the default apply to consume, use the tick pipeline's addBefore(SLOT_APPLY, ...).

docs.title: Actual Default Behavior of Format Readers
docs.text:
Reader Read interface Default mapping MmdSkeletonDynamicsReader void read(MmdModelData, SkeletonDynamicsBuilder) authored rigid body order, direct Bone references, valid joints, imported unitScale; no required profile, rigid writeback, profile radius scale 1 same as above static void readIk(SkeletonDynamicsBuilder) converts only PMX IK already attached to bones; usable for skeletons without a full tail same as above static void readBoneConstraints(SkeletonDynamicsBuilder) converts PMX inheritance/fixed axes into generic constraints; the full read calls it automatically GltfSkeletonDynamicsReader void read(GltfModelData, SkeletonDynamicsBuilder) generates candidates in node order; requires an explicit profile, affine writeback, skin bone bind followers; does not guess/create IK automatically

MMD uses the controller bone name as the chain name, and reverses chains from the file's tip-to-base to base-to-tip; positive iteration counts are capped at 256, tolerance is 1e-4f, the step angle takes the absolute value of the original limit, and authored local pose takeover is enabled. Expressible single-axis Euler limits are converted to Hinge; other box limits keep RotationLimit. DIRECTION is used when there is a single link, the controller/effector bind positions coincide, and the controller has a vector tail. Chains without a valid effector/link or with a non-positive iteration count do not enter the definition. Invalid or self-connected PMX joints do not enter the simulatable table.

The external indices of glTF profiles continue to correspond to node order; MMD profiles correspond to the original rigid body order. Both sources complete conversion at the Reader boundary, so at runtime Body.source().bone() directly yields a generic bone reference.

docs.title: Solver Adaptation for Custom Hosts
docs.text:
CalikoIkSolver(Skeleton skeleton, PoseAccess pose) provides void solve() and Map<String, SolveResult> results(). It is usually managed by SkeletonInstance; when used directly, the host implements:

PoseAccess method Host responsibility Transform absolute(Bone bone) the evaluated absolute pose Transform correction(Bone bone) mutable per-instance local IK correction Vector3f target(IkChain chain) returns a new vector for this target; closures modify the returned value to solve for the shared target boolean enabled(String chain) chain toggle void refresh(Bone driver, Bone endpoint) after correction, synchronously rebuild the affected hierarchy; subsequent reads must see the latest pose

The host is responsible for animation/physics evaluation order, correction cleanup, and thread ownership. The solver has mutable state and cannot solve the same instance concurrently. The current library is the official Caliko 1.3.8 core; dependency notes and licenses are included under modules/render-core/libs.

docs.title: Source Entry Points
docs.text:
The classes for this page are all in the render-core module; see the "Types and Packages" table for package paths:

  • SkeletonDynamics
  • SkeletonDynamicsBuilder
  • SkeletonDynamicsReader
  • SkeletonInstance
  • CalikoIkSolver

docs.title: UI model previews
docs.text:
GuiModelPreview displays a model published by the existing model loader. Resource locations and optional MMD entry names follow the normal registration contract. Each preview owns a local ModelInstance, material state, GPU buffers and transparent depth canvas. It does not mount its instance in the world backend or change an existing world's model pose.

var preview = new GuiModelPreview(
        ResourceLocation.parse("kasuga_lib:models/gltf/maribel.glb"), null);
preview.setView(-0.55f, 0.25f, 1f); // yaw / pitch in radians; positive zoom

render returns false while the asset is unavailable, allowing the host to draw a placeholder. It resolves the current publication on each draw and releases the old private instance when the asset changes. Default framing fits the model's bounds; zooming in can intentionally crop it. An alternative constructor accepts a Supplier<Model> that lends an asset or returns null.

Toolkit Control Ownership Vanilla ModelPreviewWidget(x, y, width, height, preview) The owning Screen calls close() from removed() LDLib2 ModelPreviewElement(preview) Removal closes the preview; supports normal ModularUI and world panels LDLib2 Compose ModelPreview(modelLocation, modelName, ...) Removal or an asset-key change releases the preview; see the Compose adapter ModernUI ModelPreviewView(context, modelLocation, modelName) Uses the public MinecraftSurfaceView renderer; detach schedules cleanup on Minecraft's render thread

Toolkit adapters live separately in external/uip/ldlib and external/uip/modernui. The shared renderer depends on neither toolkit. Give each owning control its own preview.

For custom hosts use preview.render(graphics, x, y, width, height, partialTick); an overload accepts opacity in [0,1]. Rendering, instance access and closing belong to the Minecraft render thread; setView may be called by UI input threads. currentFrame() lends a read-only color frame, valid until the next draw, resize or close; never delete its texture or framebuffer. instance() allows the caller to pose the local model. The preview does not drive world physics or global scheduling.

The native preview material path supports depth, skinning and model textures independently of Iris world passes. Verified on macOS arm64, MC 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.203, LDLib2 2.2.1 and ModernUI 3.13.0.1. Windows, Linux and Iris combinations have not been exercised.

docs.title: Development demos
docs.text:
./gradlew :external:uip:ldlib:runClientModelDemo -PkasugaModelToolkit=vanilla
./gradlew :external:uip:ldlib:runClientModelDemo -PkasugaModelToolkit=ldlib
# Place an isolated world in this module's run/model-demo/saves first.
./gradlew :external:uip:ldlib:runClientModelDemo -PkasugaModelToolkit=world -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=YourTestWorld
./gradlew :external:uip:modernui:runClientModelDemo

Add -PkasugaModelCapture=/absolute/path/model.png to run the smoke, capture and exit. Inspect passed in the adjacent model-report.json: a failed client assertion can still yield a successful Gradle exit. Vanilla/LDLib2 check actual model pixels, rotation, repeated GUI resizing, current attachment dimensions/completeness and close cleanup. :modules:modelling:renderGlTest checks color/FBO/depth retirement immediately after resize, before later allocations can reuse their OpenGL names. A delayed glIsTexture(oldId) query cannot identify the original object. ModernUI checks its real render callback and detach cleanup. Demo classes stay out of release jars.

docs.title: UML rendering framework and backend interfaces
docs.text:
Interface, configuration, and call reference. For the principles see uml-render-framework.md.

models.uml.framework defines the public capabilities extracted from existing rendering implementations. It does not depend on Minecraft, Iris, or LWJGL; model structures and JOML math types remain public data types. uml.bridge and uml.backend handle adaptation and default implementations and are no longer the only entry point for all capabilities. MC, OpenGL, and platform upload strategies stay in concrete implementations.

docs.title: Layers and responsibilities
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Pipeline[ModelPipeLine / host render callback] --> Schedule[framework.schedule.RenderScheduler]
    Pipeline --> Backend[framework.render.RenderBackend]
    Backend --> Context[framework.render.RenderContext]
    Context --> Factory[framework.render.RenderableFactory]
    Factory --> Geometry[framework.render.ModelGeometryAdapter]
    Context --> Buffers[framework.buffer]
    MC[MCBackend / MCBridge / IVertexBuffer] -.implements or adapts.-> Backend
    MC -.implements or adapts.-> Geometry
    GL[MappedBuffer / GpuUploadRing / GL Device] -.implements.-> Buffers
Layer Interface/implementation Responsibilities framework.schedule RenderScheduler<I>, DefaultRenderScheduler<I> Per-instance visibility policy, host frame marks, render distance limit, unmount cleanup framework.schedule FrameSampleCache<I> Deduplicates identity sampling across camera views/material passes within a shared frame token framework.render ModelGeometryAdapter Vertex/mesh conversion, skeleton binding selection; does not own scheduling or drawing framework.render RenderableFactory<R> Creates render resources for one instance, receives explicitly provided backend services framework.render RenderContext<R,Q,E> Resource cache for one mount, hard visibility switch, host transform/lighting metadata, release framework.render RenderBackend<A,C,Q> Mount registry, context creation, draw submission, replacement and unmount, backend shutdown framework.buffer TypedBuffer<T> Fixed-capacity CPU element read/write, partial/full updates, borrowed byte view framework.buffer UploadBuffer, UploadDevice Full snapshot upload, dirty element ranges, in-flight read protection; device calls and state restoration framework.buffer RenderBuffer<D,S> Geometry upload, update, draw, and markSubmitted after every consumption uml.bridge Bridge<R> Combines geometry conversion with the legacy resource creation entry point, compatible with the old pipeline uml.backend Backend, BackendContext Default lifecycle implementation of registry and context mc / uml.backend.gpu MC renderer, OpenGL buffer/device Vanilla frustum/lighting, shader, VAO/VBO/TBO, Iris, and platform policies

docs.title: The boundary between Bridge and Backend
docs.text:
Bridge provides the model conversion rules. The backend owns services such as the executor, chooses the context type and passes those services explicitly to the resource factory. The current MC main path is:

MCBackend.add(key, bridge, instance)
  → MCBackend.createContext(bridge, instance)
  → MCRenderableContext(bridge, instance, factory)
  → factory: bridge.createRenderable(instance, backend.executor)

This path does not require Bridge to look up the executor from the string mc_backend. Bridge.getBackendContext, setBackends/getBackends, and the single-argument createRenderable/apply are kept as compatibility entry points for old calls; the default Backend.createContext can still call the old factory. New backends should override createContext and return a type-matching context directly. Do not let the geometry adapter close the executor, manage frame marks, or handle the draw pipeline.

Q is the host frame context, E is pre-render metadata, R is the mount resource; none of them substitutes for another. BackendContext does not allocate R at construction; the first apply creates and caches it. The default Backend.add calls apply up front, so the mount is published only after resources are prepared successfully. beforeRender(Q) reads metadata; it does not sample animation and does not create buffers. Animation sampling, version updates, morph, and upload are done by the rendering implementation and cannot be achieved by rebuilding the context over and over.

docs.title: Mount and release rules
docs.text:
• The registry matches mounts by the caller's key; key, adapter, instance, context, and resources must not be null.
  • Replacing the same key prepares the new context first. If preparation fails, the unpublished context is closed and the old mount is kept; on success the new mount is published and the old context is closed. A failure to release the old resources reports an exception, and the new mount is already in effect at that point.
  • getRenderingObjects is a read-only view; mount changes must go through add/remove.
  • remove first removes from the registry, then releases resources; release exceptions are visible and are not silently ignored.
  • A context owns only the render resources returned by the factory; it does not own the ModelInstance, the Bridge, or the shared executor. close is idempotent; after closing, apply throws, and resources of an unmounted instance cannot be reallocated.
  • On shutdown the Backend tries to release all mounts and aggregates release exceptions; after shutdown it rejects new mounts and submissions. The MC Backend then releases batching/translucent resources and stops the executor.
  • Mounts, buffer operations, and drawing are held by the render thread; the scheduler independently synchronizes tick/render access.

docs.title: Scheduling rules
docs.text:
The framework modes are ALWAYS, MANUAL, HOST_RENDERER. MC's VANILLA_RENDERER maps to HOST_RENDERER; the old static ModelRenderScheduler only forwards to ModelRenderScheduling.scheduler(). ModelPipeLine and MCBackend use the same framework scheduling domain. Other backends may create an independent DefaultRenderScheduler.

Instances are distinguished by object identity. Switching modes keeps the per-instance render distance limit; setVisible selects MANUAL. Render distance uses host world units; a non-positive value disables the distance gate, and NaN/Infinity are rejected. shouldRender answers the policy result only; the distance and frustum checks are performed by the backend in order. Culled instances are not sampled and not uploaded; physics stepping continues to be managed by the independent runtime.

The host renderer calls markRenderedThisFrame within its own visible frame. The first model pass calls flipFrame once, and later material/translucent passes share the mark; when the next flip has no new mark, the old mark expires. Marks made after a flip are also immediately visible. Removing the last mount cleans up the instance policy and both mark sets; unmounting the whole render domain can call resetAll. For MC's concrete timing see render-scheduling.md.

Multi-camera calls clearFrameMarks() before each host view pass; it clears only visibility marks and keeps the instance policy and render distance. FrameSampleCache.beginFrame(token) instead clears the sample set when the token changes; later camera views with the same token use firstSample(instance) to avoid duplicate sampling, while still being able to sample instances visible only in the new camera view. For the MC producer see the multi-camera and offscreen output document.

docs.title: Buffer rules
docs.text:
TypedBuffer counts index/offset in elements and sizeOfType/bufferCapacity in bytes. For a short array, updateAll updates only the prefix, keeping the capacity and the tail; updateRange must not go out of bounds and may write zero elements at the end of the capacity. slice keeps the packed byte order and borrows memory; it must not outlive the close point. A direct writeData in an implementation must also check the closed state and the element range. Closing is idempotent.

GpuUploadRing implements UploadBuffer, and the old GpuUploadRing.Device extends the framework's UploadDevice. Upload requires a complete direct snapshot; dirty bits are element indices, stride is in bytes, and mergeGap is in elements. An empty dirty set may reuse the current storage; each slot independently fills in the changes since its last upload. The input position/limit stay unchanged.

Every GPU consumption, including repeated draws of unchanged data and translucent replay, must mark markSubmitted. A busy slot cannot be overwritten; the device may reallocate storage; fence checks do not block. The device is responsible for API calls and bind state restoration; the ring owns the release of buffers/fences. The concrete OpenGL and macOS TBO orphan policies continue to be provided by the existing device implementations.

IVertexBuffer extends RenderBuffer<FlatModelData, ShaderInstance> and only adds access to the Minecraft VertexBuffer and the GL id. A new host integrates with the framework contract through its own data/shader types without referencing Minecraft interfaces.

docs.title: Sky Volumetric Clouds and Cumulonimbus Instances
docs.text:
Interfaces, configuration, and call reference. For the mechanics see volumetric-clouds.md.

Volumetric clouds are a separate optional feature, off by default. CloudEffects.setEnabled(true) automatically draws a sky cloud field spread around the observer position, and hides the vanilla block clouds in the main view and in standalone camera views at the same time. Turning it off restores the previous cloud settings; the toggle neither modifies nor saves the user's vanilla cloud options. Leaving the world turns it off automatically. Dimensions without a vanilla cloud layer do not draw the sky cloud field.

docs.title: Enabling the sky cloud field
docs.text:
import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.SkyCloudSettings;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.builtin.cloud.CloudEffects;

CloudEffects.sky().settings(SkyCloudSettings.DEFAULT);
CloudEffects.setSkyEnabled(true);
CloudEffects.setEnabled(true);

// Coverage, seed, and quality are adjustable at runtime; a change of wind speed does not teleport existing cloud clusters.
CloudEffects.sky().settings(CloudEffects.sky().settings()
        .withQuality(SkyCloudSettings.Quality.FAST));
CloudEffects.setEnabled(false);

The cloud field stacks 1–4 independent continuous density layers. Low cumulus layers have rolling tops, dark cloud bases, and varying development heights; mid-level cloud decks spread into sheets, and high thin clouds stretch into bands. Weather regions control cloud clusters, cloud gaps, and thickness variation; cloud bodies can cross weather grid boundaries, connect, or overlap, and are no longer arranged one per cell. A small number of cumulonimbus clouds that use independent shape envelopes are kept in the low layers.

The default three cloud layers have cloud base Y values of 900, 2700, and 5400, with thicknesses of 2100, 900, and 600. These values are adjustable scene scales; cumulus and cumulonimbus can also extend to the heights of other layers. The SCATTERED, CLOUDY, and OVERCAST presets use coverage controls of .38, .80, and .98 respectively: scattered cloud keeps large areas of clear sky, cloudy weather connects the cloud clusters, and overcast forms a continuous sheet.

SkyCloudSettings parameters are the seed, weather cell size, raw cloud base, maximum cumulonimbus thickness, coverage control, maximum display distance, X/Z wind speed, quality, and a layer list. The nine-parameter constructor generates three default layers from the cloud base and thickness. The actual height of each layer is controlled by SkyCloudLayer, and the list can contain several layers of the same type; changing the quality, coverage, or seed keeps the layer list. Wind speed uses world units per second. coverage=0 hides the clouds completely in clear weather, and rain increases the coverage; the sun direction, day/night, and weather colors come from the world.

Each layer separately controls the type, cloud base, thickness, horizontal shape scale, coverage offset, and optical density. Coverage and density are set separately, so a single cloud still keeps a sense of solidity even under scattered cover. A density of zero hides that layer, including the cumulonimbus embedded in it. The configuration can be replaced at runtime:

import java.util.List;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.SkyCloudLayer;

CloudEffects.sky().settings(SkyCloudSettings.CLOUDY.withLayers(List.of(
        new SkyCloudLayer(SkyCloudLayer.Type.CUMULUS, 900, 2100, 5200, 0, 2),
        new SkyCloudLayer(SkyCloudLayer.Type.STRATIFORM, 2700, 900, 3400, -.08f, 1.5f),
        new SkyCloudLayer(SkyCloudLayer.Type.CIRRUS, 5400, 600, 8000, -.12f, .55f))));

Each observer position uses a 32×32 weather window. The window relocates with the observer position, and clouds in the overlapping part stay unchanged; a standalone camera view can observe its own local window at a distant position. Near the world border, the camera position is first subtracted in double, then converted to GPU coordinates. Frame.weatherCellCount() only counts the candidate occupancy of weather control cells; a continuous cloud body has no per-cloud numbering, and that statistic cannot represent the on-screen coverage either. Each layer generates its weather independently.

docs.title: Creating a single cumulonimbus
docs.text:
The single-cloud API is kept; it can be used together with the sky cloud field, or with the field turned off to observe a single cloud:

import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.CloudPose;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.cloud.CloudSettings;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.effect.builtin.cloud.CumulonimbusCloud;

var cloud = new CumulonimbusCloud(CloudPose.at(100, 900, 1800).withYaw(20),
        CloudSettings.CUMULONIMBUS);
var handle = CloudEffects.spawn(cloud);
CloudEffects.setSkyEnabled(false);  // Observe only explicitly created instances
CloudEffects.setEnabled(true);
cloud.wind(.6, 0, .2);
cloud.moveBy(20, 0, 0);
cloud.rotateBy(30);                // Around the world Y axis, in degrees
cloud.scale(1.2f, 1, 1.2f);
cloud.settings(CloudSettings.CUMULONIMBUS.withCoverage(.75f));
handle.remove();
cloud.close();
CloudEffects.setEnabled(false);

A single cloud's position is the center of its base; the default size is 1600 wide, 1200 high, and 1200 deep. CloudSettings controls density, extinction, erosion, coverage, the anvil, seed, and quality. Direct transforms take effect immediately; wind and internal noise advance only with the client tick and stop when paused; the main view and several camera views sample the same moment and do not advance animation by render count.

docs.title: Rendering and cost
docs.text:
The cloud field uses one ray-marching pass covering the sky and one compositing draw, and does not create a fullscreen pass per cloud. It first intersects the ray with the height interval of each layer, sorts and merges overlapping intervals, and skips the gaps between layers directly. The sample budget is allocated by the square root of the interval length, so high thin clouds are not starved of budget by low layers and disappear; the densities of several layers at the same point are summed. The total number of samples per ray is limited by the budget, and the march ends early when the transmittance is very low. The weather window and the GPU textures use a cache of at most 8 entries, so travelling does not make memory grow continuously.

A shared shape texture preserves the cloud tower and anvil envelopes of the cumulonimbus; periodically generated Perlin-Worley/Worley noise provides the body, rolling, and erosion of the continuous layers. Each layer uses its own weather, noise phase, and shape scale, and thin clouds use a stretched anisotropic shape. The cloud field samples nearby density along the sun direction to approximate self-shadowing, and uses density scattering and highlight compression to preserve the relief of the cloud body; a single cumulonimbus uses a cached lighting voxel atlas, usually updated every 0.25 seconds.

For the cloud field, FAST/BALANCED/HIGH use width and height resolutions of 1/3, 1/2, and 1 of the original viewport, respectively; the total budget per ray is 112/160/256 samples, with 1/2/3 local lighting samples; high thin clouds use simplified lighting. For single-cloud quality, the corresponding resolutions are 1/3, 1/2, and 1, with at most 48/80/128 fine steps. Low-resolution results are upscaled with conservative depth and depth-aware interpolation. Both paths clip at the opaque scene depth, write no depth, do not limit the sky clouds by the terrain far plane, and restore the host GL state.

Distant views add atmospheric perspective and distance fade. There is currently no long-range cross-cloud shadowing, no ground cloud shadows, no temporal reprojection, and no complete weather simulation; compositing with transparent objects such as water follows render stages. The extra gbuffer channels of an Iris shader pack are not yet verified, and acceptance with the shader pack disabled cannot be used to infer its compatibility.

docs.title: Examples and verification
docs.text:
Development client:

  • /ksglib debug cloud enables the whole sky cloud field.
  • /ksglib debug cloud sparse switches to a sparse, multi-layer scattered-cloud state.
  • /ksglib debug cloud dense switches to a cloudy state with connected cloud clusters.
  • /ksglib debug cloud overcast switches to a continuous sheet.
  • /ksglib debug cloud single places a cumulonimbus in front and turns the sky cloud field off.
  • /ksglib debug cloud stop turns volumetric clouds off and restores the vanilla clouds.

Standalone preview, without starting Minecraft:

./gradlew :modules:modelling:renderPreview -PkasugaRenderScene=sky \
  -PkasugaRenderWidth=1920 -PkasugaRenderHeight=1080 --offline --no-daemon

The arrow keys change the view direction, W/S fly, and Escape exits. -PkasugaRenderFrames=60 ends automatically and saves the preview image; -PkasugaRenderScene=cloud keeps the original orbit preview of a single cumulonimbus. Images and reports are in modules/modelling/build/reports/renderHarness/.

./gradlew renderingReleaseCheck :modules:modelling:renderGlTest --offline --no-daemon
./gradlew :modules:modelling:renderBench -PkasugaRenderScene=sky \
  -PkasugaRenderWidth=1920 -PkasugaRenderHeight=1080 \
  -PkasugaRenderWarmup=8 -PkasugaRenderFrames=24 --offline --no-daemon

The benchmark uses GL_TIME_ELAPSED and covers the depth copy, the complete cloud field, and compositing, across ground, scattered cloud, overcast, inside the cloud layer, rain, and a distant observer position. This is GPU time for a standalone scene and cannot be converted into a full Minecraft frame FPS.

On 2026-10-04, on an Apple M3 Max, 1920×1080, BALANCED, with 16 warm-up frames and 64 sampled frames:

View / state GPU P50 GPU P95 Ground, default multi-layer 4.72 ms 5.99 ms Scattered 4.77 ms 5.84 ms Overcast 1.65 ms 1.97 ms Inside the cloud layer 7.21 ms 8.56 ms Rain 2.01 ms 3.18 ms Distant observer position 3.78 ms 5.19 ms

Overcast is faster because occlusion makes the ray marching end earlier. The values come from a standalone run of renderBench; the report is at build/reports/renderHarness/bench/report.json, relative to the module directory.

The pure-JVM regression checks per-layer weather independence, configuration immutability, weather continuity, spatial overlap, wind and interpolation, world-border precision, and cache boundaries. The GPU regression of the production shader checks the on-screen coverage difference between scattered and overcast, the separate visibility of each layer, the budget error relative to double sampling, several directions, distant/inside/above viewpoints, occlusion, relocation continuity, state restoration, and caching, and keeps the single-cloud regression.

Client acceptance in a temporary world uses -PkasugaTestSkyCloud=true, verifying a real camera near and 40000 units away, the main frame, the shared clock, and restoration of the vanilla cloud toggle. The success log is SKY_CLOUD_SMOKE_PASS, and the reports and screenshots are in debug/sky-cloud/ under the game directory. -PkasugaTestCloud=true keeps the single-cloud acceptance. These switches are only for purpose-built temporary test worlds.

docs.title: World UI and Free-Cursor Input
docs.text: Package: lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.backend.ui. Call these APIs on the Minecraft client thread. For coordinate transforms and input ownership, see the design. 中文.

docs.title: Integrating an Existing Screen
docs.text:
Minecraft mc = Minecraft.getInstance();
UIBackend backend = Constants.UI_BACKEND; // Available after client setup.
Screen panel = new MyPanelScreen();
panel.init(mc, 320, 180); // Panel-local dimensions, independent of the input viewport.

// Center the panel 2.5 blocks ahead of the camera, 1.92 blocks wide. Local +Y points down.
var camera = mc.gameRenderer.getMainCamera();
var center = camera.getPosition().add(
        camera.getLookVector().x * 2.5,
        camera.getLookVector().y * 2.5,
        camera.getLookVector().z * 2.5);
Matrix4f localToWorld = new Matrix4f()
        .translation((float) center.x, (float) center.y, (float) center.z)
        .rotate(camera.rotation())
        .scale(.006f, -.006f, 1)
        .translate(-160, -90, 0);
backend.addRenderable(panel, localToWorld);
backend.openPointer();

The built-in world_ui pipeline renders Constants.UI_BACKEND at AFTER_LEVEL in the main view. Call openPointer() from gameplay with a player, a world, and no other Screen active, for example from a key binding. A chat command must finish the chat Screen first, as the development demo does with mc.setScreen(null). The method returns the WorldUiInputScreen submitted to Minecraft.setScreen; other mods may still cancel screen opening.

The input Screen draws no background and does not pause the world. Minecraft's Screen lifecycle releases the mouse. Escape closes the input layer and restores mouse-look. The panel remains registered and returns to crosshair interaction. Call removeRenderable(panel) to remove it. Registrations belong to the backend and survive world changes; callers must remove world-specific panels when leaving their world.

In normal mouse-look, clicking an EditBox or MultiLineEditBox with the crosshair temporarily captures the keyboard. Characters reach the text field while gameplay movement and shortcuts are suppressed; the mouse still rotates the view. Escape clears text focus and exits without opening the pause menu. Repeats/releases from keys still held at exit are consumed; fresh presses resume gameplay. Buttons, disabled/hidden fields, and read-only fields do not start capture. World changes, window focus loss, another Screen, or target removal also end capture.

A panel with its own widget tree can implement WorldUiTextInput and report editable text focus through hasTextInputFocus(). It must clear internal focus when setFocused(false) is called, so Escape, target removal and panel changes can end editing. The shared backend remains independent of third-party widget libraries. LDLib2's LdElement.attach(backend, ui, width, height, transform) implements this contract and owns ticking, closing and world-boundary cleanup; see the LDLib2 world-UI adapter and demo.

A panel Screen can use its normal child-widget focus, keyboard, and text handling. Override the panel's own renderBackground if it should be transparent; its appearance is separate from the input layer. World rendering temporarily disables panel blur and then restores its previous value.

Widgets first render into a transparent RGBA canvas with the normal orthographic GUI depth range. The canvas is then drawn once on the world plane, preserving the small depth separation between text and shadows. Canvas density follows GUI scale, targets resize when needed, and local scissor rectangles use canvas dimensions. Premultiplied-alpha composition preserves translucent edges and does not write the panel rectangle into world depth. MIN_GUI_Z, MAX_GUI_Z, and boundary text shadows affect only canvas ordering. Composite vertices always use local Z=0, so GUI depth cannot push the panel towards the player. Canvas clipping reserves one extra unit beyond each GUI depth endpoint.

docs.title: API and Contracts
docs.text:
API Behavior addRenderable(Renderable) Centers the default panel at the world origin, using GUI height as pixels per block; duplicate registration does not duplicate drawing addRenderable(Renderable, Matrix4fc) Registers the panel and copies its pixel-local to absolute-world transform setTransform(Renderable, Matrix4fc) Sets or updates a transform; rejects non-finite, non-affine, or singular matrices removeRenderable(Renderable) Stops rendering and releases that target's captured mouse buttons and keys openPointer() Opens the input Screen; throws IllegalStateException without a player/world or while another Screen is active getInputRouter().setMaxDistance(float) Maximum hit distance from the rendered near plane, default 5 blocks; requires a finite positive value worldChanged() Clears input and releases temporary GPU canvases while retaining panel registrations; the global backend uses the existing world-change hook close() Clears input, canvases, and registrations; custom backend owners must call it on destruction resetInput() Clears hover, keyboard focus, and captures, balancing held mouse buttons and keys with release events isKeyboardCaptured() Whether normal-view text keyboard capture is active WorldUiTextInput.hasTextInputFocus() A third-party panel reports editable text focus in its own widget tree and clears that state on focus loss renderAllUis(GuiGraphics, float) Custom world-render entry using the current world projection and effective model-view; do not call during the HUD orthographic pass renderWorld(WorldRenderPipelineContext) World-pipeline entry for a custom backend; saves/restores projection and model-view and accepts only the main view

Screen.width/height or the position and size of a LayoutElement define the input rectangle. Objects without GuiEventListener or known dimensions only render. Plane intersection reuses RayTracingHelper.intersectRayWithPlane. The nearest rectangle receives input; ties follow registration order. Picking does not test block occlusion or texture alpha.

The transparent layer consumes incoming mouse, scroll, and keyboard events, including misses, so they do not operate the world. Keyboard input goes to the last clicked panel, whose normal child dispatch selects the widget. Escape always exits. An accepted mouse press captures its target per button. Dragging outside the rectangle continues to project onto that panel's plane, and release returns to the original target. Parallel rays or intersections behind the ray origin retain the last valid capture coordinates. Window focus loss, screen replacement, target removal, dimension changes, and disconnect cancel captures.

docs.title: Reusing an Existing Raycast
docs.text:
Use the projection component independently when the host already has a world-space hit solver:

var projection = new ScreenPointerProjection(worldProjection, guiWidth, guiHeight);
Vector3f origin = new Vector3f(), direction = new Vector3f();
if (projection.ray(mouseGuiX, mouseGuiY, origin, direction)) {
    // If viewMatrix includes camera translation, inverseView restores absolute world coordinates.
    inverseView.transformPosition(origin);
    inverseView.transformDirection(direction).normalize();
    existingRaycast(origin, direction);
}

When the view matrix contains only camera rotation, apply its inverse and then add the camera world position to origin. ray produces a unit ray starting on the near plane, supporting perspective and orthographic cameras. Coordinates are GUI logical pixels with (0,0) at the top left. Convert raw GLFW/window cursor coordinates using guiWidth / screenWidth and guiHeight / screenHeight; do not mix framebuffer dimensions with window coordinates. The constructor copies and validates the projection and viewport, throwing IllegalArgumentException for invalid values. Non-finite cursor coordinates make ray return false. Capture the rendered projection again after FOV, zoom, or viewport changes.

docs.title: Development Acceptance
docs.text:
./gradlew :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest --tests 'lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.backend.ui.*' --offline
./gradlew :modules:modelling:compileContentTestingJava --offline
./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClient

In a test world, run /ksglib debug world_ui. A panel is fixed in front of the camera at its opening pose, and the free cursor opens immediately. Click both sides, type in the text field, scroll, drag outside the panel, and release. Check the counters and local drag deltas. Press Escape, turn the camera, and check crosshair interaction. Run the command again to rebuild the panel and reopen the cursor. /ksglib debug world_ui stop removes it.

After leaving the free cursor, crosshair-click the text field and type WASD/Chinese. Text should change without moving the player, while the mouse still rotates the view. Hold W, press Escape, then release and press W again: editing exits first, and the fresh press restores movement. Buttons must not capture the keyboard. Run /ksglib debug world_ui min_z and /ksglib debug world_ui max_z to check complete glyphs/shadows and unchanged panel distance; both presets use the same world transform as the default.

Check that text, shadows, button borders, and edit-box borders have no stripes or missing fragments. Enter long ASCII and Chinese text to check clipping, then stop the demo and verify world, hand, and HUD rendering.

Window resizing, GUI scale, FOV, third-person views, and focus changes require real-client acceptance. JVM tests cover projection math and routing state; they do not replace in-game rendering or GLFW verification.

With an existing isolated test world, run the real keyboard Mixin/character and GUI-depth pixel smoke:

./gradlew :modules:modelling:runClientHeadless --offline \
  -PkasugaClientDirectory=run/world-ui-smoke -PkasugaQuickPlayWorld=TestWorld \
  -PkasugaTestWorldUiInput=true

Place TestWorld under that run directory's saves/. The test uses a hidden window and exits on completion; JSON and PNG output is in debug/world-ui-input/ under the run directory. It does not cover OS input-method candidate windows or the feel of player interaction.

docs.text:
Trap: the old layout does not match the current implementation. The layout described by earlier upstream docs is data/<modid>/kasugalib/*.json (flat files, a sources field), which is deprecated. The current contract is the index directory data/<modid>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/ plus the content directory data/<modid>/kasuga_lib_content/.

Reference pages (this directory):

Document Type Content schema.md Reference Fields, types, D1–D6 rules, and error classification for the index manifest and content files api-registration.md Reference Registration-phase entry point JsonTreeBuilder, the index API, content dispatch, and conflict resolution api-extension.md Reference The TypeHandler system, BuildContext, FactoryRegistry, and property parsers api-diagnostics.md Reference The Diagnostics facade, the /kasuga_data command, and error classification api-reload.md Reference The reload API, the assertable pure-function surface, and call examples
