docs.title: Data-Driven Diagnostics API (Diagnostics, Commands, and Error Classification)
6. The Diagnostics Facade
docs.text: diagnostics/Diagnostics.java is the unified diagnostics facade. Errors are addressed along two dimensions that never mix.

docs.title: 6.1 Dimensions
docs.text:
mod dimension: buckets keyed by mod id, which are the existing JsonTreeBuilder buckets. report(String, Throwable) / errors(String) delegate to them verbatim, so the contract "assert that JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors(modId) is empty" keeps holding.

domain/source-key dimension: buckets keyed by (Domain, key), for failures that "belong to a source rather than a mod". Producers already write to this dimension: the reload domain uses Domain.RELOAD_DATA, key = namespace (both ReloadOrchestrator and FsmReloadHandler go through it). The remaining domains (RELOAD_ASSETS, CONFIG) are still reserved.

docs.title: 6.2 Method Table
docs.text:
mod dimension:

Signature Responsibility Failure behavior report(String modId, Throwable error) (:64) Records one failure into the mod bucket, equivalent to JsonTreeBuilder.addLoadingError No validation errors(String modId) (:73) An immutable snapshot of that mod Returns List.of() when there is no bucket errorsByMod() (:78) All mods, keys sorted by id, immutable Returns an empty map when there is no bucket clear(String modId) (:83) Clears that mod's bucket only The other mods and every source bucket are untouched

domain/source-key dimension:

Signature Responsibility Failure behavior report(Domain domain, String key, Throwable error) (:96) Records one failure into some source's bucket A null in any of the three parameters throws NullPointerException (an up-front check, treated as a programming error) errors(Domain domain, String key) (:107) An immutable snapshot of a single source bucket Returns List.of() when there is no bucket errors(Domain domain) (:116) The aggregate over all sources of one domain, sources sorted by key Returns an empty list when there is no bucket clear(Domain domain) (:125) Clears every source bucket of one domain The other domains and every mod bucket are untouched

Shared by both dimensions:

Signature Responsibility clearAll() (:130) Clears both dimensions summarize() (:143) One line per non-empty bucket, see 6.4

docs.title: 6.3 Domain
docs.text:
public enum Domain { REGISTRATION, RELOAD_DATA, RELOAD_ASSETS, CONFIG }   // Diagnostics.java:40
Value Meaning REGISTRATION Content registered by the mod jar, read once during mod construction RELOAD_DATA Reload data from data packs, read from the pack stack on /reload RELOAD_ASSETS Pack-stack assets, read on resource reload CONFIG Files under config/

docs.title: 6.4 summarize Output Format
docs.text:
public static List<String> summarize()   // Diagnostics.java:143

One line per non-empty bucket. The mod bucket format is <mod>: N error(s); the source bucket format is <DOMAIN>[<key>]: N error(s). Mods come first, sorted by id, then Domain declaration order, with sources sorted by key. The result is deterministic, so commands and tests can assert it.

docs.title: 6.5 Which Dimension Producers Use
docs.text: Reload-domain errors go through the domain/source-key dimension (Domain.RELOAD_DATA), key = the namespace the failing file sits in. ReloadOrchestrator.reportError (:566-573) and each handler's reportError / reportWarning (for example FsmReloadHandler.java:118-130) call Diagnostics.report(Domain.RELOAD_DATA, namespace, ...). Registration-phase errors still go through the mod dimension. The two dimensions are told apart in the output by different labels: mod dimension [<mod>] <error>, reload dimension [RELOAD_DATA[<namespace>]] <error> (the label is provided by Diagnostics.bucketLabel, the same source as the summary line). The reload dimension is cleared per round (Diagnostics.clear(Domain.RELOAD_DATA) at the start of runCycle, :208) and does not accumulate.

docs.title: 7. The /kasuga_data errors Command
docs.text:
DataDiagnosticsCommands.java is the in-game entry point of the diagnostics facade.

public static LiteralArgumentBuilder<CommandSourceStack> kasugaDataCommand()   // :42

Command syntax:

  • /kasuga_data errors: prints the one-line-per-bucket summary of Diagnostics.summarize(), both dimensions included — mod dimension <mod>: N error(s), reload dimension RELOAD_DATA[<namespace>]: N error(s). With no errors it prints Kasuga data: no loading errors recorded.
  • /kasuga_data errors <mod>: lists both dimensions of that mod's errors — registration phase (mod dimension) as [<mod>] <throwable> per entry; reload phase (Domain.RELOAD_DATA, key = namespace) as [RELOAD_DATA[<mod>]] <throwable> per entry (the label comes from the same source as the summary line, provided by Diagnostics.bucketLabel). With no errors it prints Kasuga data: no loading errors for '<mod>'.

Constraints and registration:

  • Permission level 2 (requires(source -> source.hasPermission(2)), :44). On a dedicated server this command outputs internal loading diagnostics, which counts as administrator information; console level 4 is unaffected.
  • kasugaDataCommand() does not depend on a dispatcher or an event, so a pure test can register it and then assert the shape of the command tree.
  • Auto-discovery: the class carries @EventBusSubscriber (:28), and once FML scans it, onRegisterCommands (:54) registers the command tree on RegisterCommandsEvent. The registration sits on the COMMON side, because the facade itself is common.
  • The return value is the number of lines printed, for the command system and tests to read.

docs.title: 12. Error Classification
docs.text:
Go into the error bucket (an ERROR log is written and the failure enters the bucket as an exception — during the registration phase into the mod dimension, through JsonTreeBuilder.addLoadingError or Diagnostics.report(String, …); during the reload phase into the Domain.RELOAD_DATA source dimension, through Diagnostics.report(Domain, namespace, …)):

Case Source Index file unreadable or not JSON readIndexManifest:188 Unknown top-level field in an index (including the old field name sources, see 3.7) parseIndexManifest:226-230 Neither index field declared parseIndexManifest:240-244 Field is not an array readPathArray:256-263 Array element is not a string readPathArray:268-274 The same path listed under both domains resolveIndexManifests:308-316 No index declares either domain resolveIndexManifests:323-326 Index directory cannot be listed listIndexFiles:767-771 Illegal content path parseSource:396-402 Mod file not found parseSource:408-412 Content file missing parseSource:423-427 Content file read / JSON exception parseSource:434-436 Unknown top-level field in content (including a top-level block_entities) dispatchContent:475-490 Type field is not an array dispatchContent:504-510 Array element is not an object dispatchContent:504-516 handler.apply throws applyUnchecked:712 Duplicate id conflict resolveDuplicates:667-670 Legacy layout directory present buildForMod:66-74 buildAll exception for a single mod buildAll:171 reload decode/register/validate failure ReloadOrchestrator.reportError:566-573, FsmReloadHandler.reportError:118-125 reload wrap-up finds a dangling clip reference FsmReloadHandler.reportWarning:127-130

Log only, never the bucket (downgraded to WARN level):

Case Source Factory not found RegTypeHandler:71-73 Group reference cycle JsonTreeBuilder:823-825 Unknown block property / illegal value JsonPropertyParser:50-57 Unknown item property JsonItemParser:63 BE parent block not found / BE type unknown BlockEntityTypeHandler:76-86 Fallback warning when a duplicate id unexpectedly reaches apply RegTypeHandler:101-105 A mod declares no on_register (a reload-only mod) JsonTreeBuilder:100-104 (INFO) Index directory absent and no legacy layout JsonTreeBuilder:74 (DEBUG)

Notes: Diagnostics.report does not rethrow and rejects null arguments up front, and the buckets stay readable while loading is under way (each key is synchronized separately). Every error is swallowed into a bucket and the mod keeps starting. The conditional D9 hint shows up in two kinds of message: on the registration side the unknown-field message points at on_reload (JsonTreeBuilder:559-570; the reload key names are enumerated at runtime from ReloadHandlerRegistry); on the reload side the unknown-field message points at on_register (ReloadOrchestrator:439-446). The reload-domain bucket is cleared per round (Diagnostics.clear(Domain.RELOAD_DATA) at the start of runCycle, :208), so repeated /reloads of the same broken file do not accumulate.

Other pages in the data-driven series: Registration API · Extension API · Diagnostics API · Reload API · Series index

docs.title: Data-driven extension API (TypeHandler, BuildContext, and property parsers)
8.1 TypeHandler
docs.text:
public interface TypeHandler<T> {                                  // TypeHandler.java:8
    int PHASE_GROUPS = 0;                                          // :11
    int PHASE_CONTENT = 1;                                         // :14
    int PHASE_EMBEDDED = 2;                                        // :17
    String getTypeName();                                          // :20
    int getPhase();                                                // :27
    T parse(JsonObject json);                                      // :29
    void apply(T definition, BuildContext context);                // :31
    default String getParentTypeName() { return null; }            // :38
    default String getEmbeddedKeyName() { return null; }           // :48
    default List<JsonObject> extractEmbedded(JsonObject parentJson) { return null; }  // :50
    default String resolveIdentity(String modId, T definition) { return null; }       // :64
}
Method Responsibility and constraints Failure behavior getTypeName() The declared top-level JSON field name, unique within TypeHandlerRegistry With the same name a later registration overrides an earlier one, with no warning getPhase() The apply phase, see 2.4 None parse Turn a JSON object into a definition object Recommended to be a pure function; a thrown exception loses only the current entry while siblings parse as usual, and produces one entry <i> in '<key>' failed to parse: <msg>; entry skipped apply Register the definition into the registration tree The exception is caught by applyUnchecked and turned into a bucket entry, without interrupting other entries getParentTypeName() Non-null means this is an embedded type, and the value is its parent type's field name null means a top-level type getEmbeddedKeyName() The key name of the embedded type inside the parent entry, for diagnostics only When an embedded type does not override it, null is returned and the diagnostic loses one hint extractEmbedded(parentJson) Extract the list of embedded objects from the parent entry Returning null means there is no embedded content; it takes no part in top-level dispatch resolveIdentity(modId, definition) The identity used for deduplication A default of null opts out of deduplication

docs.title: 8.2 TypeHandlerRegistry
docs.text:
public static <T> void register(TypeHandler<T> handler);            // :11
public static TypeHandler<?> get(String typeName);                  // :15
public static Collection<TypeHandler<?>> all();                     // :19
public static TypeHandler<?> findByParent(String parentType);       // :23

A global static table (LinkedHashMap) shared by all mods, with no namespace isolation. all() returns an immutable view preserving registration order. findByParent searches linearly and returns only the first match, so a parent type can currently carry at most one embedded subtype.

docs.title: 8.3 Top-level vs embedded
docs.text: A top-level type occupies one top-level JSON field (such as blocks). An embedded type occupies no top-level field and can only enter from a parent entry via extractEmbedded. BlockEntityTypeHandler is the reference implementation (getParentTypeName returns "blocks", getEmbeddedKeyName returns "block_entity"): it copies the parent entry's id into the embedded object's _parent_block and uses that at apply time to find the parent block back with context.getBlockReg(...) (BlockEntityTypeHandler.java:33-44, 71-101). When it is written as a top-level field by mistake, dispatchContent reports an unknown field and gives the correct key name, while the rest of the file's fields dispatch as usual.

docs.title: 8.4 RegTypeHandler
docs.text:
handler/RegTypeHandler.java is the abstract base class shared by blocks / items, pinning down the registration flow.

protected abstract String resolveRawId(T definition);                       // :19
protected abstract Reg<?, ?> createRegistration(T definition, String path); // :21
protected String resolveType(T definition) { return getTypeName(); }        // :28
protected void configureTypeSpecific(T definition, Reg<?, ?> reg) {}        // :30
protected String resolveRegistryGroup(T definition) { return null; }        // :32
protected JsonObject resolveItemProperties(T definition) { return null; }   // :34
protected ResourceLocation resolveCreativeTab(T definition) { return null; }// :36
protected String resolveNamespace(String rawId)                              // :38
protected String resolvePath(String rawId)                                   // :43
public String resolveIdentity(String modId, T definition)                    // :58
public void apply(T definition, BuildContext baseContext)                    // :63

The fixed flow of apply: split the id into namespace and path (with no :, the namespace is treated as minecraft); when createRegistration returns null, log the No factory for type '<type>' (id '<id>') WARN and skip; when the namespace is not minecraft, attach a ResourceLocation mapping to the Reg, which is the namespace-rewrite mechanism; attach the group (falling back to the root group when it cannot be found); resolve the creative tab (definition level first, otherwise inherit from the group level); run type-specific configuration; put the Reg into context.putReg(getTypeName(), ...) for cross-handler lookup.

RegTypeHandler.apply catches exceptions internally, logs a WARN, and returns (:107-111). resolveItemProperties is currently declared in the implementation but has no call site; the implementations BlockTypeHandler / ItemTypeHandler each parse properties in their own configureTypeSpecific (BlockTypeHandler.java:68-88, ItemTypeHandler.java:64-72). Whether this hook will be wired up is to be confirmed.

docs.title: 8.5 Built-in handlers
docs.text: Handler getTypeName getPhase parse output Source RegistryGroupHandler registry_groups PHASE_GROUPS RegistryGroupDef(id, parent, properties, item_properties) RegistryGroupHandler.java:20-33 BlockTypeHandler blocks PHASE_CONTENT BlockDef(id, type, registry_group, properties, item_properties, params) BlockTypeHandler.java:19-34 ItemTypeHandler items PHASE_CONTENT ItemDef(id, type, registry_group, properties, params) ItemTypeHandler.java:16-30 BlockEntityTypeHandler block_entities PHASE_EMBEDDED BlockEntityDef(type, parentBlockId, params), produced by extractEmbedded from the block_entity key BlockEntityTypeHandler.java:21-53

docs.title: 8.6 Adding a new type
docs.text:
1. Implement TypeHandler<T>. If the output is to go into an MC registry, inherit RegTypeHandler<T> instead and implement resolveRawId and createRegistration.
  2. Call TypeHandlerRegistry.register(handler) to declare the typeName; the top-level field name is getTypeName().
  3. If you go through RegTypeHandler, register the corresponding factory with FactoryRegistry (see section 10); the handler constructs the Reg from the value of the JSON type field.
  4. Override resolveIdentity when deduplication is needed; override getParentTypeName / getEmbeddedKeyName / extractEmbedded when embedding is needed.

TestGenericFactory.java is the minimal example you can copy in a test: a custom handler plus FactoryRegistry.registerGeneric, with parse taking the factory from FactoryRegistry.getGeneric. Real dispatch is done by JsonTreeBuilder; that example walks TypeHandlerRegistry.all() by hand only to assert the parse result.

docs.title: 8.7 ContentStructure (shared structure layer)
docs.text:
structure/ContentStructure.java:30. The structure-decision layer shared by the registration domain (the JsonTreeBuilder dispatcher) and the reload domain (ReloadOrchestrator and the two decoders): a pure function depending only on Gson and java.util, with no Minecraft or loader types, whose every rule is pinned by pure JVM unit tests.

public final class ContentStructure {
    public enum Kind { BODY_NOT_OBJECT, UNKNOWN_KEY, MISSING_KEY, VALUE_NOT_ARRAY, ELEMENT_NOT_OBJECT }  // :33

    public record Issue(Kind kind, String key, int index, JsonElement actual) {}   // :55
    public record Field(List<Element> elements, List<Issue> issues) {}             // :65
    public record Element(int fileIndex, JsonObject body) {}                       // :76

    public static Issue body(JsonElement raw);                        // :84 a non-object body → one issue, otherwise null
    public static List<Issue> unknownKeys(JsonElement body, Set<String> knownKeys);  // :98 one issue per unclaimed key
    public static Field field(JsonElement body, String typeKey);      // :123 single-field structural split: valid elements + issues
    public static String joinWithOr(List<String> items);              // :162 joins with " or ", reused by two hints
    public static String describe(JsonElement json);                  // :177 human-readable description of a JSON type
}
  • body: the file body must be a JSON object; null is treated as a non-object. Returning null means it passed.
  • unknownKeys: checks key by key, each key not in knownKeys produces one UNKNOWN_KEY; a non-object body returns an empty list (that case is body's job).
  • field: splits one top-level field. A missing key or a non-array value each produce one issue and no element (the caller rejects the whole field on that basis); a non-object element produces an issue while its siblings are kept (element-level isolation).
  • describe: the shared JSON type description (such as "an array" / "a primitive (5)"), replacing the three private copies that used to be byte-identical.

One decision, per-side rendering: ContentStructure only decides structure and never produces user-facing wording. An Issue carries the decision result and the offending value, and each caller renders it with its own template. That is what lets the two sides keep their respective wording (in particular, ReloadHandler.describeFile() is still the reload domain's own wording contract) and lets the two sides' cross-domain hints point in opposite directions (D9: the registration domain hints "list it under on_reload", the reload domain hints "list it under on_register"), while the shape rules themselves are implemented in exactly one place.

Where it sits in the layering: it stops at the "structure" layer and does not cross into "element → T"; mapping an element to a definition type remains each handler's own parse (entry level) / decode (file level) job. So after this layer was added, the six handlers' code did not change by a single line. TypeHandler.parse / ReloadHandler.decode take the Field.elements() (List<Element>) returned by field(...) as input and each do their own type conversion and validation; Element.fileIndex() keeps the element's index in the top-level array, so diagnostics can reference the original position.

docs.title: 10. FactoryRegistry
docs.text:
modules/core/src/main/java/lib/kasuga/registration/factory/FactoryRegistry.java. The data-driven handlers take their factory from here by the JSON type field.

public interface BlockFactory        { Reg<?, Block> create(String id, @Nullable JsonObject params); }        // :18
public interface ItemFactory         { Reg<?, Item> create(String id, @Nullable JsonObject params); }         // :23
public interface BlockEntityFactory  { Reg<?, ?> create(String id, Supplier<Block[]> validBlocks, @Nullable JsonObject params); }  // :28
public interface GenericFactory      { Reg<?, ?> create(String id, JsonObject params); }                       // :33

public static void register(String type, BlockFactory factory);            // :44
public static BlockFactory get(String type);                              // :48
public static boolean contains(String type);                              // :52
public static void registerItem(String type, ItemFactory factory);         // :58
public static ItemFactory getItemFactory(String type);                    // :62
public static boolean containsItem(String type);                          // :66
public static void registerBlockEntity(String type, BlockEntityFactory factory);  // :74
public static BlockEntityFactory getBlockEntityFactory(String type);      // :79
public static boolean containsBlockEntity(String type);                   // :83
public static Set<String> getBlockEntityTypes();                          // :87
public static void registerGeneric(String type, GenericFactory factory);  // :93
public static GenericFactory getGeneric(String type);                     // :95
public static boolean containsGeneric(String type);                       // :97
  • Internally a ConcurrentHashMap; registering the same type twice silently overrides.
  • The id parameter contains only the path; the namespace has already been stripped by the handler and handed to the Reg's namespace rewrite, so do not prepend a namespace again inside the factory.
  • params is the raw object of the params field in the definition, may be null, and its semantics are defined by the factory.
  • BlockEntityFactory.validBlocks is a Supplier<Block[]> and is evaluated lazily; the factory should store the Supplier rather than calling get() immediately during construction.
  • get* returns null when nothing is registered, and the caller turns that into a diagnostic.

docs.title: 11.1 JsonPropertyParser
docs.text:
public static final JsonPropertyParser INSTANCE;    // :23
public static JsonPropertyParser getInstance();     // :217
public List<Function<BlockBehaviour.Properties, BlockBehaviour.Properties>> parseBlockProperties(JsonObject json);  // :28
public void registerCompiler(PropertyCompiler compiler);   // :197
public void registerCompiler(String key, BiFunction<String, JsonElement, Function<BlockBehaviour.Properties, BlockBehaviour.Properties>> supplier);  // :201
public void removeCompiler(PropertyCompiler compiler);     // :209
public int compilerSize();                                 // :213
  • parseBlockProperties(null) returns an empty list.
  • Compilers are tried in list order, stopping at the first valid(key, value) hit. Built-in keys are matched with an exact ResourceLocation (RLCompiler, :189).
  • An unmatched key logs the Unknown block property: <key> WARN and is skipped, without a bucket entry.
  • An illegal value logs the Failed to parse block property '<key>' WARN and is skipped.
  • buildCompilers (:148) registers the built-in keys, including the boolean switches, friction, strength, map_color, sound_type, light_emission, and so on.

docs.title: 11.2 JsonItemParser
docs.text:
public static final JsonItemParser INSTANCE;        // :15
public List<Function<Item.Properties, Item.Properties>> parseItemProperties(JsonObject json);  // :38
public void registerParser(String key, ItemPropertyParser parser);  // :67
public interface ItemPropertyParser { Function<Item.Properties, Item.Properties> parse(String key, JsonElement value); }  // :72
  • parseItemProperties(null) returns an empty list.
  • tab is a reserved key: it is skipped directly at the parser stage (:52), and the handler layer translates it into a creative tab binding.
  • An unknown key logs the Unknown item property: <key> WARN and is skipped.
  • Built-in keys: stacks_to, rarity, fire_resistant, durability, no_repair (:23-35).

docs.title: 11.3 Property inheritance and override
docs.text:
The order in which properties take effect is decided by the property chain of the Reg tree: parents before children, and whatever applies later overrides what applied earlier. The chain runs root-group properties, parent group, child group, block level; the block level applies last and therefore has the highest priority. Item properties work the same way: a group's item_properties comes before a block-level item_properties. Override here is achieved through apply order, with no field merging; a key of the same name is overridden whole.

Other pages in the data-driven section: Registration-phase API · Extension API · Diagnostics API · Reload API · Section index

docs.title: Data-driven registration-phase API (JsonTreeBuilder, index, and content dispatch)
docs.text: This page is a reference (for looking things up). Its subject is the KasugaLibNext data-driven Java API: classes, methods, signatures, call timing, and failure behavior. Applies to: Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge 21.1.203 / Parchment 2024.11.17 / Java 21. Line numbers on this page refer to the current working tree (the uncommitted data-driven reimplementation), baseline commit ec864a1; signatures evolve with the code, so references are written as class:line and can be checked back against the code. Boundary: which key a JSON field is written under, what type it has, and whether it is required all belong to schema.md; the getting-started tutorial belongs to intro.md, and the steps for content authors and extension authors belong to guide-content.md / guide-extension.md. This page mentions field names only at the level of "which method reads it, and what happens when the read fails". Terminology: a domain is one of the two arrays in the index manifest, on_register (registration domain) and on_reload (reload domain); a bucket is a list holding diagnostics, split along two dimensions: the mod dimension, split by mod id (registration-phase errors), and the domain/source-key dimension, split by (Domain, key) (reload-phase errors use RELOAD_DATA[<namespace>]).

docs.title: 1. Module and package structure
docs.text:
Code root: modules/data-driven/src/main/java/lib/kasuga/registration/data_driven/.

data_driven/
├── TypeHandler.java                 # handler interface: top-level/embedded types, phase, identity
├── TypeHandlerRegistry.java         # global static handler table (LinkedHashMap, order-preserving)
├── JsonTreeIntegration.java         # the wiring point with RegisterContextRegistry
├── builder/
│   └── JsonTreeBuilder.java         # registration-phase entry: index parsing, content dispatch, dedup, apply, error bucket
├── context/
│   ├── BuildContext.java            # build context base class (modId / rootGroup / meta access)
│   ├── RegBuildContext.java         # registration-scenario context (group / reg access)
│   └── JsonRegistryGroup.java       # a group created from JSON (a RegistryGroup subclass)
├── handler/
│   ├── MetaTypeHandler.java         # marker base class, no extra behavior
│   ├── RegistryGroupHandler.java    # registry_groups, PHASE_GROUPS
│   ├── RegTypeHandler.java          # abstract base class for registration-type handlers (shared by blocks/items)
│   ├── BlockTypeHandler.java        # blocks, PHASE_CONTENT
│   ├── ItemTypeHandler.java         # items, PHASE_CONTENT
│   └── BlockEntityTypeHandler.java  # block_entities (embedded in blocks), PHASE_EMBEDDED
├── dedup/
│   ├── DuplicateIdResolver.java     # pure-function last-wins deduplication
│   └── EffectiveId.java             # id normalization
├── reload/                          # reload domain: extension points + orchestrator
│   ├── ReloadHandler.java           # extension interface: decode/register for one reload type
│   ├── ReloadHandlerRegistry.java   # global static handler table (LinkedHashMap, order-preserving)
│   ├── ReloadOrchestrator.java      # reload-cycle orchestrator: clear buckets / discover / dedup / register / wrap-up
│   ├── Decoded.java                 # the result of one decode (entries + errors)
│   └── Reloaded.java                # a landed registration entry + the namespace it came from
├── diagnostics/
│   ├── Diagnostics.java             # the diagnostic facade (mod dimension + domain/source-key dimension)
│   └── DataDiagnosticsCommands.java # /kasuga_data errors [mod]
└── property/
    ├── JsonPropertyParser.java      # block property parsing
    ├── JsonItemParser.java          # item property parsing
    └── compiler/                    # custom property matchers

The orchestration and decoding of the reload domain live in two places:

  • modules/data-driven/src/main/java/lib/kasuga/registration/data_driven/reload/ (the orchestrator ReloadOrchestrator, the extension points ReloadHandler / ReloadHandlerRegistry / Decoded / Reloaded)
  • modules/modelling/src/main/java/lib/kasuga/rendering/models/mc/dynamic/fsm/ (the consumers: the two handlers FsmReloadHandler / FsmClipsReloadHandler, the registrar bean FsmReloadHandlerRegistrar, and the pure decoders StateMachineDefinitionLoader.java and AnimationClipLoader.java)
  • modules/render-core/src/main/java/lib/kasuga/rendering/models/uml/dynamic/fsm/FsmAnimationClips.java and FsmDefinitions.java (bucketed storage)

Dependency direction: modelling → data-driven. data-driven does not depend on modelling.

docs.title: 2. Registration-phase entry point: JsonTreeBuilder
docs.text: builder/JsonTreeBuilder.java is the only entry point of the registration domain. All methods are static, and the class cannot be instantiated (:798).

docs.title: 2.1 buildForMod
docs.text:
public static JsonRegistryGroup buildForMod(String modId)   // JsonTreeBuilder.java:61

Responsibility: load one mod's on_register content, and build and return its root registry group <modId>:json_root.

Parameter constraint: modId must have a corresponding mod file in FML's ModList (internally via findModFile, :723). When it is not found, null is returned and no error is reported.

Execution order (one call):

  1. ensureHandlersRegistered() (:52), idempotent, registers the four built-in handlers once.
  2. clearLoadingErrors(modId) (:63), clears only that mod's bucket.
  3. Locate the index directory data/<modId>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/ (findIndexDir, :776).
  4. Read the index manifests one by one (listIndexFiles scans the directory, readIndexManifest parses), then aggregate them (resolveIndexManifests).
  5. Parse only the content files on_register points at; the on_reload section is recognized and validated here, but not parsed (:105-110).
  6. Resolve duplicate ids before any apply side effect (:119).
  7. Apply each handler in ascending getPhase() order; registry_groups gets an extra topological sort before apply (:135-146).
  8. Return rootGroup (:148).

Cases that return null:

Case Location Error recorded? The index directory does not exist, and the old-layout directory data/<mod>/kasugalib/ does not exist either :75-79 No, only a DEBUG record The index directory does not exist, but the old-layout directory does :66-74 Yes, WARN + bucket entry, hinting at migration to on_register The index directory exists, but no manifest declares either domain (an empty directory included) :95-99 Yes; the aggregation stage records "declares neither ... in any index file"

Note: a mod that declares only on_reload does not count as nothingDeclared(), so it returns a non-null empty root group (:100-104 records only INFO), not null.

docs.title: 2.2 buildAll
docs.text:
public static Map<String, JsonRegistryGroup> buildAll()   // JsonTreeBuilder.java:151

Responsibility: walk every mod file in ModList, call buildForMod for each mod, and collect the non-null results with the mod id as key, preserving LinkedHashMap order.

Parameters: none. Constraint: the same mod file path is processed only once (visitedRoots, :159).

Failure behavior: when a single mod throws, the catch records an ERROR and puts the exception wrapped in an IllegalStateException into that mod's bucket (:168-172), then carries on with the next mod.

Note: there is no call site for buildAll() anywhere in the repository (only its declaration); the actual wiring currently goes through buildForMod. Whether it is a reserved API is to be confirmed.

docs.title: 2.3 When JsonTreeIntegration is wired up
docs.text:
JsonTreeIntegration (JsonTreeIntegration.java:13) is a Micronaut @Context bean. @PostConstruct (:21) registers a COMMON-side callback with RegisterContextRegistry; the callback body calls JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod(modRegistry.getModId()) and, when the result is non-null, attaches it as a child node of modRegistry (:24-33).

The callback fires lazily: it runs only at the first registration-event dispatch for that mod. The guarantee this gives is that every @Context static factory registration precedes JSON parsing, without relying on explicit ordering.

docs.title: 2.4 Phase semantics
docs.text:
Constant Value Handler that uses it Reason TypeHandler.PHASE_GROUPS 0 registry_groups Groups must exist before content TypeHandler.PHASE_CONTENT 1 blocks, items Regular content TypeHandler.PHASE_EMBEDDED 2 block_entities A BE has to attach to an already existing block Reg

Within the same phase the order is registration order (TypeHandlerRegistry uses a LinkedHashMap). The application order of registry_groups is also topologically sorted by parent reference via topoSortGroupDefs (:869); when there is a cycle, the Cycle detected among registry groups WARN is logged, the nodes on the cycle apply in their original order, and RegistryGroupHandler.store falls back to the root group for a parent it cannot find. A reference cycle therefore loses only hierarchy, never a group.

docs.title: 3. Index API
docs.text: Index directory: data/<modId>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/. Every .json under it is a manifest, and a manifest declares only content-file paths, never types.

docs.title: 3.1 IndexManifest
docs.text:
public record IndexManifest(boolean declaredOnRegister, boolean declaredOnReload,
                            List<String> onRegisterPaths, List<String> onReloadPaths)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:344

The parsed result of one manifest, not yet consumed. empty() (:347, package-visible) returns a "nothing declared" instance, used when the manifest file as a whole cannot be read.

Member Meaning declaredOnRegister on_register appears as an array (an empty array counts too, D2) declaredOnReload on_reload appears as an array onRegisterPaths The entries of on_register, in file order onReloadPaths The entries of on_reload, in file order

docs.title: 3.2 ResolvedIndex
docs.text:
public record ResolvedIndex(boolean declaredOnRegister, boolean declaredOnReload,
                            List<String> onRegisterPaths, List<String> onReloadPaths)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:362
// public boolean nothingDeclared()   // :365

The result of aggregating all of one mod's manifests and removing cross-domain conflicts. nothingDeclared() is the D4 test: when it is true, no manifest ever declared either domain, so the caller must return immediately and register nothing.

docs.title: 3.3 parseIndexManifest
docs.text:
public static IndexManifest parseIndexManifest(String modId, String label, JsonObject root)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:222

Responsibility: parse one in-memory manifest, consuming no file. It has no NeoForge dependency and can be called from pure JVM tests.

Constraints: a null root is treated as an empty file. Only on_register and on_reload are recognized; any other top-level field goes down the unknown-field path and is reported (see 3.6). The return value is never null.

Failure behavior: every violation is recorded as an ERROR and put into the modId bucket, with no exception thrown; within one call, one broken field does not implicate its sibling fields (D3).

docs.title: 3.4 resolveIndexManifests
docs.text:
public static ResolvedIndex resolveIndexManifests(String modId, List<IndexManifest> manifests)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:294

Responsibility: aggregate all of one mod's manifests, run the cross-domain fail-closed check, and return the paths each domain can consume. A pure function, testable.

Constraint: manifests is passed in load order, and the aggregation keeps that order.

Failure behavior:

  • The same path appearing in both on_register and on_reload (within one manifest or across manifests, both count) is reported as an ERROR and put into the bucket (D6), and is removed from both domains, so neither consumes it.
  • When no manifest declares either domain, one aggregate WARN is recorded plus a bucket entry (D4), and the returned nothingDeclared() is true.

docs.title: 3.5 listIndexFiles
docs.text:
public static List<Path> listIndexFiles(Path indexDir, String modId)   // JsonTreeBuilder.java:762

Responsibility: list the files under the index directory that end in .json, sorted by path string.

Failure behavior: when the directory cannot be listed, an ERROR is recorded and put into the bucket, and an empty list is returned. An empty result is itself a legal result (it means there are no manifests) and is judged separately by buildForMod.

docs.title: 3.6 How D1 to D6 show up at the API layer
docs.text:
The rule numbers follow the design document. Each corresponds to one testable behavior:

Rule Meaning Where it lands D1 Both fields are individually optional; when neither appears (an empty file, or a file with unknown fields only) an error is reported and nothing is consumed parseIndexManifest:240-244 D2 An empty array is legal and counts as "declared" parseIndexManifest:237, the resolveIndexManifests:323 branch D3 An unknown top-level field is reported and processing continues; a field that is not an array is reported and its sibling fields are still processed parseIndexManifest:226-230, readPathArray:256-277 D4 The aggregate warning branches on "which field was declared", not on the entries that were parsed out resolveIndexManifests:323-326 D5 sources is not an alias; it is reported as an unknown field goes through parseIndexManifest:226-230 D6 A path listed in both arrays fails closed, and neither domain consumes it resolveIndexManifests:308-316

readPathArray (:256) is private: a field that exists but is not an array, or an array element that is not a string, each records one ERROR and a bucket entry, without implicating sibling fields.

docs.title: 3.7 The deprecated field
docs.text: The old index field was named sources. After the hard migration (D5) it is no longer a legal field: writing sources goes down the unknown-field path, reports contains unsupported field 'sources' and puts a bucket entry in, and that manifest declares no domain. The only legal domain fields today are on_register and on_reload.

docs.title: 3.8 Path contract
docs.text:
public static String validateSourcePath(String path)              // JsonTreeBuilder.java:383
public static String[] indexDirectorySegments(String modId)       // JsonTreeBuilder.java:745

validateSourcePath: content-file path validation. Returning null means legal; otherwise it returns a human-readable reason. Rules: non-empty, no leading /, ends in .json, no empty segment, no ./.. segment. A path is resolved relative to data/<mod>/. A pure function with no NeoForge dependency.

indexDirectorySegments: returns the segment array of the index directory relative to the mod file root, fixed at {"data", modId, "kasuga_lib", "data_driven"}. Every call returns a new array, so a caller's modification cannot pollute other callers. ReloadOrchestrator.indexResourcePath drops the first two segments to get the pack-stack path kasuga_lib/data_driven.

docs.title: 4.1 parseSource (private)
docs.text:
parseSource (:395) reads and parses one content file by path:

  1. Validate with validateSourcePath; if illegal, record an ERROR and a bucket entry, then return.
  2. Deduplicate by path string using the parsedSources set; the same content file is parsed only once per buildForMod, even when several manifests reference it.
  3. Locate the mod file with findModFile, concatenate data/<modId>/<sourcePath>, and read it.
  4. A missing file records a Source file not found ERROR and a bucket entry.
  5. A read/parse exception records an ERROR and a bucket entry (:431-434).
  6. Hand it to dispatchContent.

docs.title: 4.2 dispatchContent (private)
docs.text:
dispatchContent (:461) dispatches a content file to handlers by top-level field:

  • First collect the names of all handlers with getParentTypeName() == null into knownFields, and put every embedded handler into embeddedByField keyed by typeName.
  • Every top-level field not in knownFields is reported as an error and put into the bucket. If that field name happens to be an embedded type, the message adds a hint naming which key of which parent entry it should be written into (:475-490).
  • Each unknown-field message also appends a conditional hint (D9): if these fields belong to reload-domain content (written as a state_machines array, for instance), list the file under on_reload instead (:483-490).
  • For every known top-level handler: the field must be an array and its elements must be objects; otherwise each is reported as an error, put into the bucket, and skipped.
  • Embedded types enter only through extractEmbedded(parentJson) and do not take a top-level dispatch slot (:528-535).

docs.title: 4.3 parseContentBody
docs.text:
public static Map<String, List<Object>> parseContentBody(String modId, String contentLabel, JsonObject root)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:620

Responsibility: the in-memory half of the content pipeline. parseSource handles location and reading, and hands the body to it once read. Returns an immutable map grouped by "handler typeName to definition list", preserving dispatch order.

Constraints and failure behavior: parse and collect only; no registration, no apply. Every malformed input is reported through the bucket rather than thrown; the caller gets back the part that could still be parsed (partial-apply semantics). No NeoForge dependency, so it can be called directly from pure JVM tests.

docs.title: 4.4 applyUnchecked
docs.text:
public static void applyUnchecked(TypeHandler handler, Object definition, BuildContext context, String modId)
// JsonTreeBuilder.java:712

Responsibility: run one handler.apply and turn an exception into a bucket diagnostic.

Constraint: buildForMod calls it for every surviving definition. On an exception it records the Failed to apply '<type>' handler for mod '<mod>' ERROR and puts the wrapped IllegalStateException into the bucket (the original exception is kept as the cause). It is public because the contract "a failed apply must leave a trace" could otherwise only be exercised by a full mod load.

docs.title: 5. Conflict resolution
docs.text: Duplicate ids are resolved before any apply side effect, so that MappedRegistry never sees a duplicate key.

docs.title: 5.1 DuplicateIdResolver
docs.text:
dedup/DuplicateIdResolver.java, a pure function with no Minecraft types.

public record Candidate(String typeName, String identity, String sourcePath, Object payload)  // :39
public record Conflict(Candidate loser, Candidate winner)                                     // :47
public record Result(List<Candidate> winners, List<Conflict> conflicts)                       // :65
public static Result resolve(List<Candidate> candidates)                                      // :73
public static String describe(Conflict conflict)                                              // :109
public static Throwable toLoadingError(Conflict conflict)                                     // :124
  • A null Candidate.identity opts out of deduplication: it is always a winner and conflicts with no entry.
  • The conflict key is (typeName, identity). Different typeName values never conflict.
  • resolve is last-wins: for the same key it takes the one appearing last in the candidate sequence. The sequence order is the load order, and the method does not sort internally.
  • describe / toLoadingError produce human-readable messages, containing the type field, the identity, and the source file of the loser and of the winner.

docs.title: 5.2 EffectiveId
docs.text:
public static String of(String modId, String rawId)   // EffectiveId.java:39

Responsibility: normalize a raw id to the ResourceLocation string it finally registers under, for deduplication comparison.

Raw id Normalized result foo <modId>:foo minecraft:foo <modId>:foo othermod:foo othermod:foo (verbatim)

When rawId is null, returns null. It splits namespace and path on the first : only.

docs.title: 5.3 Per-type identity
docs.text:
Type identity Source blocks / items the normalized effective id RegTypeHandler.resolveIdentity (RegTypeHandler.java:58) block_entities the host block's effective id BlockEntityTypeHandler.resolveIdentity (:66) registry_groups the raw id string, not normalized RegistryGroupHandler.resolveIdentity (:50) A custom handler TypeHandler.resolveIdentity returns null by default, i.e. it takes no part in deduplication TypeHandler.java:64

Why registry_groups is not normalized: groups do not go into an MC registry, and the loader references them by raw string everywhere (a block's registry_group lookup, store's putRegistryGroup), so normalizing only the decision key would produce a mismatch where a duplicate is decided but the reference cannot be found.

docs.title: 5.4 last-wins order
docs.text:
resolveDuplicates (:652) builds candidates in the load order of parsed:

  1. Index files by ascending filename;
  2. within one manifest, by the writing order of the on_register array;
  3. within one content file, by the writing order of the type-field arrays;
  4. embedded block_entities follow the position of the host blocks entry.

Result: a loser never enters apply at all, and the registry sees the winner exactly once; each conflict records one WARN and goes into that mod's bucket as an IllegalStateException; there is also a summary Resolved N duplicate id(s) WARN. When identity resolution fails it degrades to null and does not escape (identityOf, :691).

Other pages in the data-driven section: Registration-phase API · Extension API · Diagnostics API · Reload API · Section index

docs.title: Data-Driven Reload API (Including the Assertable Pure-Function Surface and Call Examples)
13. Reload API
docs.text: The reload domain is orchestrated by data-driven's ReloadOrchestrator, and the extension point is ReloadHandler (symmetric with TypeHandler in the registration phase). The orchestrator does not know any type name — it walks ReloadHandlerRegistry and treats each handler's typeName() as a legal top-level key.

docs.title: 13.1 ReloadHandler (the Extension Point)
docs.text:
reload/ReloadHandler.java:41. One handler owns the decode/register of one reload type; functionally it corresponds to that type's "old decoder + registration step + wrap-up validation".

public interface ReloadHandler<T> {
    String typeName();                                    // :50 top-level key, also the dedup collision space
    default String describeFile() { return "reload-domain file"; }  // :60 the noun used in decode diagnostics
    default Set<String> globDirectories() { return Set.of(); }      // :72 default empty = index only
    void clearBucket();                                   // :85 once per cycle, before register
    Decoded<T> decode(JsonObject root);                   // :97 pure decode; delegates to the existing decodeFile
    void register(T payload);                             // :107 registers the last-wins winner
    default void afterReload(List<Reloaded<T>> registered) {}  // :117 cross-type validation
}
Method Responsibility and constraints Failure behavior typeName() The top-level JSON key it claims, e.g. "state_machines"; unique in the registry, and also the collision space for deduplication A later registration under the same name replaces the earlier one in place describeFile() The noun used in decode diagnostics, e.g. "state machine file" → "Failed to decode state machine file '<path>'" Defaults to "reload-domain file"; a handler whose diagnostic text is pinned by a test should override it globDirectories() Extra directories under data/<ns>/ discovered by directory glob; default empty = index-only Return an ordered collection so that discovery order is preserved clearBucket() Once per cycle, before discovery. Drops only the reload source ("script wins"), so it delegates to the bucket's clearResource() An exception is isolated in place by the orchestrator (runClear, :250-261) and recorded under Domain.RELOAD_DATA; the other handlers carry on decode(root) root is guaranteed to be a JSON object. Must not read files (the orchestrator owns I/O) and must not throw for malformed content (return it as Decoded.errors()) A thrown exception is isolated per file and recorded by the orchestrator register(payload) Called only for the last-wins winner, and only after the whole discovery round has finished You should throw (the orchestrator isolates it and attributes it by namespace); do not swallow afterReload(registered) Called once every handler's registration stage is done, and only for the entries registered this round; cross-type validation belongs here A thrown exception is attributed to the library mod (KasugaLib.MODID) and does not block later handlers

docs.title: 13.2 ReloadHandlerRegistry
docs.text:
reload/ReloadHandlerRegistry.java:27. ReloadHandlerRegistry is the reload-side counterpart of TypeHandlerRegistry: static, indexed by typeName(), order-preserving via LinkedHashMap.

public static void register(ReloadHandler<?> handler);       // :37
public static ReloadHandler<?> get(String typeName);         // :45
public static Collection<ReloadHandler<?>> all();            // :50 immutable view, keeps registration order
public static void clearForTest();                           // :58 test only, never called in production
  • Order carries weight: the orchestrator walks all() to decide the dispatch order and the register order, and together they decide cross-type last-wins. If you need a specific order (for example state machines before clips), register in that order.
  • Registration is idempotent by type name: registering the same typeName again replaces it in place and keeps the original position; a @Context bean re-running in tests therefore does not produce duplicate keys.
  • clearForTest() is a hook for tests (TypeHandlerRegistry has no counterpart, so handlers registered by a test leak into later tests, a documented design pitfall); production code does not call it.

docs.title: 13.3 Decoded / Entry
docs.text:
reload/Decoded.java:19. The result of one decode: the decoded entries plus human-readable diagnostics.

public record Decoded<T>(List<Entry<T>> entries, List<String> errors) {   // :19
    public record Entry<T>(String id, T payload) {}                        // :28
    public static <T> Decoded<T> empty();                                  // :36
}
  • Entry.id is the entry's effective id within the handler type (the key for the deduplication decision); payload is the value handed back to register. The handler picks the identity itself; the orchestrator never knows how a handler assembles the id.
  • Whole file rejected → only errors; entries is empty.

docs.title: 13.4 Reloaded
docs.text:
reload/Reloaded.java:14. A payload that passed deduplication and has been handed to register, plus the namespace it came from. The orchestrator carries it through the wrap-up stage so that the handler's afterReload can attribute diagnostics to the mod that produced the entry — a generic handler cannot get that namespace from the payload itself.

public record Reloaded<T>(String modId, T payload) {}

docs.title: 13.5 ReloadOrchestrator
docs.text:
reload/ReloadOrchestrator.java:121. It implements ScopedResourceManagerConsumer and ScopedResourcePackListener and is the only orchestrator in the reload domain. The DI entry point ReloadOrchestrator() (:133) registers into ResourceSystem through init() (:155); the host entry point ReloadOrchestrator(ReloadHandler<?>...) (:145) first registers the handlers passed in, then runs cycles — tests, or a host that brings its own buckets, use it to bypass the modelling-side registrar bean.

public ReloadOrchestrator()                                      // :133 DI entry point
public ReloadOrchestrator(ReloadHandler<?>... handlers)          // :145 registers, then runs
public void reload(ResourceManager resourceManager)              // :186
public static String indexResourcePath(String modId)             // :290
  • The set of top-level keys is no longer a hard-coded constant: it is derived by knownTypeNames() (:473) from ReloadHandlerRegistry.all(). Adding a type = registering a handler, not editing the orchestrator.
  • The registration-type examples in the D9 reverse hint are derived by registrationFieldsExample() (:488) from TypeHandlerRegistry.all() (a top-level registration type = a handler with no parent); nothing is invented when the registry is empty.
  • reload(ResourceManager) is the per-cycle entry point, wrapped in a final fallback catch (:188-190): every RuntimeException that escapes the guards of the individual stages is attributed to the library's own mod id (KasugaLib.MODID) and recorded in a bucket. Because the method sits on the reload listener path and the buckets were already cleared before that stage, exceptions must not escape.
  • indexResourcePath(modId) drops the first two segments from JsonTreeBuilder.indexDirectorySegments(modId) and returns the pack-stack path kasuga_lib/data_driven. It shares the same source as the registration side's directory spelling.

The stage order of one cycle (runCycle, :194):

  1. Build the cycle: create one HandlerCycle per handler in the registry (:199-201).
  2. Clear the buckets: call runClear(entry) → clearBucket() for each handler, exactly once per round (:213-215; runClear, :250-261). Only the reload source is cleared, so entries registered by a script or by code are untouched; an exception thrown by one clearBucket() is isolated in place and recorded, while the other handlers clear as usual.
  3. Aggregate the glob directories: collect each handler's globDirectories() into a deduplicated ordered set (:222-225); a directory shared by two handlers is listed once, and files are routed by their top-level key.
  4. Per-namespace discovery (collectNamespace, :266): first readReloadPaths reads that namespace's index manifest on_reload, then collectGlob (:348-367) scans the aggregated directories (skipping paths already listed by an index), and finally collectIndex (:369) reads the files that on_reload points to.
  5. Registration stage: call register(entry) for each handler (:507-526), in registry order; glob candidates come first and index candidates after (HandlerCycle.candidates(), :595). Within the same type the later entry is last-wins.
  6. Wrap-up stage: call runAfterReload(entry) for each handler (:530-538), only for the entries actually registered this round, and after all the registers have completed — only then can a cross-type validation see another handler's bucket.

Dispatch (dispatch, :429): routing by top-level key. An unknown top-level key is reported as an error first, with the D9 reverse hint attached (:439-446); for every non-unknown key, each handler is checked in turn for root.has(typeName()), and on a hit the content is decoded, wrapping the Decoded.Entry into DuplicateIdResolver.Candidate(typeName, id, label, new Reloaded<>(namespace, payload)).

Deduplication (resolveAndReport, :545): uses the shared DuplicateIdResolver. The loser never enters the handler's register ("loser never has a side effect"), and each conflict logs a WARN plus one bucket entry, attributed to the mod the loser lives in.

Neither indexResourcePath nor runCycle has any special dependency beyond Minecraft; reload needs a ResourceManager.

docs.title: 13.6 Exception Guards
docs.text:
Four layers of participant-level guards plus one fallback layer:

Layer Scope Source Per handler, bucket clearing clearBucket() throws runClear:250-261 Per file Read and decode exceptions, including the decoder itself throwing readAndDispatch:405-415 Per namespace The discovery mechanism itself (directory glob, manifest read) throws collectNamespace:266-288 Per entry Registering a single entry throws register:507-526 Per handler, wrap-up afterReload throws runAfterReload:530-538 Fallback Exceptions none of the above could attribute reload:186-193

When every entry in a cycle fails, the bucket stays in its cleared state, and that is intentional: empty is the truthful outcome, and the errors are in the diagnostics bucket.

docs.title: 13.7 StateMachineDefinitionLoader
docs.text:
It stays in modelling, demoted to a pure file-level decoder: it no longer holds a listener, does not clear buckets, and does not list files (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.java:14-33).

public static final String PATH = "state_machines";                     // :39
public static final String FIELD_STATE_MACHINES = "state_machines";     // :42
public record DecodedFile(List<StateMachineDefinition> definitions, List<String> errors) {}  // :55
public static DecodedFile decodeFile(JsonElement json);                  // :67

StateMachineDefinitionLoader's directory-listing method has been removed (0 callers). The directory glob is now done by ReloadOrchestrator's own collectGlob (:348-367) using ResourceManager.listResources, and FsmReloadHandler.globDirectories() (:69-71) declares the directories to scan; StateMachineDefinitionLoader.PATH (:39) is kept so that globDirectories() can reference it.

decodeFile: the file shape is {"state_machines": [ <definition>, ... ]}. A non-object root, a missing top-level key, or a non-array value all reject the whole file and return one error; extra top-level keys no longer reject the file (a genuinely unknown key is reported by the orchestrator, and this decoder only ignores it), while a non-object array element or a failed decode skips only that element and the siblings carry on as usual. An empty returned errors means the file is clean. It is now called through by FsmReloadHandler.decode; the orchestrator no longer knows it directly.

docs.title: 13.8 AnimationClipLoader
docs.text:
Likewise a pure file-level component (AnimationClipLoader.java:14-39).

public static final String FIELD_ANIMATION_CLIPS = "animation_clips";   // :45
public record DecodedFile(List<AnimationClip> clips, List<String> errors) {}  // :57
public static DecodedFile decodeFile(JsonElement json);                  // :69
public static void register(FsmAnimationClips clips, AnimationClip clip);// :113

decodeFile: the shape is {"animation_clips": [ <clip>, ... ]}, and the failure-isolation rules are the same as in StateMachineDefinitionLoader.decodeFile. A clip's id is carried by the element's own id field (AnimationClip.CODEC reads it), and there is no separate id key; keys the record does not name are ignored by the codec, so comment-like fields can be written. Called through by FsmClipsReloadHandler.decode.

register: writes the decoded clip into the RESOURCE half of the bucket by calling clips.registerResource. When clips or clip is null it is a no-op. It is now called through by FsmClipsReloadHandler.register. Animation clip files can arrive only through on_reload; there is no animation_clips/ directory glob.

docs.title: 13.9 The Two Modelling-Side Handlers and the Registrar Bean
docs.text:
These three classes live in modelling's lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.dynamic.fsm package. They are consumers and did not move into data-driven along with the orchestrator:

Class typeName Discovery Role FsmReloadHandler (:42) state_machines glob state_machines/ decode → StateMachineDefinitionLoader.decodeFile; register writes the RESOURCE half of FsmDefinitions; afterReload runs the dangling clip check FsmClipsReloadHandler (:24) animation_clips index-only (keeps the default empty set) decode → AnimationClipLoader.decodeFile; register → AnimationClipLoader.register FsmReloadHandlerRegistrar (:23) — — @Context + @PostConstruct (:25-31), registering the two handlers into ReloadHandlerRegistry in fsm → clips order, bound to the process-level FsmRegistries.GLOBAL bucket

docs.title: 13.10 FsmDefinitions and FsmAnimationClips
docs.text:
Both bucketed storage classes live in render-core. Each bucket splits by source into RESOURCE (the reload path, which clearResource can drop) and SCRIPT (the runtime/script path, which survives reloads).

FsmAnimationClips (FsmAnimationClips.java:30):

public enum ClipSource { RESOURCE, SCRIPT }                              // :35
public record Entry(AnimationSampler<?> sampler, Object data, ClipSource source) {}  // :43
public void register(Id id, AnimationSampler<?> sampler, Object data)    // :53
public void registerResource(Id id, AnimationSampler<?> sampler, Object data)  // :66
public Entry get(Id id)                                                  // :87
public boolean remove(Id id)                                             // :92
public void clearResource()                                              // :100
public void clearAll()                                                   // :108
public void clear()                                                      // :117
  • register writes a SCRIPT entry and replaces a same-id RESOURCE entry with a WARN (script wins).
  • registerResource writes a RESOURCE entry and does not override a same-id SCRIPT entry; a later RESOURCE overrides an earlier one.
  • get returns null when nothing is found; it also returns null when the id is null.
  • register / registerResource throw IllegalArgumentException for a null id, sampler, or data (validate:76).
  • clearResource clears RESOURCE only; clearAll clears everything; clear() is an alias for clearResource() and no longer clears code-registered entries.

FsmDefinitions (FsmDefinitions.java:27) is isomorphic: register (SCRIPT, :59), registerResource (RESOURCE, :71), clearResource (:84), clearAll (:95), remove (:107), get (:116), hash (:126), addListener (:142). An identity change (override, removal, clearing) notifies the InvalidationListener. hash(id) returns the content hash, 0 when absent, for the sync layer's identity check.

script-wins is a write-side invariant: a single map plus the guard in registerResource; get is an ordinary query, and the result does not depend on registration order.

docs.title: 14. The Pure-Function Surface Assertable from Tests
docs.text:
The APIs below have no NeoForge dependency or can be called on a plain JVM; they are exposed specifically so that tests can assert the contract:

API What it asserts JsonTreeBuilder.indexDirectorySegments The index directory segment array; pins the spelling and the levels JsonTreeBuilder.validateSourcePath Content path rules JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest Index schema D1 through D5 JsonTreeBuilder.resolveIndexManifests Aggregation D4 and the dual-listing fail-closed D6 JsonTreeBuilder.parseContentBody Content dispatch, embedded types, partial apply, the D9 hint JsonTreeBuilder.listIndexFiles The failure branches and the ordering of the directory scan JsonTreeBuilder.applyUnchecked A failed apply landing in the bucket DuplicateIdResolver.resolve / describe / toLoadingError last-wins and the conflict messages EffectiveId.of The id normalization table Diagnostics methods spanning both dimensions Two-dimension isolation, clearing, the summarize format DataDiagnosticsCommands.kasugaDataCommand The shape of the command tree ReloadOrchestrator.reload / indexResourcePath The reload cycle, the two entry points, cross-entry deduplication, diagnostics A ReloadHandler implementation (fixture) Wiring in a new reload type: ReloadHandlerExtensionPointTest uses a fake handler to assert dispatch/dedup/registration and the after-stage order ReloadHandlerRegistry.register / all / clearForTest Registry order preservation, same-name replacement, test isolation StateMachineDefinitionLoader.decodeFile The wrapper-layer decode contract (the directory glob is the job of ReloadOrchestrator.collectGlob; the decoder no longer lists files) AnimationClipLoader.decodeFile / register Animation clip file decoding and script-wins registration ContentStructure.body / unknownKeys / field / joinWithOr / describe Shared structural decisions: the body check, unknown keys, field splitting (Field/Element), hint joining, the type description

docs.title: 15. Call Examples
docs.text:
Every snippet below compiles against the current signatures. Each one names the real test case it imitates, with the test class in parentheses.

Register a mod and check the error bucket afterwards (imitating JsonTreeBuilderIndexPathTest.contentTestingIndexLoadsWithoutErrors):

import java.util.List;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.builder.JsonTreeBuilder;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.context.JsonRegistryGroup;

JsonTreeBuilder.clearLoadingErrors("kasuga_lib");
JsonRegistryGroup root = JsonTreeBuilder.buildForMod("kasuga_lib");
// a null root means no on_register content was declared; when non-null it is the root group hanging off the mod's registration tree
List<Throwable> errors = JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors("kasuga_lib");

Parse one index manifest and aggregate it (imitating JsonTreeBuilderIndexSchemaTest.declaringNeitherDomainIsReportedAndConsumesNothing and crossListedPathIsConsumedByNeitherDomain):

import java.util.List;
import com.google.gson.JsonObject;
import com.google.gson.JsonParser;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.builder.JsonTreeBuilder;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.builder.JsonTreeBuilder.IndexManifest;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.builder.JsonTreeBuilder.ResolvedIndex;

JsonObject doc = JsonParser.parseString(
        "{\"on_register\": [\"carriages/m1/blocks.json\"]}").getAsJsonObject();
IndexManifest manifest = JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest("kuayue", "index.json", doc);
ResolvedIndex index = JsonTreeBuilder.resolveIndexManifests("kuayue", List.of(manifest));
if (!index.nothingDeclared()) {
    for (String path : index.onRegisterPaths()) {
        // path is relative to data/kuayue/ and has passed the dual-listing fail-closed check
    }
}

Parse a content file only, without registering (imitating JsonTreeBuilderEmbeddedTypeDispatchTest.topLevelEmbeddedTypeIsReportedAndTheRestOfTheFileStillDispatches):

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Map;
import com.google.gson.JsonObject;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.builder.JsonTreeBuilder;

JsonObject body = /* an already-parsed content file */ new JsonObject();
Map<String, List<Object>> collected =
        JsonTreeBuilder.parseContentBody("kuayue", "carriages/m1/blocks.json", body);
// the keys of collected are the handlers' typeName; parse errors go to JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors("kuayue")

Write to and read the diagnostics bucket (imitating DiagnosticsTest.modDimensionIsTheExistingBucket and summarizePrintsOneLinePerNonEmptyBucketDeterministically):

import java.util.List;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.builder.JsonTreeBuilder;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.diagnostics.Diagnostics;

Diagnostics.report("kuayue", new IllegalStateException("boom"));
List<Throwable> perMod = Diagnostics.errors("kuayue");
// perMod is the same bucket as JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors("kuayue")
List<String> lines = Diagnostics.summarize();   // one line each: "<mod>: N error(s)" (mod dimension) or "<DOMAIN>[<key>]: N error(s)" (source dimension)
Diagnostics.clear("kuayue");

Register and run the diagnostics command (imitating DataDiagnosticsCommandsTest.onRegisterCommandsRegistersKasugaDataErrorsIntoTheDispatcher):

import com.mojang.brigadier.CommandDispatcher;
import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.diagnostics.DataDiagnosticsCommands;
import net.minecraft.commands.CommandSourceStack;
import net.minecraft.commands.Commands;
import net.neoforged.neoforge.event.RegisterCommandsEvent;

CommandDispatcher<CommandSourceStack> dispatcher = new CommandDispatcher<>();
DataDiagnosticsCommands.onRegisterCommands(
        new RegisterCommandsEvent(dispatcher, Commands.CommandSelection.ALL, null));
dispatcher.execute("kasuga_data errors kuayue", source);   // source needs permission >= 2

Run one reload cycle (imitating ReloadOrchestratorTest.loadsValidDefinitionsIntoInjectedBucket):

import lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.reload.ReloadOrchestrator;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.dynamic.fsm.FsmClipsReloadHandler;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.dynamic.fsm.FsmReloadHandler;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.dynamic.fsm.FsmAnimationClips;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.dynamic.fsm.FsmDefinitions;
import net.minecraft.server.packs.resources.ResourceManager;

FsmDefinitions definitions = new FsmDefinitions();
FsmAnimationClips clips = new FsmAnimationClips();
// the varargs constructor registers these two handlers into ReloadHandlerRegistry; that order is the dispatch/register order
ReloadOrchestrator orchestrator = new ReloadOrchestrator(
        new FsmReloadHandler(definitions, clips), new FsmClipsReloadHandler(clips));
orchestrator.reload(resourceManager);   // one cycle: clear buckets, dual-entry discovery, deduplicated registration, wrap-up validation

The orchestrator has moved to lib.kasuga.registration.data_driven.reload (data-driven), while the two handlers stay in modelling's lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.dynamic.fsm, so this example imports both packages. In tests the varargs constructor brings its own buckets; in production the handlers are registered by FsmReloadHandlerRegistrar and the DI constructor runs with no arguments.

Decode and register animation clips (imitating AnimationClipLoaderTest.decodesTheWrappedClipArray; the registration call is made by the orchestrator):

import com.google.gson.JsonParser;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.dynamic.fsm.AnimationClipLoader;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.dynamic.animation.AnimationClip;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.dynamic.fsm.FsmAnimationClips;

FsmAnimationClips clips = new FsmAnimationClips();
AnimationClipLoader.DecodedFile decoded =
        AnimationClipLoader.decodeFile(JsonParser.parseString(json));
for (AnimationClip clip : decoded.clips()) {
    AnimationClipLoader.register(clips, clip);   // writes the RESOURCE half; a SCRIPT entry with the same id is not overwritten
}

docs.title: Reference Usage Notes
docs.text:
parseContentBody, parseIndexManifest, resolveIndexManifests, DuplicateIdResolver, and EffectiveId are all pure functions and can be asserted directly in an ordinary JUnit test with no NeoForge runtime. buildForMod, buildAll, ReloadOrchestrator.reload, and the registration side of FsmAnimationClips need a mod or game runtime; buildForMod-style tests usually guard with Assumptions.assumeTrue (see JsonTreeBuilderIndexPathTest, JsonTreeBuilderLoadingErrorTest).

Other pages in the data-driven series: Registration API · Extension API · Diagnostics API · Reload API · Series index

docs.title: Data-driven JSON format specification (schema)
docs.text: Type: Reference (information-oriented, for looking things up). Applies to: Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.203, Parchment 2024.11.17, Java 21. The format described on this page holds only within this version range. Code baseline: KasugaLibNext branch model-loader, verification date 2026-10-04, baseline commit ec864a1. Line numbers in this page refer to the current working tree (the uncommitted data-driven reimplementation). Authoritative source: the rules on this page come from the current code and tests. The old sources layout has been migrated to the index manifest; each rule gives the class, line number, or test name so you can check it yourself.

docs.title: 0.1 Three concepts you must keep apart
docs.text:
• registration phase: the phase during mod startup and construction in which objects are written into MC registries (such as BuiltInRegistries.BLOCK); the source it reads is the mod jar, it completes once, and it cannot hot reload.
  • reload phase: the resource re-read triggered by /reload; the source it reads is the pack stack, and data packs can override it.
  • index file (index manifest): a .json under data/<namespace>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/ that declares only which content files belong to which domain; it contains no registration objects of its own.

A mod's index files can declare only the registration domain, only the reload domain, or both.

docs.title: 0.2 What this page covers
docs.text:
Covered: the index file format; the registration-phase content file format (registry_groups / blocks / items / embedded block_entity); duplicate id rules; the wrapper format of reload-phase content files; the classification and outlets of errors.

Not covered: the concrete effect of each properties key in the registry (see guide-content.md); the complete codec fields inside state machine definitions and animation clip elements (see ../../reference/fsm.md and the codecs under uml/); TypeHandler extensions on the Java side (see guide-extension.md).

docs.title: 1.1 Location and discovery rules
docs.text:
The index directory is fixed at a 4-segment path:

data/<namespace>/kasuga_lib/data_driven/
  • Pinned by JsonTreeBuilder.indexDirectorySegments(modId), which returns {"data", modId, "kasuga_lib", "data_driven"} (JsonTreeBuilder.java:745-747).
  • Note that kasuga_lib is a fixed spelling and data_driven uses an underscore. Writing kasuga-lib, or dropping the kasuga_lib level, leads to silently loading 0 entries; that risk is pinned by JsonTreeBuilderIndexPathTest.indexDirectorySegmentsMatchCanonicalLayout() with assertArrayEquals (JsonTreeBuilderIndexPathTest.java:27-33).
  • Every .json file in the directory is treated as an index and read in ascending filename order (JsonTreeBuilder.listIndexFiles, :762-774; resolveIndexManifests aggregates in the order passed in). There is no filename convention; index.json is only a habit.
  • A missing directory only logs DEBUG and does not count as an error (JsonTreeBuilder.java:77).
  • The reload side reuses the same path segments when it reads the same directory (ReloadOrchestrator.indexResourcePath, :290).

docs.title: 1.2 Top-level fields
docs.text:
An index file has only two top-level fields, each a string array:

Field Type Domain Meaning on_register string[] registration phase Lists the content files parsed during mod construction and written into MC registries on_reload string[] reload phase Lists the content files parsed on /reload and written into the reload bucket

Both are optional, but at least one must appear (D1/D2). The field constants are in JsonTreeBuilder.java:40,42; parsing is in parseIndexManifest (:222-250).

A legal index declaring both domains:

{
  "on_register": [
    "kasuga_lib_content/blocks.json",
    "kasuga_lib_content/groups.json"
  ],
  "on_reload": [
    "state_machines/panel.json",
    "animation_clips/wheel.json"
  ]
}

docs.title: 1.3 sources is removed (breaking change)
docs.text:
sources is now an illegal field. It is no longer recognized and has no alias any more; it goes down the "unknown top-level field" path: an error is logged plus a bucket entry, and the file thereby "declares nothing" (which logs another "neither is declared" error).

{
  "sources": ["kasuga_lib_content/blocks.json"]
}

The example above produces two errors: (1) contains unsupported field 'sources'; (2) declares neither 'on_register' nor 'on_reload'. For the code see JsonTreeBuilder.parseIndexManifest (:226-230 unknown field, :240-244 neither declared); it is pinned by JsonTreeBuilderIndexSchemaTest.legacySourcesFieldIsReportedAsUnknown().

The old sources field and the old flat layout data/<namespace>/kasugalib/ were both removed by a hard migration, with no compatibility window. If the old directory exists on disk and there is no new index directory, one WARN is logged plus a bucket entry, hinting at migration to on_register (JsonTreeBuilder.java:65-79).

docs.title: 1.4 Field-level rules D1–D6
docs.text:
The executable version of these rules is JsonTreeBuilderIndexSchemaTest (8 cases, see section 6). The rules are implemented in parseIndexManifest (single file) and resolveIndexManifests (aggregation across files).

  • D1 Declare at least one field: neither field appears (an empty file, or a file with unknown fields only) → error + bucket entry, and the file contributes no paths. An empty file (GSON parses it as null) is reported too (JsonTreeBuilder.java:240-244; tests declaringNeitherDomainIsReportedAndConsumesNothing / emptyFileIsReportedInsteadOfSilentlyIgnored).
  • D2 An empty array is legal: {"on_register": []} is legal and counts as declared (JsonTreeBuilder.java:237; test emptyArrayIsValidAndCountsAsDeclared).
  • D3 A failure in one field does not implicate its sibling: when on_register is not an array only that field is reported and on_reload is still read, and the other way round (readPathArray, :256-277; test nonArrayFieldDoesNotAbortTheSibling). A non-string element in the array is reported and skipped, and the remaining elements are kept (:268-274).
  • D4 The aggregate warning branches on "was anything ever declared": a pure reload mod that declares only on_reload does not raise "registration domain not declared"; only when no file declares either field does the aggregation stage record one WARN + one bucket entry (resolveIndexManifests, :323-326; test pureReloadModDoesNotRaiseTheAggregateError). When every file at the single-file level fails its declaration, the aggregate error is still raised (test allBrokenSchemaStillRaisesTheAggregateError).
  • D5 sources is an unknown field, not an alias (:226-230; test legacySourcesFieldIsReportedAsUnknown).
  • D6 A path listed in both arrays fails closed: the same path (within one file or across files) appearing in both arrays → error + bucket entry, and that path is consumed by neither domain (it is deleted from both lists). The check spans all index files of that mod (resolveIndexManifests, :308-316; test crossListedPathIsConsumedByNeitherDomain).

docs.title: 1.5 Path entry rules
docs.text:
Array elements are paths relative to data/<namespace>/ and must carry the .json suffix. Validation is in JsonTreeBuilder.validateSourcePath (:383-392), and the reload side reuses the same function (ReloadOrchestrator.collectIndex, :369). Violating any rule → error + bucket entry, and that entry is skipped:

Rule Message fragment when violated Non-empty path is empty Does not start with / (must be relative) path must be relative Ends with .json path must include the '.json' suffix No empty segment (//) path contains an empty segment No . or .. segment path must not contain '.' or '..'

Also:

  • The fact that a path cannot cross namespaces is structural: parseSource always joins the path under data/<modId>/ (JsonTreeBuilder.java:414-420). For the same reason, an entry pointing at assets/ can never take effect.
  • The same path listed in several places within the same mod → silently deduplicated, parsed only once (parsedSources in parseSource, :404), with no error.
  • The reload side additionally requires the path to form a legal ResourceLocation (only [a-z0-9/._-] is allowed); illegal characters such as uppercase are reported separately (ReloadOrchestrator.java:369).
  • An illegal path, a missing file, and an unreadable JSON file all produce error + bucket entry (parseSource, :395-436).

docs.title: 1.6 Merging multiple manifests
docs.text: All index files of the same mod are fully read in first and then consumed together: paths are concatenated by "ascending index filename → array writing order within the file" (JsonTreeBuilder.java:92-96,296-301). That is why D6's double-listing check works across files, and why each content file is parsed at most once per load round.
