docs.title: 2.1 File top-level structure
docs.text:
In a content file the top-level field name is the top-level registration type, and the value must be an array of objects. There are currently 3 top-level types:

Top-level field handler phase Effect registry_groups RegistryGroupHandler 0 Establish property groups (parent/child) blocks BlockTypeHandler 1 Register blocks items ItemTypeHandler 1 Register standalone items

block_entities is not a top-level field; it is an embedded type, written as in section 2.5.

One content file can contain several top-level fields at once (for example one registry_groups set and one blocks set), dispatched one by one by dispatchContent (JsonTreeBuilder.java:461).

{
  "registry_groups": [
    { "id": "mymod:panels", "properties": { "no_occlusion": true } }
  ],
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:panel",
      "type": "simple_block",
      "registry_group": "mymod:panels",
      "properties": { "destroy_time": 2.0 },
      "item_properties": { "tab": "mymod:main" }
    }
  ]
}

Validation of top-level fields:

  • Unknown top-level field → error + bucket entry, and the remaining fields in the same file dispatch as usual (partial apply; JsonTreeBuilder.java:475-490).
  • A known field whose value is not an array → error + bucket entry, the remaining fields proceed as usual (:504-510).
  • An array element that is not a JSON object → error + bucket entry, that element is skipped, the remaining elements proceed as usual (:504-516).

docs.title: 2.2 registry_groups entries
docs.text:
Parsing is in RegistryGroupHandler.parse (RegistryGroupHandler.java:26-33), application in store (:54-90).

Field Type Required Default Meaning id string yes — Group id. Matched by the raw string, with no namespace normalization parent string no null → attached to the root group Parent group id; when the parent does not exist it falls back to the root group (:58-63) properties object no — Block properties passed down to child content (see section 2.6) item_properties object no — Item properties passed down to child content; tab is singled out as this group's creative tab (:73-76)
  • A group has no type field.
  • Blocks and items look their group up through registry_group using the raw string; therefore id is not normalized and mymod:panels and panels are two different groups (RegistryGroupHandler.resolveIdentity, :49-52).
  • Before applying, a topological sort is done by parent: parents before children; a cycle only gets a WARN, not an error, and falls back to the original order (JsonTreeBuilder.topoSortGroupDefs, :869).

docs.title: 2.3 blocks entries
docs.text:
Parsing is in BlockTypeHandler.parse (BlockTypeHandler.java:25-34), generic application in RegTypeHandler.apply (RegTypeHandler.java:62-112).

Field Type Required Default Meaning id string yes — Block id, either namespace:path or a bare path type string yes — Factory name, looked up in FactoryRegistry.BlockFactory (BlockTypeHandler.createRegistration, :59-64) registry_group string no null → attached to the root group Owning group id (raw-string match) properties object no — Block properties, see section 2.6 item_properties object no — Item properties for the block's item; tab decides the creative tab (BlockTypeHandler.resolveCreativeTab, :51-57) params object no null Passed to the factory verbatim by create(path, params) state_machine string no — Forwarded into the BE params only when the entry contains a block_entity (see section 2.5)
  • When id or type is missing, parse throws (json.get("id").getAsString()); the registration phase's element-level tolerance catches that exception → error + bucket entry, so only that entry is lost while sibling entries in the same file register as usual (JsonTreeBuilder produces entry <i> in '<key>' failed to parse: <msg>; entry skipped). Missing values for the other fields fall back to their defaults.
  • type finds no matching factory → only a WARN is logged, the entry is skipped, and it does not go into the bucket (RegTypeHandler.java:70-74).
  • Unknown keys inside the object are silently ignored (parse reads known keys only), the opposite of the error for an unknown top-level file key; see section 2.7.

docs.title: 2.4 items entries
docs.text:
Parsing is in ItemTypeHandler.parse (ItemTypeHandler.java:22-30).

Field Type Required Default Meaning id string yes — Item id type string yes — Factory name, looked up in FactoryRegistry.ItemFactory (:56-60) registry_group string no attached to the root group Owning group id properties object no — Item properties, see section 2.6; tab decides the creative tab (:48-53) params object no null Passed to the factory

docs.title: 2.5 block_entities (embedded type)
docs.text:
A block entity has no id of its own; it is carried by its host block, and the way to write one is to put a block_entity object inside that block's entry:

{
  "blocks": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:be_block",
      "type": "be_block",
      "block_entity": {
        "type": "test_be",
        "params": { "tick_interval": 4 }
      }
    }
  ]
}
  • The top-level field name is block_entities, but the embedded key name is block_entity (BlockEntityTypeHandler.getTypeName :21, getParentTypeName :27, getEmbeddedKeyName :30).
  • Extraction logic: BlockEntityTypeHandler.extractEmbedded (:33-44) injects the host block's id into the embedded object's _parent_block; if the host block has a top-level state_machine of JSON primitive type (string / number / boolean), it is forwarded into the embedded object's params.state_machine (:37-42). The test is isJsonPrimitive(), so number and boolean pass too, converted to text by getAsString() before being stored in params; objects, arrays, and null are ignored.

Fields of the embedded block_entity object:

Field Type Required Default Meaning type string yes — Block entity factory name, looked up in FactoryRegistry.BlockEntityFactory params object no null Passed to the factory; the common keys model / state_machine are interpreted by the concrete factory _parent_block string — injected Do not write this by hand; it is injected by extractEmbedded
  • Duplicate detection: two BE entries attached to the same host block count as duplicates (resolveIdentity, :66-68, using the host block's effective id).
  • Host block not found / unknown BE factory → only a WARN, no bucket entry (BlockEntityTypeHandler.apply, :75-86).

docs.title: 2.6 Inner keys of properties / item_properties
docs.text:
A top-level field's properties and item_properties are open objects whose keys are claimed by two parsers; an unknown key only gets a WARN and is ignored, never an error.

Block properties properties (JsonPropertyParser.buildCompilers, JsonPropertyParser.java:148-174):

Key Value type Key Value type no_occlusion bool light_emission int no_collision / no_collission (spelling alias) bool friction float requires_correct_tool bool speed_factor float replaceable bool jump_factor float dynamic_shape bool destroy_time float random_ticks bool explosion_resistance float no_loot_table bool strength float or a [destroy, resist] two-element array ignited_by_lava bool map_color DyeColor name (lowercase) liquid bool sound_type sound type name (see below) force_solid_on bool air bool no_terrain_particles bool
  • The legal values of sound_type come from JsonPropertyParser.buildSoundTypeMap (:97-146), such as stone / wood / metal / glass; an unknown value only warns.
  • map_color uses MC DyeColor names; an unknown value only warns.

Item properties item_properties (block entries) / properties (item entries) (JsonItemParser, JsonItemParser.java:20-36):

Key Value type Meaning stacks_to int Maximum stack size rarity string COMMON / UNCOMMON / RARE / EPIC (case-insensitive) fire_resistant bool Fire resistance durability int Durability no_repair bool Cannot be repaired tab string Creative tab ResourceLocation; consumed separately by the loader and not passed into the modifiers above

Properties are inherited along the parent chain, and a child entry overrides its parent (RegTypeHandler.apply sets registry_group as the parent, Reg.applyProperties applies parents before children).

docs.title: 2.7 Unknown keys inside an object vs unknown top-level file keys
docs.text:
The two positions differ in strictness, which is the difference easiest to trip over:

  • An unknown top-level file field → error + bucket entry (dispatchContent, JsonTreeBuilder.java:475-490). A misspelled blokcs is caught.
  • An unknown key inside an object → silently ignored (each handler's parse reads known keys only), with no error. For example, an extra foo in a block entry produces no diagnostic at all.

docs.title: 2.8 An embedded type written as a top-level field by mistake
docs.text:
Writing block_entities as a top-level field (instead of putting it in the block_entity key of a blocks entry) goes down the "unknown top-level field" path: error + bucket entry, with the message naming the block_entity key of a blocks entry as where it belongs, and the rest of the file's blocks dispatch as usual.

{
  "block_entities": [ { "type": "test_be" } ],
  "blocks": [ { "id": "mymod:ok", "type": "simple_block" } ]
}

The behavior is pinned by JsonTreeBuilderEmbeddedTypeDispatchTest.topLevelEmbeddedTypeIsReportedAndTheRestOfTheFileStillDispatches(). This covers only the case of writing an embedded type as a top-level field; if the embedded object itself fails to parse from a missing field, the exception is likewise caught by element-level tolerance, so only that embedded element is lost while the rest of the file's entries proceed as usual (the same as a missing id/type in section 2.3).

docs.title: 3. Duplicate ids and last-wins
docs.text: Deduplication happens before any registration side effect: once parsing has finished entirely the conflict is adjudicated first, and a loser never reaches apply at all (JsonTreeBuilder.resolveDuplicates, :652). This is because MC's MappedRegistry.register does not reject duplicate keys, and applying a duplicate would leave inconsistent entries (DuplicateIdResolver.java:11-14).

docs.title: 3.1 Determining identity
docs.text:
The conflict space is (typeName, identity); the same id under different types is not a conflict. The identity of each type (TypeHandler.resolveIdentity):

Type identity Normalization blocks / items EffectiveId.of(modId, id) No namespace or a minecraft: prefix → <modId>:path; other namespaces are kept verbatim block_entities the host block's effective id same as above registry_groups the raw id string not normalized

EffectiveId.of is at EffectiveId.java:39-52, with the table test EffectiveIdTest (unnamespacedIdsResolveUnderTheModNamespace / explicitMinecraftNamespaceResolvesToTheOwningMod / otherNamespacesAreKeptVerbatim).

docs.title: 3.2 What "last" means exactly
docs.text:
The "last" in last-wins is a position in the load sequence, not a path's lexicographic order:

  1. Between index files: ascending filename order;
  2. Within one index file: the writing order of the on_register array;
  3. Within one content file: the writing order of the type-field arrays;
  4. Embedded BEs: they follow the position of the host blocks entry.

Rationale: JsonTreeBuilder builds the candidate sequence in the order above (:105-110,655), and DuplicateIdResolver.resolve takes the last one purely by the index passed in (:73-100). DuplicateIdResolverTest.lastMeansLastInSequenceNotLexicographicallyLastSource() pins the case where a source that comes earlier lexicographically but later in load order still wins.

docs.title: 3.3 Result
docs.text:
• The winner reaches apply; the loser is discarded whole, and its embedded BE is isolated along with it (JsonTreeBuilder.java:678).
  • Each conflict records a WARN log line plus one loading-error bucket entry (:667-670). Note that the log level is WARN, but it lands in the error bucket.
  • When there are conflicts, one summary WARN is recorded as well (:672-674).
  • The diagnostic message contains the type field, the id, and the source paths of the winner and the loser (DuplicateIdResolver.describe, :109-115).

docs.title: 4.1 The two content types and how they are discovered
docs.text:
ReloadOrchestrator is the only orchestrator in the reload domain (ReloadOrchestrator.java:121), and it knows no type name itself: the typeName() of every registered ReloadHandler is a legal top-level key, and the orchestrator walks ReloadHandlerRegistry to obtain the key set. The two handlers currently registered on the modelling side are state_machines and animation_clips (FsmReloadHandler / FsmClipsReloadHandler, see section 4.6).

Content Top-level key Discovery State machine definitions state_machines directory glob data/<ns>/state_machines/*.json + listed in on_reload Animation clips animation_clips only listed in on_reload
  • state_machines/ has a directory glob: FsmReloadHandler.globDirectories() (FsmReloadHandler.java:69-71) declares StateMachineDefinitionLoader.PATH (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.java:39), enumerated by ReloadOrchestrator.collectGlob (:348-367) with ResourceManager.listResources. A state machine file is read even when no index lists it.
  • animation_clips/ has no directory glob. A clip file that no index lists is never read (AnimationClipLoader.java:28-29; FsmClipsReloadHandler.globDirectories keeps the default empty set).
  • state_machines/ files listed by an index are skipped by the glob entry point, to avoid reading them twice (ReloadOrchestrator.collectGlob, :348-367).
  • Application order: glob-discovered first, index-listed second; on the same id the latter wins (class docs :77-91; register, :507-526).

docs.title: 4.2 state_machines wrapper
docs.text:
Each file is a wrapper object carrying the state_machines top-level key, whose value must be an array of definitions (extra top-level keys no longer reject the file, see section 4.4):

{
  "state_machines": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:panel",
      "layers": [
        {
          "id": "base",
          "initial_state": "idle",
          "states": [
            { "id": "idle", "duration_ticks": 20 }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  • One file can hold several definitions, and the array order is the in-file last-wins order (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.java:14-33).
  • The element schema is decided by StateMachineDefinition.CODEC; this page specifies only the wrapper, and element fields are in ../../reference/fsm.md and the corresponding codec.

docs.title: 4.3 animation_clips wrapper
docs.text:
Likewise a wrapper object carrying the animation_clips top-level key:

{
  "animation_clips": [
    {
      "id": "mymod:wheel_spin",
      "duration_seconds": 2.5,
      "bones": [
        {
          "bone": "wheel_r",
          "keyframes": [
            { "time": 0.0, "transform": { "rotate": [0, 0, 0] } }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
  • The element carries its own id (the very id states[].clip references), and the loader does not extract an id additionally (AnimationClipLoader.java:21-27).
  • Keys in the element that the codec does not name are ignored, and can serve as comments or editor metadata (:26-27).
  • The file takes effect only in on_reload and registers into the reload bucket; a SCRIPT clip of the same name is not overridden by the file (AnimationClipLoader.register, :113-121).

docs.title: 4.4 File-level strictness, element-level tolerance
docs.text:
The two decoders isolate failures identically (StateMachineDefinitionLoader.decodeFile :67-100; AnimationClipLoader.decodeFile :69-102):

  • File level: a non-object body, a missing top-level key, or a non-array value → the whole file is rejected, with one error + bucket entry. {"state_machines": {}} is rejected as a whole (StateMachineDefinitionLoaderTest.nonArrayValueRejectsWholeFile).
  • File level (genuinely unknown key): a top-level key claimed by no reload type → one unsupported top-level field 'extra' + bucket entry, but known keys still contribute as usual (partial apply, no longer a whole-file rejection). In {"state_machines": [...], "extra": 1}, state_machines registers as usual (StateMachineDefinitionLoaderTest.extraTopLevelKeyDoesNotAffectThisType(); AnimationClipLoaderTest.ignoresAnExtraTopLevelKey()).
  • Multiple top-level keys are legal: one file can carry both state_machines and animation_clips, and the two decoders each read their own key and each contribute their own entries (AnimationClipReloadTest.mixedTopLevelKeysAreConsumedByBothHandlers).
  • Element level: an array element that is not an object, or that cannot be decoded for a missing field → only that element is skipped, its siblings proceed as usual, and each one is reported. See StateMachineDefinitionLoaderTest.badElementIsSkippedWhileSiblingsDecode() and AnimationClipLoaderTest.skipsAMalformedElementAndKeepsItsSiblings() / skipsAnElementWithoutAnId().
  • An empty array is legal (AnimationClipLoaderTest.emptyClipArrayIsValid()).

docs.title: 4.5 Reload domain routing and the reverse D9 hint
docs.text:
• The domain is decided by the index array, and the content type by the top-level key.
  • An unknown top-level key in a reload file → error + bucket entry, with a reverse hint attached: if these fields are registration content (such as blocks/items/registry_groups), list the file under on_register instead (ReloadOrchestrator.java:439-446).
  • One file can carry both content types at once: the two handlers each claim their own top-level key and each contribute their own entries (ReloadOrchestrator.dispatch, :429-470). Unknown top-level keys are determined by ContentStructure.unknownKeys, and there is no longer a "single top-level key" check.
  • The reload wrap-up re-checks the clips referenced by state machines; a dangling reference only records a WARN + bucket entry, and does not affect registration (FsmReloadHandler.afterReload, :95-116).

docs.title: 4.6 Extending to a new reload type
docs.text: Reload types are not hardcoded: extend or implement ReloadHandler<T> and register it by calling ReloadHandlerRegistry.register(handler) from a @Context bean's @PostConstruct, with no need to change the orchestrator. typeName() is the top-level key this type claims, and doubles as the deduplication collision space. For detailed steps and a minimal example see guide-extension.md §6, and for interface signatures see api-reload.md §13.

docs.title: 5.1 Errors (error log + bucket entry)
docs.text:
Format errors in the registration and reload phases are basically all in this list:

Case Source Unknown index field / field not an array / element not a string JsonTreeBuilder.java:226-274 A single file declares neither domain; every file declares neither :240-244 (error) / :323-326 (WARN + bucket) The same path listed in both arrays :308-316 Failure reading an index file or directory :188, :767-771 Unknown top-level field in a content file, field not an array, element not an object :475-516 Illegal content file path / missing file / parse exception :396-436 handler apply throws :712 Duplicate id conflict :667-670 (WARN log + bucket entry) Reload side: manifest read failure, illegal path, missing file, wrapper shape violation, unknown top-level key ReloadOrchestrator.java:307,369,405-470 Duplicate id on the reload side :545-556 (WARN log + bucket entry) Dangling clip reference at reload wrap-up FsmReloadHandler.java:111-116 (WARN log + bucket entry)

docs.title: 5.2 Warnings (warn, no bucket entry)
docs.text:
The following cases only log and do not write a bucket entry, because the entry is downgraded rather than malformed:

  • Unknown factory type → the entry is skipped (RegTypeHandler.java:70-74).
  • Unknown properties / item_properties key → that key is ignored (JsonPropertyParser.java:50-52; JsonItemParser.java:63).
  • Unknown map_color / sound_type (JsonPropertyParser.java:80-82,90-92).
  • BE host block not found / unknown BE factory (BlockEntityTypeHandler.java:77,83).
  • A cycle in group references (JsonTreeBuilder.java:823-825).

docs.title: 5.3 Reading diagnostics
docs.text:
All errors are bucketed by mod id. The reading API:

  • JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors(modId) / getLoadingErrorsByMod() / getLoadingErrors() (JsonTreeBuilder.java:743-775).
  • The unified facade Diagnostics: Diagnostics.errors(modId), Diagnostics.errors(Domain, key), Diagnostics.summarize() (Diagnostics.java:64-166). The mod dimension delegates verbatim to JsonTreeBuilder's bucket (registration phase); the domain × source dimension already has writers: the reload phase uses Domain.RELOAD_DATA with the key = namespace (Diagnostics.java:21-31,96-105).
  • The contract the tests assert: assertEquals(List.of(), JsonTreeBuilder.getLoadingErrors(modId)).

docs.title: 5.4 D9 hint text (content listed under the wrong domain)
docs.text:
Conditional hints in both directions; the error message strings are a public contract:

  • Registration side: on_register lists a reload-domain file (with state_machines or the like at the top level) → it goes down the unknown-field path, and the message ends with "list this file under 'on_reload' instead". The key names in the example are enumerated from ReloadHandlerRegistry at runtime rather than written literally; when the registry is empty (pure JVM unit tests) the example is omitted. The constraint still holds that data-driven does not depend on modelling: both registries are owned by data-driven, and handlers are registered by the modelling side, see JsonTreeBuilder.java:559-570 and section 4.6; test JsonTreeBuilderReloadHintTest.reloadDomainContentUnderOnRegisterIsReportedWithOnReloadHint().
  • Reload side: on_reload lists a registration-domain file → the message ends with "list the file under 'on_register' instead", see ReloadOrchestrator.java:441-446.

Partial-apply guarantee: listing content under the wrong domain still leaves the other domain in the same file processed as usual (JsonTreeBuilderReloadHintTest.halfApplyStillDispatchesSiblingRegistrationFields()).

docs.title: 7. Boundaries with other documents
docs.text:
• This page (schema.md): the authoritative reference for the JSON format, covering fields, types, requiredness, path rules, and error classification.
  • intro.md: an introductory explanation that answers "what is this, and why use it".
  • guide-content.md: a task-oriented guide that answers "how do I build my first content file"; its property key semantics and troubleshooting checklist take this page's format as authoritative.
  • guide-extension.md: Java-side extensions (custom TypeHandler / factories / property compilers).
  • api-registration.md / api-extension.md / api-diagnostics.md / api-reload.md: Java API references; where their index chapters still say sources, this page is authoritative.
  • ../../reference/fsm.md: the codec fields inside state machine definition and animation clip elements.

docs.title: Appendix A: Not covered / to be confirmed
docs.text:
• The complete field table and defaults of state_machines / animation_clips elements: this page specifies only the wrapper. For the element schema, treat the corresponding codec (StateMachineDefinition.CODEC / AnimationClip.CODEC) as the final authority; this page does not check it field by field.
  • The runtime behavior when tab points at a creative tab that does not exist: the code only parses the string into a ResourceLocation (BlockTypeHandler.resolveCreativeTab) and does not validate at the format level whether that tab exists.
  • Data pack indexes (data packs carrying on_register data) are not done this round; the registration phase reads the mod jar only, and a data pack's on_register section is not consumed. Whether a "snapshot comparison WARN" is needed is not implemented yet.

docs.title: Formula Module
docs.text:
modules/formula is KasugaLib's general-purpose expression engine: arithmetic (compute) plus boolean logic (logic), with namespace-scoped variable and function registration. It is a pure JVM library with zero Minecraft dependencies — it does not touch the game, so it can be consumed by modelling, core, scripting, or any other module.

The engine was migrated from the 1.0 Forge external artifact Mixed-Arithmetic-Logic-Interpreter and is the expression layer behind Blockbench data_points (e.g. "time * 360", "math.sin(time * 180) * 30", query.anim_time * 45) and future FSM conditions.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Java 21 (the module's Gradle toolchain is pinned to Java 21).
  • No Minecraft/NeoForge runtime is required. Unit tests run on plain JUnit 5.
  • The module is registered through settings.gradle (include ':modules:formula'). Consumers add implementation project(":modules:formula").

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import lib.kasuga.formula.Code;
import lib.kasuga.formula.compute.data.Namespace;
import lib.kasuga.formula.compute.infrastructure.Formula;

// A fresh namespace inherits every built-in function and constant from the root.
Namespace ns = new Namespace(Code.ROOT_NAMESPACE);

Formula f = Code.decodeFormula("sin(rad(time * 180)) * 30", ns);
ns.assign("time", 0.5f);          // variables are auto-registered on first use (initial 0)
float result = f.getResult();     // sin(90°) * 30

Logical expressions decode the same way:

var cond = Code.decodeLogical("a > 3 and b <= 10", ns);
ns.assign("a", 5f);
ns.assign("b", 9f);
boolean ok = cond.getResult();    // true

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Operator Meaning Precedence ^ power (Math.pow) highest * / % multiply, divide, modulo — same level, left-associative middle + - add, subtract — same level, left-associative lowest

Modulo shares the precedence of * and /: 10 % 3 * 5 evaluates as (10 % 3) * 5 = 5, not 10 % 15.

** is accepted as an alias for ^ (Python style): 2 ** 3 == 8.

Unary minus is supported in all forms: -5, -(2 + 3), 2 * -3, 3 - -2. Parentheses nest arbitrarily deep.

docs.title: Built-in Functions
docs.text:
Registered on the root namespace by Code:

Arity Functions 1 cos sin tan asin acos atan log lg exp round sqrt rad deg floor ceil 2 pow max min 3 none by default — register with namespace.register3Param(...)

Trigonometric functions take radians. rad/deg convert between degrees and radians. Arguments are separated by commas: pow(2, 10), max(3, 7).

docs.title: Static Constants
docs.text: pi and e are registered as read-only static variables (they live in STATIC_VARS, so assign on them is a no-op).

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
• Names start with a lowercase letter: [a-z][a-z1-9]*, optionally containing _.
  • Dotted names separate variable scopes: query.anim_time is a single variable whose codec contains a ..
  • A variable used in an expression is auto-registered on the instance map with initial value 0; every getResult() reads the latest value written by namespace.assign("x", v).

docs.title: Comparison Operators
docs.text: >, <, >=, <=, ==, !=, and <> (alias for !=). Symbol operators do not require surrounding spaces: a>b, a>=5, and a+1==6 all parse correctly.

docs.title: Boolean Operators
docs.text: and, or, not (word operators). Because they are words, they require surrounding spaces so they cannot collide with variable names: nota is a variable, while not a is a negation. Literal booleans are spelled True / False (capitalized). Numeric values are truthy when non-zero.

docs.title: Precedence
docs.text: Highest to lowest: ==, !=, > <, >= <=, not, and, or. Use parentheses to override: not (a > 3).

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Chained comparisons are not supported: a > b > c throws FormulaSyntaxError (the intermediate result is a boolean, not a numeric). Write a > b and b > c instead.
  • Mixed relational operators in one expression (e.g. a == b > c) are not supported for the same reason.

docs.title: Namespaces And Registration
docs.text:
Namespace is the symbol table. A child namespace copies the parent's functions, static variables, and instance variables at construction; later registrations stay local.

API Behavior register(codec, function) register a function instance register1Param/2Param/3Param(codec, computer) register a function from a lambda register(codec, value) register a static (read-only) variable registerInstance(codec, assignable) register a runtime variable (auto-created when an expression uses an unknown name) assign(codec, value) write a runtime variable containsInstance(codec) / getInstance(codec) inspect the instance map clone() shallow copy — the maps are copied, the parent link is preserved

Code is the static facade over the root namespace: Code.decodeFormula, Code.encodeFormula, Code.decodeLogical, Code.encodeLogical, Code.root().

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All exceptions extend RuntimeException:

Exception Meaning FormulaSyntaxError malformed expression (unbalanced brackets, bad operator sequence, non-numeric operand in a comparison, ...). Carries an optional message and a (formula, position) hint. FormulaParseError a token could not be parsed into any formula element; wraps the underlying FormulaSyntaxError plus the offending input string. FormulaOperationError an operator received an operator as an operand (e.g. two operators in a row).

docs.title: Development And Debugging
docs.text:
Run from the repository root:

.\gradlew.bat :modules:formula:test
.\gradlew.bat :modules:formula:compileJava

To run one test class:

.\gradlew.bat :modules:formula:test --tests lib.kasuga.formula.FormulaComputeTest

The unit tests cover operator precedence (including % sharing * / precedence), ** power, unary minus, function nesting, variable assignment/reassignment, dotted names, no-space symbol operators, word-operator spacing, and the chained-comparison error.

docs.title: Modelling Module
docs.text:
modules/modelling provides KasugaLib's client-side model loading, model-instance lifecycle, Minecraft renderer backend, texture atlas integration, and related animation/physics features.

This document describes the standard integration path for a mod that ships models with its resource pack, plus the validation and debugging methods to use while developing the module itself. The implementation is client-only: do not access its rendering APIs from a dedicated server.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Java 21. The module's Gradle toolchain is pinned to Java 21.
  • A client resource reload must complete before a scanned model can be instantiated. In a development client, restart the game or press F3 + T after changing model assets or model_proxy.json.
  • The module is initialized by lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.Constants; it registers the built-in pipelines and the resource reload listener.

docs.title: 1. Add the model asset
docs.text:
Place the model in your own mod's resource directory. For example:

src/main/resources/assets/examplemod/models/vehicles/engine.bbmodel

Its model key is therefore:

examplemod:models/vehicles/engine.bbmodel

The path must include the models/ prefix and the file extension. Do not use the vanilla model identifier convention (examplemod:vehicles/engine) for this API.

docs.title: 2. Opt in through model_proxy.json
docs.text:
The scanner only loads resources matched by:

src/main/resources/assets/<namespace>/models/model_proxy.json

The JSON object maps a namespace to an array of resource-path patterns. A minimal configuration for the file above is:

{
  "examplemod": [
    "models/vehicles/**/*.bbmodel"
  ]
}

Patterns are relative to the resource namespace:

Pattern Meaning * Any characters except / ** Any characters across directories ? One character !pattern Exclude resources matching pattern

For example, "models/**/*.obj" includes OBJ files anywhere below models, while "!models/legacy/**" excludes the legacy subtree. The loader combines the namespaces declared by the proxy configurations it reads into one scanner configuration.

docs.title: 3. Use a supported extension
docs.text:
The built-in router chooses a pipeline by file extension:

Extension Pipeline Source form .geo.json Bedrock JSON .json Java Edition JSON .obj Wavefront OBJ Text .mmd.zip PMX/MMD archive ZIP .glb, .gltf glTF Binary .bbmodel Blockbench native model Text

.geo.json is routed before generic .json. For an unsupported format, register a pipeline and a route through PipelineRegistry during client initialization.

docs.title: Creating And Rendering An Instance
docs.text:
After the resource reload has published the model, resolve its pipeline, create an instance, then add that instance to the Minecraft bridge/backend. The built-in names are mc_bridge and mc_backend.

import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.registry.PipelineRegistry;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.dynamic.ModelInstance;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.dynamic.ModelPipeLine;
import lib.kasuga.rendering.models.uml.math.Transform;
import net.minecraft.resources.ResourceLocation;

ResourceLocation modelKey = ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(
        "examplemod", "models/vehicles/engine.bbmodel"
);
ResourceLocation instanceKey = ResourceLocation.fromNamespaceAndPath(
        "examplemod", "engine_at_spawn"
);

ModelPipeLine<?, ?, ResourceLocation, ResourceLocation, ?> pipeline =
        PipelineRegistry.resolve(modelKey);
if (pipeline == null || !pipeline.hasModel(modelKey)) {
    // The proxy rule did not match, or resource reload has not completed yet.
    return;
}

if (!pipeline.hasInstance(modelKey, instanceKey)) {
    Transform transform = new Transform().translate(x, y, z);
    ModelInstance instance = pipeline.createInstance(modelKey, instanceKey, transform, null, null);
    if (instance != null) {
        pipeline.addToRenderer(modelKey, instanceKey, "mc_bridge", "mc_backend");
    }
}

Call this only on the client-side game/render flow. createInstance returns null when the model key is not published. Reuse a stable instanceKey; creating another instance with the same key replaces the pipeline's lookup entry without automatically removing the old renderable.

When an instance is no longer needed, remove it through the pipeline rather than retaining and closing it yourself:

pipeline.removeInstance(modelKey, instanceKey);

This removes it from every registered backend and closes its runtime animation/physics state.

docs.title: Blockbench (.bbmodel)
docs.text:
The bbmodel pipeline supports native Blockbench JSON with cube and mesh elements, nested outliner groups, element/group visibility, rotations, per-face texture selection, face UV rotation, external textures, and embedded data:image/... textures.

Use face.texture as the texture-array index written by Blockbench. For external texture sources, resource locations may be written with or without textures/ and .png; the loader normalizes them to atlas identifiers. For example, both examplemod:textures/vehicles/engine.png and examplemod:vehicles/engine resolve to the sprite examplemod:vehicles/engine.

Blockbench records UV coordinates in texture pixels. KsgBbModelLoader converts them to normalized UVs using the texture's UV canvas: uv_width/uv_height when the file declares them, otherwise the declared texture size, otherwise the project resolution. The canvas is deliberately independent of the decoded image, because Blockbench stretches an image over its canvas — qj_bogey_main.bbmodel keeps 64×64 pngs on a 128×128 canvas whose face UVs reach 128, so dividing by the image size would sample the wrong region. This conversion is intentionally local to the bbmodel loader. Do not add pixel-UV normalization in FlatModelData or another shared backend path, because those paths are also used by OBJ, PMX, glTF, Bedrock, and Java Edition models.

Cube faces follow Blockbench's CubeFace.UVToLocal convention: the uv rectangle is mapped so that u points to the viewer's right and v downward as seen from outside the cube (top face u=+X, v=+Z; bottom face u=+X, v=-Z), and rotation turns the texture clockwise. Each face is emitted top-left → bottom-left → bottom-right → top-right, which is also the winding the backend needs for outward normals.

Element, group and animation rotations are used exactly as stored (no sign flips) and composed intrinsic Z → Y → X, i.e. the matrix Rz·Ry·Rx that three.js Euler.order = "ZYX", Minecraft's ModelPart (ZP/YP/XP order) and RotHelper.rotation all use. Each element rotates around its own origin, inside its parent group's already-rotated frame, so nesting is relative. Only rotations that span more than one axis can tell the orders apart, which is why a wrong order shows up as "some parts are rotated wrong". Blockbench's Bedrock export writes negated X/Y angles (test_fan_be.bbmodel [0,45,0] ↔ test_fan_be.geo.json [0,-45,0]), so the sign flips in RotHelper belong to the Bedrock loaders — do not copy them here.

The repository has runnable content-testing examples in:

modules/modelling/src/contentTesting/resources/assets/kasuga_lib/models/block/test/blockbench/

docs.title: Development And Debugging
docs.text: Run commands from the repository root. On Windows use gradlew.bat; on macOS/Linux use ./gradlew.

docs.title: Compile And Unit Tests
docs.text:
.\gradlew.bat :modules:modelling:compileJava
.\gradlew.bat :modules:modelling:test
.\gradlew.bat :modules:modelling:modelUnitTest

To run only the Blockbench loader tests:

.\gradlew.bat :modules:modelling:test --tests lib.kasuga.rendering.models.mc.typo.bbmodel.BbModelDefinitionTest

modelUnitTest is the module's pure-Java test task. The regular test task uses the configured NeoForge test runtime.

docs.title: Start The Client With A Selected Smoke Model
docs.text:
The contentTesting development client displays model smoke tests by default; production code does not create these instances. The default selection is bbmodel; pass a filename or a complete resource path to show exactly one Blockbench model in front of the player:

.\gradlew.bat :modules:modelling:runClient `
  '-PkasugaTestModel=bbmodel' `
  '-PkasugaTestBbmodel=qj_bogey_main.bbmodel'

The short kasugaTestBbmodel value is resolved under:

models/block/test/blockbench/

Alternatively pass models/vehicles/engine.bbmodel. The selected resource must be included by the active model_proxy.json before the client starts; embedded textures are registered while the resource reload builds the atlas, so loading a new bbmodel after the atlas has been published is not supported.

Other built-in smoke selections are obj, be, and je; any other value takes the MMD test path:

.\gradlew.bat :modules:modelling:runClient '-PkasugaTestModel=obj'

Set -Dkasuga.renderTestModels=false on the JVM to suppress all hardcoded smoke models when investigating unrelated rendering behavior.

docs.title: Logs And Failure Triage
docs.text:
The client run directory is:

modules/modelling/run/client/

Inspect logs/latest.log after a resource reload or client run.

Symptom Checks Model is absent Confirm the exact ResourceLocation, make sure model_proxy.json matches it, then restart/reload resources. Look for the warning Test bbmodel ... is unavailable after resource reload. Wrong model appears Ensure the kasugaTestModel and kasugaTestBbmodel Gradle properties are both set. A short bbmodel name always resolves under the test Blockbench directory. Green/missing texture Verify external texture namespace/path, check that the texture exists below assets/<namespace>/textures, and search the log for atlas/sprite errors. Texture appears tiled or granular Check the texture's UV canvas, not just the image: the loader normalizes pixel UVs by uv_width/uv_height (falling back to the declared size and the project resolution), so a texture whose image is smaller than its canvas must still have all face UVs inside the canvas. Do not compensate by changing shared backend UV logic. Faces are mirrored, rotated, or lit from the wrong side Face uv rectangles are mapped Blockbench-style (u = viewer's right, v = down, viewed from outside; rotation is clockwise) and emitted in outward-wound corner order. Compare against KsgBbModelLoaderFaceUvTest, and do not reorder a single face's corners without moving its UVs with them. Single-axis rotations look right but some rotated parts are wrong Those parts carry a rotation on two or three axes, so the euler order is what differs: it must be intrinsic Z → Y → X (Rz·Ry·Rx, KsgBbModelLoaderRotationTest). The angles themselves are used unflipped; negating X/Y is the Bedrock loaders' job (RotHelper), because Blockbench's Bedrock export already writes negated X/Y. Model exists but is not visible Check pipeline.hasModel, pipeline.hasInstance, then pipeline.isRendering(modelKey, instanceKey, "mc_backend"). Confirm the transform is in front of the camera and use removeInstance before recreating a changed instance. Loader error Search latest.log for Invalid Blockbench model, Unable to decode embedded texture, and the model's resource path.
